recipes.name: Almond Zucchini Bread
recipes.description: The secret to zucchini bread that isn't gummy is The Squeeze. Zucchini is mostly water; you must grate it and then squeeze it in a kitchen towel until it is absolutely dry before measuring.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a loaf pan with parchment paper.
The Squeeze: Grate the zucchini. Place in a towel and squeeze vigorously until no more water comes out. Measure 1 cup of the dry shreds.
Dry: In a large bowl, whisk the almond flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon.
Wet: In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, maple syrup, mashed banana, and coconut oil.
Mix: Fold the wet ingredients into the dry. Stir in the zucchini shreds.
Bake: Pour into the pan. Bake for 35-40 minutes until the top is dark golden brown and a tester comes out clean.
Rest: Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes before lifting out via the parchment paper.

recipes.name: Aloo Gobi (Potato Cauliflower Curry)
recipes.description: Tender potatoes and cauliflower with toasted cumin, coriander and a thick tomato-spice coating. Give the potatoes a head start, then uncover briefly to remove excess moisture.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) yellow-fleshed potatoes, weighed after trimming; peel if desired and cut into 3/4-inch / 2 cm cubes
680 g cauliflower florets, weighed after removing leaves and the tough core; cut into 1-inch / 2.5 cm pieces
100 g onion, peeled and finely diced
2 green serrano chiles, slit lengthwise; see the milder option
150 g ripe tomato, finely chopped, with its juices
1 tsp fine salt, for the vegetables
1/2 tsp fine salt, reserved for the final seasoning; use only as needed
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, divided between the two vegetable stages
1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, reserved only if the pan dries before the vegetables soften
1/4 tsp cayenne, optional for extra heat

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare everything: Wash, trim, weigh and cut the vegetables as listed. One large or two smaller cauliflower heads may be needed; weigh the florets after trimming. Drain the cauliflower well. Lightly crush the coriander seeds so there are no large, hard whole seeds. Measure the spices and divide the cooking water into two equal portions; keep the separate hot-water reserve aside. Finish all cutting and measuring before heating the oil.

Start the whole spices: Heat all the measured oil in the deep pan over medium heat. Add cumin and crushed coriander seeds and stir for about 20–30 seconds, until they sizzle and smell fragrant. Lower the heat if they darken quickly; do not let them burn.

Soften the onion and aromatics: Add the onion and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until soft and beginning to turn pale gold. Add garlic, ginger and the slit serranos and stir for 30–60 seconds, until fragrant. For the milder powdered-chile option, leave the serranos out and add its cayenne in the next step.

Build the tomato coating: Lower the heat to medium-low. Stir in turmeric, ground coriander and the cayenne if using the milder powdered-chile option for about 20 seconds, then promptly add the tomato and its juice. Cook for about 5–7 minutes, stirring, until the tomato softens and the mixture looks thick rather than watery. Do not insist on dry-frying ground spices when they are beginning to catch.

Give the potatoes a head start: Add the potatoes and the initial fine salt, turn to coat for 1–2 minutes, then pour in the first half of the cooking water. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer, cover tightly and cook over medium-low for about 12–18 minutes, gently turning once or twice. Test a cube: it should be partly cooked, with a tender exterior and some resistance at the center. If still hard all the way through, continue covered, adding 1 tbsp corrective hot water if the pan is dry, before adding cauliflower.

Add cauliflower and finish cooking: Fold in the cauliflower and the remaining half of the cooking water. Let the pan return to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook about 15–20 minutes, gently turning every five minutes. A knife should enter both a potato center and a cauliflower stem easily. If the pan dries before that point, use the corrective water a tablespoon at a time, within its separate listed allowance. Continue beyond the estimate when needed; avoid vigorous stirring that breaks up the florets.

Dry the coating and finish: Uncover and cook over medium heat for about 3–5 minutes, folding gently, until no loose liquid collects underneath. Stir in garam masala and the optional finishing cayenne and cook for 30 seconds. Turn off the heat, add the lemon juice gradually and fold in cilantro. Taste and use the reserved fine salt only as needed. Remove the slit chiles before serving if you do not want a diner to bite into one.

Serve: Divide into four main portions with bread, or six generous vegetable sides alongside dal. If serving with rice, remember that the potatoes already provide a substantial starch component; offer rice in smaller portions.

recipes.name: Anadama Bread
recipes.description: Anadama is a quintessential New England bread, supposedly named after a fisherman's wife named Anna. The bread is defined by the bittersweet depth of molasses and the rustic texture of cornmeal.

recipeInstructions.text: The Porridge: In a small saucepan, whisk the first listed water portion and cornmeal. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly for 5 minutes until thickened. Remove from heat.
Melt: Stir in the butter and molasses. Let cool until lukewarm (critical - if too hot, it will kill the yeast).
The Yeast: In a large bowl, dissolve the yeast in the warm water. Let sit for 10 minutes until foamy.
The Dough: Stir the cornmeal mixture into the yeast. Add two thirds of the measured flour and the salt. Gradually add the remaining flour until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Turn out onto a floured surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be slightly tacky but not sticky.
Rise 1: Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm spot until doubled (about 1 hour).
Shape: Deflate the dough. Shape into a loaf and place in a greased 9x5 pan.
Rise 2: Cover and let rise again until doubled (about 45 minutes).
Bake: Bake at 375°F for 30 minutes until the top is dark golden brown and the bottom sounds hollow when tapped.

recipes.name: Anelletti Al Forno
recipes.description: Anelletti al Forno is a traditional Sicilian pasta bake, often served on special occasions and holidays, particularly New Year's Day. The name comes from 'anelletti,' meaning 'little rings,' the small ring-shaped pasta traditional to Sicily.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 lb Ground Beef + 1/2 lb Ground Pork
1 Carrot, 1 Celery stalk, 1 small Onion (finely minced)
1 (28 oz) can Whole Peeled Tomatoes, crushed

recipeInstructions.text: The Ragu: Sauté the carrot, celery, and onion in oil cook until golden brown and softened (15 mins). Brown the beef and pork. Deglaze with red wine. Stir in tomato paste, tomatoes, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Simmer on LOW for 2 hours until thick and dark. Stir in peas at the end.
The Eggplant: Salt eggplant cubes for 30 mins, rinse, and pat dry. Fry in 1 inch of oil until deep golden. Drain on paper towels.
The Pasta: Boil anelletti in salted water until very al dente (2 minutes less than package). Drain.
Toss: In a massive bowl, toss the pasta with 4 cups of the ragu and the fried eggplant.
Layer: In a greased 9x13 dish, layer half the pasta. Top with chopped eggs, ham, and half the cheeses. Cover with remaining pasta.
The Crown: Top with remaining cheese and breadcrumbs.
Bake: Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes until bubbling.
Rest (Critical): Let sit for 15 minutes before slicing. This allows the pasta "cake" to set so it doesn't collapse.

recipes.name: Apple Banana and Carrot Muffins
recipes.description: The common flaw in "Healthy" muffins is a gummy, dense texture. We solve this by Grating, not Simmering.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
The Veg: Grate the apple and carrot using the fine holes of a box grater. Squeeze out any excess juice (drink it!).
Wet: In a large bowl, whisk the mashed banana, eggs, melted butter, vanilla, grated apple, and grated carrot.
Dry: In a separate bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt.
Fold: Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet until just combined. Do not over-mix, or the muffins will be tough.
Bake: Portion into the tin. Bake for 20-25 minutes (standard) or 15 minutes (mini) until a tester comes out clean.
Rest: Cool on a wire rack.

recipes.name: Apple Chai Oatmeal Cups
recipes.description: Chai-spiced oatmeal is a meal-prep staple that tastes warm and comforting straight from the fridge, no reheating needed. Cardamom, ginger, and allspice bloom in melted coconut oil before mixing into the batter, distributing the spice evenly instead of leaving it in scattered bits.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 cups Almond Milk or Whole Milk

recipeInstructions.text: Bloom: In a small bowl, whisk the melted coconut oil with all the chai spices. Let sit for 2 minutes.
Dry: In a large bowl, combine the oats and baking powder.
Wet: In another bowl, whisk the mashed banana, eggs, milk, and maple syrup. Stir in the spiced coconut oil.
Combine: Pour the wet mixture over the oats. Fold in the minced apples.
Bake: Scoop into a lined 12-count muffin tin. Bake at 350°F for 20 minutes until the tops are firm and golden.
Cool: Let cool for 10 minutes in the tin to allow the oats to set.

recipes.name: Apple Cider Cream Pie
recipes.description: This pie concentrates two cups of unfiltered apple cider down to 1/2 cup syrup, intensifying its flavor tenfold. The apple cider vinegar in the crust inhibits gluten development, creating a tender, flaky pastry that contrasts beautifully with the rich custard filling.
recipeIngredient: 1 stick Unsalted butter, chilled and diced

recipeInstructions.text: The Crust: In a food processor, pulse flour, cornstarch, sugar, and salt. Add butter and pulse until it looks like coarse meal. Drizzle in milk and vinegar; pulse until dough just forms. Pat into a disk, wrap in plastic, and chill for 30 minutes.

Blind Bake: Roll dough to an 11-inch round and fit into a 9-inch pie plate. Crimp edges and chill until firm (15 mins). Preheat oven to 425°F. Line with parchment and weights; bake for 15 mins. Remove weights and parchment. Cover edges with foil and bake 15 mins more at 350°F until set but not browned.
The Reduction: While the crust cools, boil the apple cider in a saucepan until reduced to 1/2 cup (about 10-12 mins). Let it cool completely.
The Custard: Whisk the reduced cider with 3/4 cup sugar, sour cream, and salt. Whisk in the eggs until smooth.
Bake: Pour custard into the cooled shell. Bake at 350°F for 35-40 minutes until the edges are set but the center is still slightly jiggly. Cool completely (this is mandatory for the set).
Finish: Whip heavy cream with 1/4 cup sugar and cinnamon until firm peaks form. Mound over the cooled pie before serving.

recipes.name: Apple Pie
recipes.description: A restaurant-quality apple pie requires Physics. We use the Vodka Hack: replacing half the water with cold vodka prevents gluten from forming (alcohol doesn't trigger gluten), resulting in a crust that is impossibly flaky and easy to roll.
recipeIngredient: 14 tbsp Unsalted Butter, ice cold and cubed
2 tbsp Vodka (ice cold - The flakiness secret)
3 lbs Baking Apples (Granny Smith or Mutsu)

recipeInstructions.text: The Crust: Pulse flour, sugar, salt, and butter in a food processor until pea-sized bits remain. Add vodka and water. Pulse until just combined. Wrap in plastic and chill for at least 1 hour.
The Filling: Peel and slice apples. Toss with lemon juice and sugar.
The Reduction: In a large skillet, melt butter. Add apples and cook for 7 minutes until they release their juices. Drain apples in a colander, catching the juice.
Caramelize: Return the juice to the skillet. Boil for 5-8 minutes until it turns into a thick syrup. Toss the syrup and spices back with the apples. Let cool completely.
Roll: Roll out bottom crust. Fill with cooled apples. Roll out top crust and seal edges. Cut 4 steam vents.
Wash: Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake: Bake at 375°F for 50 minutes on the lowest rack (to ensure the bottom crust gets direct heat).
Cool: Let cool for at least 2 hours before slicing.

recipes.name: Arugula & Feta Salad with Strawberry Vinaigrette
recipes.description: Peppery arugula, sliced strawberries, feta and toasted sunflower seeds with a fresh strawberry, honey and rice-vinegar dressing.
recipeIngredient: 5 oz baby arugula, washed if needed and dried thoroughly
1 pint fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced, for the salad
4 large fresh strawberries, hulled, additional to the salad berries, for dressing
Salt and black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare produce: Wash and dry arugula if needed. Wash berries, dry them and remove their hulls. Slice the listed salad berries and keep the additional dressing berries separate. Crumble feta and measure toasted seeds.

Blend dressing: Blend the dressing berries, olive oil, vinegar, honey and garlic until smooth. Taste with an arugula leaf and a small piece of feta, then season with salt and pepper as needed. If the blender cannot catch the small amount, use a narrower vessel or small food processor rather than adding water just to raise the level.

Dress lightly: Put arugula in a wide bowl and toss gently with about half the dressing. Add sliced berries and most of the feta, lifting carefully to avoid crushing fruit. Add more dressing only if the leaves need it; reserve any excess instead of automatically pouring it all over the salad.
Finish and serve: Scatter over the remaining feta and sunflower seeds. Divide into the intended side portions and serve immediately while leaves and seeds retain their texture.

recipes.name: Hoisin-Glazed Meatballs
recipes.description: Tender ginger-scallion meatballs with a thin, glossy sweet-tangy glaze. Includes separate temperature endpoints for beef and turkey.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) ground beef (80–85% lean) or ground turkey (93% lean)
2 scallions, finely sliced, whites and greens separated
1/4 cup (60 ml) water, plus more as needed
1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, optional garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the binder: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Line a rimmed sheet pan. Soak panko in milk for 5 minutes, then stir in the egg, half the garlic, half the ginger, soy sauce, scallion whites, and pepper.

Shape gently: Add the meat and mix just until evenly combined. Divide into 24 portions, about 35 g each including the binder, and roll gently. Arrange with gaps on the sheet pan. Wash hands and clean surfaces after handling raw meat.

Bake and check: Bake about 15–20 minutes. Check several of the largest meatballs through the center: beef must reach 160°F / 71°C; turkey must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue baking if needed; color alone is not the endpoint.

Reduce the glaze: Meanwhile, combine hoisin, plum sauce, vinegar, water, remaining garlic, and remaining ginger in a wide skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 4–6 minutes, stirring, until it lightly coats a spoon. Add water if it becomes pasty.

Coat and serve: Add the fully cooked meatballs and sesame oil. Toss over low heat for 1–2 minutes to coat. Taste the sauce and add a little water if too concentrated. Finish with scallion greens and optional sesame seeds; serve with plain rice and vegetables.

recipes.name: Napa Slaw with Edamame and Crispy Wontons
recipes.description: Napa cabbage and carrots with edamame, toasted sesame dressing and optional crisp wonton strips. Add the strips at the table to keep them crisp.
recipeIngredient: 6 cups napa cabbage, cored and thinly shredded
1 cup cooked shelled edamame, cooled and well drained
6 wonton wrappers, cut into thin strips
Neutral oil, enough for 1/2-inch depth in the frying pan
1 pinch salt, for the wonton strips

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the edamame: Use ready-to-eat cooked shelled edamame, or cook packaged shelled edamame according to its instructions first. Cool promptly under cool running water, drain thoroughly and measure the cooked beans. Keep refrigerated if preparing ahead.
Cut the vegetables: Core and thinly shred the napa, then measure it. Julienne the carrots and slice green onions. Combine in a large bowl with the cooled edamame.

Fry the optional strips: Cut the wonton wrappers into thin strips. Heat neutral oil to a depth of 1/2 inch in a dry, deep-sided pan with ample space above the oil. Bring to 350°F / 175°C. Fry a small batch, stirring gently to separate, until pale golden; start checking within seconds. Lift out with a slotted spoon, drain in a single layer and sprinkle with the pinch of salt. Repeat, allowing the oil to recover between batches. Let strips cool before topping the slaw.
Mix the dressing: Whisk or shake toasted sesame oil, vinegar, soy sauce, honey or agave, ginger, garlic and optional chile flakes until combined.

Dress and serve: Toss the vegetables and edamame with the dressing and toasted sesame seeds, lifting from the bottom to coat evenly. Taste a forkful before adjusting seasoning. Divide into four generous side portions and add the wonton strips just before eating.

recipes.name: Cabbage Slaw with Peanuts and Sesame
recipes.description: Green and red cabbage, carrots and scallions with ginger-soy dressing, roasted peanuts and toasted sesame.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp soy sauce or gluten-free tamari
1/2 tsp sriracha or chile-garlic sauce, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the vegetables: Thinly shred and measure both cabbages. Cut carrots into thin matchsticks and slice scallions. Put them in a large bowl; prepare the cilantro and peanuts separately.
Mix the dressing: Whisk or shake the vinegar, soy sauce or tamari, both oils, honey or maple syrup, ginger, garlic and optional chile sauce until combined. Stir again just before pouring.
Dress: Pour over the cabbage, carrots and scallions. Lift and turn from the bottom until evenly coated. Taste a complete forkful before adjusting any seasoning.

Finish: Fold in cilantro, peanuts and toasted sesame seeds just before serving. Divide into six side portions. If holding briefly, cover and refrigerate the dressed vegetables, adding the toppings at service; lift portions out of any pooled liquid.

recipes.name: Authentic Roman Alfredo (Fettuccine al Burro)
recipes.description: Fettuccine in a glossy butter and Parmigiano sauce. Learn how water, movement, and gentle heat keep it smooth.
recipeIngredient: 3 oz (85 g) Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated from a block
2 quarts (2 liters) water, for cooking pasta
1 tsp fine salt, for the cooking water
1 cup (240 ml) reserved pasta water, added as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the pasta: Bring the water and salt to a boil. Add fettuccine and stir so it does not stick. Begin tasting 2 minutes before the package time; stop when it is flexible with a slightly firm center. Reserve 1 cup cooking water before transferring the pasta.
Start the sauce: While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in a wide skillet over low heat. Add 1/3 cup reserved hot pasta water and swirl until cloudy. Do not brown the butter.
Finish the pasta: Transfer pasta with tongs into the skillet. Toss over medium-low heat for about 1 minute, until the pasta reaches the texture you like. Add a splash of water if the pan looks dry.

Add cheese gently: Move the skillet off the burner. Wait until active bubbling stops, then add cheese in three small batches, tossing thoroughly after each. Add reserved water a tablespoon at a time until the sauce flows and coats every strand. If the cheese is not melting, use a few seconds of low heat while tossing, then remove again.

Taste and serve: Taste before adding salt; the cheese and cooking water already season the sauce. Add pepper if desired. Serve immediately in warm bowls, leaving the sauce slightly looser than you want on the plate.

recipes.name: Avgolemono
recipes.description: Avgolemono is a miracle of Tempering Science. It is incredibly creamy and rich, yet contains zero dairy.

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: In a large pot, bring the chicken broth to a boil. Add the rice (or orzo) and reduce heat to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes cook until fully cooked through fully cooked through fully cooked through fully cooked through fully cooked through.
Heat: Stir in the shredded chicken and keep the soup at a very low simmer (do not boil once the chicken is in).
The Emulsion: In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs vigorously for 2 minutes until foamy. Slowly whisk in the lemon juice.

Temper (Critical): While whisking the egg-lemon mixture constantly, slowly ladle in 2 cups of the hot broth, one ladle at a time. This "warms up" the eggs so they don't scramble when they hit the pot.
Combine: Pour the tempered egg mixture back into the large pot. Stir constantly over low heat for 2 minutes. The soup will instantly turn creamy and opaque.
Finish: Season with salt and a generous amount of white pepper. Serve immediately.

recipes.keywords: Greek, acidic, rich, comfort-food, weeknight, light-and-fresh, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Avocado Kale Caesar Salad
recipes.description: Shredded kale with a creamy avocado, lemon and miso dressing, diced avocado, Parmesan and toasted pepitas.
recipeIngredient: 5–6 cups lacinato kale leaves, tough stems removed, finely shredded
1 large ripe avocado, flesh divided equally between dressing and topping
1 tsp white miso paste or soy sauce
1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided and added to taste
2–3 tbsp water, plus more only as needed to thin the dressing
1 tsp olive oil, for softening kale
1 tbsp unsalted butter, for the optional breadcrumb topping

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare greens and optional crumbs: Wash, dry and shred kale. If making the topping, melt its butter in a small skillet over medium-low. Add panko and stir about 3–5 minutes until golden. Transfer to a plate to cool; do not leave crumbs in the hot skillet.

Soften kale: Put prepared kale in a wide bowl. Add the measured olive oil and a small pinch taken from the measured salt allowance. Rub and turn gently with clean hands for about 1–2 minutes until leaves become darker and more flexible. Stop before they turn wet or mushy.

Blend dressing: Blend half the avocado with the initial water allowance, optional mayonnaise, garlic, lemon juice, Dijon, miso or soy and black pepper. Add further water only as needed for a smooth spoonable dressing. Taste with a piece of kale and some Parmesan before adding more of the remaining salt.

Dress and rest: Toss kale with about half the dressing, adding more only as needed to coat without leaving a pool. Fold in half the Parmesan and let stand about 5 minutes while dicing the remaining avocado. Reserve unused dressing.
Finish: Gently fold in diced avocado. Scatter with pepitas, remaining Parmesan and optional cooled breadcrumbs. Divide into side portions and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Avocado Toast
recipes.description: Avocado toast is only as good as its two main ingredients: the bread and the avocado. The bread must be thick-cut and toasted until genuinely crunchy -- a soft, floppy base turns to mush under the weight of the avocado.
recipeIngredient: 2 slices Thick-Cut Sourdough or Rustic Bread
1 tbsp Fresh Lemon or Lime Juice
Optional Toppings: everything bagel seasoning, soft-boiled egg, cherry tomatoes, radish slices, microgreens, pickled red onions

recipeInstructions.text: Toast: Toast the bread until deeply golden and crunchy throughout -- not just colored on the surface. A proper toast should be rigid when held horizontally, not floppy.

Prep the Avocado: Halve the avocado, remove the pit, and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Add lemon juice and a generous pinch of flaky salt. Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some chunky pieces for texture. Do not make it smooth like guacamole.
Assemble: Divide the avocado between the two toasts, spreading it to the edges in a thick, even layer.
Season: Drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt and red pepper flakes.
Top (Optional): Add any combination of toppings: a halved soft-boiled egg, sliced radishes, cherry tomato halves, pickled red onions, microgreens, or everything bagel seasoning.
Serve: Eat immediately. Avocado toast does not wait -- it oxidizes and the bread softens within minutes.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, acidic, rich, weeknight, light-and-fresh, quick-lunch, toast

recipes.name: Baby’s First Smash Cake
recipes.description: This cake is designed for an 8-month-old to grab and taste, so it contains only familiar foods and no added sugar (bananas and applesauce do the sweetening). The whole wheat and oat flours provide nutrition and fiber, while the cream cheese frosting sweetened with apple juice concentrate is mild enough for a baby's palate.

recipeInstructions.text: Batter: Mash bananas until smooth. Whisk in applesauce, coconut oil, and vanilla. Fold in the flours, baking soda, and cinnamon.
Bake: Pour into mini tart pans or a muffin tin. Bake at 375°F for 15-20 minutes until a tester comes out clean. Cool completely.
Frosting: Whisk the softened cream cheese with the apple juice concentrate and vanilla until pale and fluffy.
Assemble: Stack the mini rounds with a layer of frosting between them. "Frost" the entire outside.
Smash: Serve to the birthday guest of honor.

recipes.name: Baked Chicken Parmesan
recipes.description: Thin chicken cutlets with toasted crumbs, melted mozzarella, and tomato sauce. Learn how to protect crisp edges while cooking the center properly.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 4–6 cutlets about 1/2 inch thick
1/4 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
6 oz (170 g) low-moisture mozzarella, thinly sliced
8 oz (225 g) dried spaghetti or rigatoni
1 1/2 tsp fine salt, for 3 quarts pasta water

recipeInstructions.text: Set up: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Put a rack over a rimmed sheet pan and grease with 1 tsp oil. Bring 3 quarts water and the pasta-water salt to a boil. Even the chicken to 1/2 inch thick and pat dry.

Toast the crumbs: Heat the remaining oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add panko and stir for 3–5 minutes until light golden. Spread in a shallow dish, cool briefly, then mix in Parmesan. Put beaten eggs in another shallow dish.

Bread: Season chicken with its measured salt and pepper. Dip each cutlet in egg, let excess drip off, then press into crumbs on both sides. Arrange on the rack without touching. Discard egg and crumbs that contacted raw chicken; clean hands and work surfaces.

Start baking and cook the pasta: Put the chicken tray in the oven and set a timer for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, add pasta to the boiling water. Stir and cook until just tender according to the package, then reserve 1/2 cup cooking water and drain. Warm marinara in a small pan or microwave-safe bowl.
Check the chicken: After 15 minutes in the oven, check the thickest pieces from the side with a thermometer. Continue baking until each reaches 165°F / 74°C, usually about 15–20 minutes total.

Melt the topping: Divide one third of the measured marinara over the centers of the cutlets, leaving edges exposed. Divide mozzarella over the sauced centers. Return to the oven for 3–5 minutes until melted; avoid prolonged baking once the cheese melts.

Serve: Toss pasta with the remaining marinara, adding reserved water a tablespoon at a time if needed. Divide pasta and chicken among four plates, finish with basil, and serve promptly with a green salad.

recipes.keywords: Italian, American, acidic, umami, herbaceous, comfort-food, weeknight, kid-friendly, entertaining, bake

recipes.name: Cod with Lemon Panko
recipes.description: Cod baked in lemon-garlic butter beneath a parsley-flecked panko crust. Keep the sauce around the fish so the topping stays crisp.
recipeIngredient: 4 skinless cod fillets of similar thickness, thawed if frozen and patted dry
4 tbsp unsalted butter, melted, divided equally between the sauce and crumbs
2 cloves garlic, minced, divided equally between the sauce and crumbs
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Pat the thawed fish dry, check for pin bones and arrange the portions in a shallow baking dish to check the fit. Zest the lemon, then juice it. Melt the butter.
Make the base: Mix half the butter, all the lemon juice and half the garlic, with salt and pepper to taste. Pour into the dish and set the fish on top in one layer. Season the tops lightly.
Add the crumbs: Mix panko with the remaining butter and garlic, lemon zest, paprika and parsley. Distribute over the fillets and press gently into an even layer without packing it into a thick mound.

Bake and check: Bake on the center rack, beginning to check at 10–12 minutes; many portions take 12–20 minutes, depending on thickness. Insert a thermometer from the side into the thickest center of each portion: aim for 145°F / 63°C. The flesh should separate into opaque flakes. Remove thinner pieces as they finish. If the topping darkens too soon, shield it loosely with foil; do not keep fully cooked fish baking solely to darken pale crumbs.
Serve: Lift each fillet carefully onto a plate and spoon the lemon butter around or beneath it. Serve promptly with a vegetable and, if wanted, a separately prepared potato or rice side.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, acidic, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, light-and-fresh, bake

recipes.name: Baked Creamy Macaroni and Pimento Cheese
recipes.description: This Southern staple combines pimento cheese with a classic French Mornay sauce (roux plus cheese). Shred cheddar fresh from the block - pre-shredded cheese contains cellulose that prevents smooth melting.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Sharp Cheddar Cheese, freshly shredded

recipeInstructions.text: Pasta: Preheat oven to 350°F. Cook macaroni according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
The Roux: In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute until fragrant but not browned.
The Sauce: Gradually whisk in milk, salt, cayenne, and garlic powder. Cook, whisking constantly, for 3-5 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Fold: Stir in the shredded Cheddar and drained pimentos until completely melted and glossy. Remove from heat and fold in the cooked pasta.
Bake: Pour the mixture into a greased 9x13 baking dish.
Topping: Mix panko and Parmesan in a small bowl. Sprinkle evenly over the top.
Finish: Bake for 15-20 minutes until the edges are bubbling and the topping is golden brown.

recipes.keywords: Southern, spicy, umami, rich, comfort-food, bake, roast

recipes.name: Bakery Style Chocolate Chip Muffins
recipes.description: To achieve the "Bakery High-Dome", we use two professional techniques: The Temperature Shock (starting at 425°F to trigger a rapid rise, then dropping to 375°F to finish the bake) and Resting the Batter (letting the batter sit for 10 mins before scooping allows the starch to hydrate, resulting in a more structured, tall muffin).
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Unsalted Butter, melted and cooled

recipeInstructions.text: Mix: Whisk dry ingredients in a large bowl. In a separate bowl, whisk wet ingredients. Fold together until just moistened (streaks of flour are okay).
The Rest: Let the batter sit at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Preheat: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Portion: Fill muffin cups to the absolute top. Sprinkle with extra sugar or chips.
The Rise: Bake at 425°F for 5 minutes.
The Finish: Without opening the oven door, reduce heat to 375°F. Bake for another 12-15 minutes.
Cool: Let cool for 10 minutes before removing from the tin.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, kid-friendly, weekend-project, comfort-food, bake

recipes.name: Balsamic Peach Pork Chops
recipes.description: Balsamic and peaches is an Italian pairing - sweet fruit cutting through savory pork, with the vinegar providing acidity that bridges the two. Cook these pork chops to at least 145°F in the thickest part, away from the bone, then rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipeInstructions.text: Sear: Heat oil in a large cast-iron skillet over high heat. Season pork with salt and pepper. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden.
The Glaze: Reduce heat to medium. Pour in the balsamic vinegar, honey, and thyme. Simmer for 3 minutes until the liquid is thick and syrupy.
Peaches: Place peach slices on top of and around the pork chops.
Broil: Transfer the skillet to the oven (under the broiler). Broil for 4-5 minutes until the peaches are charred at the edges and the pork hits 145°F.
Finish: Remove from oven. Sprinkle with feta, fresh basil, and chili flakes. Let rest for 5 minutes.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, spicy, sweet, acidic, herbaceous, weeknight, bake, simmer

recipes.name: Banana Egg Oat Pancakes
recipes.description: These are a gym staple made famous by bodybuilders - a high-protein, no-flour pancake that blends banana, eggs, and oats into a batter with the texture of crepes. The banana provides natural sweetness and moisture, so these need almost no oil; cook them at medium heat or the outside browns before the inside sets.
recipeIngredient: 1 large ripe Banana (the spottier the better)
1 tbsp Almond Butter or Peanut Butter
Butter or Coconut Oil for searing

recipeInstructions.text: Mash: In a medium bowl, mash the banana until almost liquid.
Mix: Whisk in the eggs, oats, nut butter, cinnamon, and salt until a cohesive batter forms.
Heat: Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add a tiny amount of butter or oil.
Sear: Drop 3-inch circles of batter into the pan. Do not move them for 3 minutes until the edges are set and bubbles appear.
Flip: Carefully flip and cook for only 60 seconds on the other side.
Serve: Serve hot with fresh fruit and a drizzle of maple syrup.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, quick-lunch, snack, weeknight, pan-fry

recipes.name: Banana Nut Bread
recipes.description: The secret to banana bread that isn't dense or dry is precision with measurements. Bananas vary wildly in size, so weighing them ensures consistent results.
recipeIngredient: 3 large Very Ripe Bananas (about 375g total), mashed
1/2 cup (1 stick) Unsalted Butter, melted and cooled
1/2 cup Walnuts or Toasted Sunflower Seeds, chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x5 loaf pan.
Melt: Melt the butter and let it cool slightly.
Wet: In a large bowl, whisk the mashed bananas, melted butter, sugar, eggs, and vanilla until smooth.
Dry: In a separate bowl, whisk the flour, baking soda, and salt.
Combine: Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet until just combined. Do not over-mix. Fold in the nuts/seeds.
Bake: Pour into the pan. Bake for 55-60 minutes until the top is split and a tester comes out clean.
Rest: Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, bake

recipes.name: Banana Oat Greek Yogurt Muffins
recipes.description: Blending rolled oats into flour creates smooth muffins without grittiness. Greek yogurt provides moisture and protein while reducing the need for added fat.

recipeInstructions.text: Blender: Place the oats, bananas, yogurt, eggs, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda in a blender or food processor. Process on high for 1 minute until smooth and creamy.
Fold: Stir in the chocolate chips by hand.
Portion: Pour into a greased or lined 12-cup muffin tin, filling 3/4 full.
Bake: Bake at 400°F for 15-18 minutes until the tops are golden and springy to the touch.
Cool: Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, snack, bake, blend

recipes.name: Banana Pancakes
recipes.description: These are real pancakes with real batter -- not the two-ingredient banana-egg variety that falls apart on the griddle. Mashing ripe bananas into a proper buttermilk batter gives you fluffy, tender pancakes with unmistakable banana flavor throughout.
recipeIngredient: 2 large Ripe Bananas, mashed (about 3/4 cup total)
3 tbsp Unsalted Butter, melted and slightly cooled
Butter or oil for the griddle
Maple syrup and sliced bananas for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Mix Dry: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon.
Mix Wet: In a separate bowl, combine buttermilk, mashed bananas, eggs, melted butter, and vanilla. Stir until just combined.

Combine: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Fold gently with a spatula until just combined -- the batter should be lumpy with a few streaks of flour still visible. Do not whisk. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.

Heat the Griddle: Heat a griddle or large nonstick skillet over medium heat (325°F if using an electric griddle). Lightly grease with butter. Test with a drop of water -- it should sizzle and evaporate within a second.

Cook: Pour 1/3 cup batter per pancake. Cook until the surface is covered in bubbles that begin to pop and the edges look set, about 2-3 minutes. Flip and cook for 1-2 minutes more until golden brown on the bottom and cooked through.

Serve: Stack pancakes and top with sliced bananas, a pat of butter, and warm maple syrup. Leftover pancakes freeze well -- cool completely, layer between parchment paper, and store in a freezer bag for up to 2 months. Reheat in a toaster.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, weekend-brunch, comfort-food, kid-friendly, saute

recipes.name: Banana Pudding
recipes.description: Banana and vanilla pudding folded with whipped topping, layered with sliced bananas and vanilla wafers for a cool, creamy spoon dessert.
recipeIngredient: 3.4 oz (96 g) sugar-sweetened banana-cream instant pudding mix; a four-serving packet formulated for 2 cups milk
3.4 oz (96 g) sugar-sweetened vanilla instant pudding mix; a four-serving packet formulated for 2 cups milk
16 oz (454 g) frozen whipped topping, thawed in the refrigerator, divided
11 oz (311 g) small crisp vanilla wafer cookies, divided
3 medium ripe but firm bananas, sliced just before layering

recipeInstructions.text: Divide the topping and wafers: Keep half the thawed whipped topping, refrigerated for the top. Reserve 20 g of the wafers in a sealed container for garnish; use all the rest in the layers.

Mix the pudding: Pour the cold milk into a large bowl. Whisk in both pudding powders gradually, then whisk for about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl until no dry pockets remain. The base will be very thick. Blend in the condensed milk gradually until smooth, then stir in the vanilla.
Fold: Fold the other half of the whipped topping into the pudding with a flexible spatula, turning the bowl and lifting from the bottom. Stop when the color is even and no large white streaks remain.

Layer: Peel and cut the bananas into roughly 1/4-inch slices. In a 4-quart serving dish, layer half the unreserved wafers, half the bananas and half the pudding. Repeat with the remaining wafers, bananas and pudding, spreading it to cover the fruit. Spread the refrigerated half of the whipped topping over the surface.

Chill and serve: Cover the dish without pressing down the topping and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until fully cold and the wafers are spoon-tender. Crush the reserved wafers over the top just before serving. Spoon into twelve dessert portions, reaching through the layers. Coffee or unsweetened tea suits its rich sweetness.

recipes.keywords: Southern, American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, entertaining, holiday, no-cook, assemble

citation.name: Bette Lordeman

recipes.name: Basmati Rice
recipes.description: A controlled stovetop absorption method, with plain, cumin, or whole-spice options and clear checks before resting.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups (400 g) aged white basmati rice, not parboiled or quick-cooking
3 cups (720 ml) water, for the unsoaked stovetop method
1 tbsp ghee, butter, or neutral oil
1 small cinnamon stick, about 1 inch long, optional
2 tbsp hot water, only if needed to finish firm grains

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and drain: Rinse rice in several changes of cool water until much of the loose starch has washed away. Drain thoroughly. Do not soak for this written method.

Heat fat and optional spices: In a 2–3 quart heavy saucepan, heat the ghee, butter, or oil over medium heat. If using spices, add them and stir for 20–30 seconds until fragrant. For plain rice, proceed directly to the next step.
Add rice and water: Stir in drained rice briefly to coat. Add the measured water and salt and bring to a gentle boil. Stir once, cover tightly, and lower heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

Cook and check: Simmer about 15–18 minutes. Check near the end that water is absorbed and taste a grain for an almost tender center. If it is still hard and the pot is dry, add the measured hot water, re-cover, and cook a little longer. If water remains and grains are firm, continue gently before resting.
Rest and fluff: Turn off heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Remove visible whole spices and fluff gently with a fork. Serve promptly or cool safely for storage.

recipes.keywords: Indian, Middle Eastern, aromatic, nutty, warm, buttery, weeknight, everyday, meal-prep, family-meal, kid-friendly, saute, simmer, steam

recipes.name: BBQ Chicken Sliders
recipes.description: The difference between good and great sliders is building flavor at every step. Marinating the thighs in BBQ sauce with smoked paprika for even 30 minutes infuses flavor deep into the meat - don't skip this.
recipeIngredient: 6 slices Sharp Cheddar Cheese (halved to fit sliders)

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate: Toss chicken thighs with 1/3 cup BBQ sauce, olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Let sit 30 minutes at room temperature (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Broil: Position rack 6 inches from broiler. Remove chicken from marinade, shake off excess. Broil on a sheet pan for 6-7 minutes per side until charred and cooked through (165°F).
Glaze & Cheese: Brush hot chicken generously with remaining BBQ sauce. Top each thigh with cheddar. Broil 1-2 more minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Toast Rolls: While chicken rests, brush cut sides of Hawaiian rolls with melted butter. Place cut-side down on a sheet pan and toast under broiler for 1-2 minutes until golden.
Slice: Let chicken rest 5 minutes. Slice into slider-sized pieces.
Assemble: Add chicken with melted cheese to toasted rolls. Top with pickles and crispy fried onions. Serve with extra BBQ sauce.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, sweet, smoky, entertaining, game-day, weeknight, broil

recipes.name: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Thin sirloin slices and broccoli with a glossy soy-oyster sauce, cooked in small batches and combined gently at the finish.
recipeIngredient: 680 g trimmed boneless top sirloin steak, weighed after removing tough outer membranes
450 g trimmed broccoli, florets about 1 1/2 inches wide and peeled stems sliced 1/4 inch thick
1/4 cup (60 ml) water, for steaming broccoli, divided
2 tbsp water, reserved for correcting dry broccoli or thick sauce
1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted beef stock or water
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil, added after sauce thickens
40 g scallions, white parts thinly sliced and green parts cut into 1-inch lengths
1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, optional garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare everything: Pat the steak dry and cut across the grain into roughly 1/4-inch-thick, 2-inch-long slices. Divide into three batches of about 225 g. Cut the broccoli as listed and divide in half. Whisk soy sauce, oyster sauce, vinegar, stock or sauce water, cornstarch and white pepper together. Keep sesame oil separate. Mince garlic and ginger and separate scallion whites and greens.

Brown and steam broccoli in two batches: Heat the pan over medium-high heat. Add 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil and half the broccoli. Cook about two minutes, turning occasionally, until some edges brown. Lower the heat slightly, carefully add 2 tbsp of the steaming water and cover for 2–3 minutes. Check a thick stem; use a little reserved water and another short steam if still hard. Uncover and let remaining water evaporate, about 30–60 seconds. Transfer to a bowl. Repeat with the other half, another 1 1/2 tsp oil and the remaining 2 tbsp steaming water.

Sear three beef batches: Let the empty pan dry and regain medium-high heat. Add 1 1/2 tsp oil; it should shimmer without heavy smoke. Spread one beef batch in one layer. Leave for about one minute until browned underneath, then turn and stir-fry another 1–3 minutes as needed. Check representative thick slices with a fine-tip thermometer inserted from the edge: at least 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat twice with 1 1/2 tsp oil per batch. Turn the heat down if residue blackens; remove burned deposits before continuing. Allow the beef at least three minutes after reaching temperature before serving.

Make the sauce: Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil, garlic, ginger and scallion whites. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant, keeping the garlic pale. Re-stir the sauce and pour it in. Bring to a gentle bubble, stirring for about 45–90 seconds until glossy and lightly thickened. Stir in the separate tablespoon sesame oil. Use reserved water in small spoonfuls if the sauce is too thick. Pour half the sauce into a heatproof cup.

Combine in two rounds: Add half the beef and its collected juices, half the broccoli and half the scallion greens to the sauce remaining in the pan. Fold over medium heat for about 30–60 seconds to coat and rewarm, then transfer to a serving platter. Return the reserved sauce to the pan and fold in the rest of the beef, juices, broccoli and scallion greens. Once hot and coated, add this round to the platter. Do not keep boiling the meat to chase a thicker glaze.

Serve: Confirm at least three minutes have elapsed since the last beef batch reached 145°F / 63°C. Divide into four portions and scatter the optional teaspoon of sesame seeds over the full dish. Serve with plain rice prepared separately; the stir-fry already includes its vegetable portion.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, American, savory, umami, warm, weeknight, stir-fry, sear, steam

recipes.name: Beef Chow Fun
recipes.description: Wide rice noodles, tender beef, ginger, scallions and bean sprouts with a thin soy coating, finished in four small batches for a home pan.
recipeIngredient: 450 g trimmed flank steak, sliced across the grain about 1/8 inch thick and 2 inches long
1 tbsp regular soy sauce, for the beef
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, for the beef
1 tsp neutral oil, for the beef coating
680 g fresh wide rice noodles (ho fun), about 3/4–1 inch wide
120 g fresh mung bean sprouts, rinsed and well drained
60 g trimmed scallions, cut into 2-inch lengths, white and green parts separated
4 tbsp neutral oil, for cooking, divided
2 tbsp water, reserved for loosening noodles only if needed
2 tbsp regular soy sauce, for the noodles
2 tbsp Shaoxing wine, for the noodles

recipeInstructions.text: Coat the beef: Stir the beef's measured soy, wine, coating water, cornstarch and measured baking soda until dispersed. Add the thinly sliced beef, turn and gently mix until evenly coated, then mix in its measured coating oil. Cover and refrigerate for twenty minutes while preparing everything else. Do not rinse off this small-dose coating or add more baking soda.

Prepare flexible noodles: Separate supple fresh noodles gently. If they are cold and stiff, follow the package warming directions. Where the package permits microwaving, transfer noodles out of non-microwave-safe packaging to a microwave-safe plate, cover loosely and warm in short 20–30-second intervals, checking and turning between intervals until they separate without force. Work in manageable portions; one fixed thirty-second blast is not enough for every cold block. Cut whole sheets into 3/4–1-inch ribbons if necessary. Divide the prepared noodles into four 170 g portions.

Mix and portion: Whisk the noodle soy, Chinese dark soy, noodle wine, sugar and sesame oil, then divide the mixture into four equal portions. Prepare ginger, scallions and drained sprouts. Keep scallion whites and greens separate; divide each and the ginger into four portions. Set out clean bowls for the cooked sprouts and beef.

Cook sprouts separately: Heat 1 tsp of the cooking oil in the pan over medium-high heat. Add the sprouts and stir for about one minute. Add the measured sprout-cooking water, cover for 1–2 minutes, then uncover and let free water evaporate. The sprouts should be steaming hot and softened through their stems, not merely warmed on the surface; extend briefly if needed. Transfer to a clean bowl and divide into four portions.

Cook two beef batches: Let the pan dry and recover heat. Add 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil and spread half the beef in one layer, leaving excess loose coating in its raw-meat bowl. Cook about one minute until browned below, turn, and cook another 1–3 minutes as needed. Check representative thicker slices with a fine probe inserted sideways from the edge: at least 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat with another 1 1/2 tsp oil and the other half. Discard leftover raw-contact coating and wash its bowl and tools. Divide the cooked beef and its juices into four portions; each has time to rest at least three minutes before serving.

Finish one noodle portion: Reduce heat if the pan is smoking heavily; remove any blackened deposits. Add 2 tsp of the remaining cooking oil over medium-high heat. Stir in one portion of ginger and scallion whites for about 20 seconds until fragrant. Add one noodle portion and lift gently to coat, then let it touch the pan for 15–20 seconds at a time, lifting and turning between contacts. Add one portion of noodle seasoning and fold until evenly coated. Add one portion each of cooked beef, juices, sprouts and scallion greens. Fold just until hot throughout, about 3–4 minutes for this whole finishing step. If firm noodles need moisture, use a little of the reserved water rather than adding extra soy; use no more than the full measured noodle-water reserve across the batch.

Plate and repeat: Serve the first portion promptly, confirming at least three minutes have passed since its beef reached 145°F / 63°C. Repeat step 6 three more times, letting the empty pan recover heat between portions before adding each fresh 2 tsp oil; add aromatics once that oil shimmers. Use the remaining measured ingredient portions. Serve as four moderate noodle-main portions. A separately prepared vegetable side can accompany them; extra rice is unnecessary because the noodles already supply the starch.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, Cantonese, savory, toasted, umami, weeknight, comfort-food, stir-fry, sear

recipes.name: Beef Hot Dogs with Corn Relish
recipes.description: Hot dogs made from beef tenderloin aren't a tradition - they're a luxury. The corn relish is the main event: fresh corn kernels provide sweetness and texture that store-bought relish can't match.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Center-cut Beef Tenderloin, cut into 4 long "dogs"
4 6-inch Baguette pieces or High-quality Brioche Buns
1 cup Roasted Corn (charred in a pan or oven)
1/4 cup Red Bell Pepper, finely diced

recipeInstructions.text: The Relish: In a small bowl, whisk the vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Toss with the roasted corn, peppers, and onions. Let marinate while you cook the beef.
The Beef: Rub the tenderloin strips with oil, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper.

The Sear: Heat a cast-iron skillet or grill to high. Sear the beef strips until browned on each side, starting to check after 2-3 minutes per side. Insert a thermometer from the side into the center of each piece and continue cooking until it reaches 145°F / 63°C; lower the heat if the outside browns too quickly. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
The Bread: Toast the baguette or brioche buns until golden.
Assemble: Place a beef strip in each bun. Top generously with the corn relish.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, entertaining, weekend-project, bake, roast, grill, no-cook

recipes.name: Cinnamon Rolls
recipes.description: The tangzhong method - pre-cooking flour and water into a paste - is an Asian bread technique that keeps these rolls soft for days. It pre-gelatinizes starches so the dough holds more moisture without becoming sticky.
recipeIngredient: 8 tbsp European-style Salted Butter (cool room temp)

recipeInstructions.text: The Tangzhong: In a small saucepan, whisk 1/4 cup flour and 3/4 cup water. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly until it forms a thick paste. Let cool.
The Mix: In a stand mixer, combine flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Add the cream, milk, egg, vanilla, and the cooled Tangzhong. Knead with a dough hook for 2 minutes.
The Butter: On low speed, add the 8 tbsp butter one tablespoon at a time. Once incorporated, knead for 10-12 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test.
First Rise: Shape into a ball, place in a greased bowl, cover, and let rest in a warm spot for 30 minutes.
Shape: On a floured surface, roll dough into a 15x21-inch rectangle. Spread the cinnamon filling to the edges, leaving a 1-inch border at the top.
The Cut: Use a pizza cutter to slice twelve 1.75-inch strips. Roll each strip tightly and place in a parchment-lined 9x13 pan.
Second Rise: Cover and let rise until doubled (1-2 hours). Preheat oven to 325°F.
Bake: Bake for 30-35 minutes until the tops are just starting to turn golden brown.
The Frosting: Whip the cream cheese and butter until smooth. Mix in powdered sugar, vanilla, and cream until fluffy.
Finish: Let the rolls cool for 15 minutes, then spread the frosting generously while they are still warm to allow some of it to seep into the spirals.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, weekend-project, comfort-food, holiday, bake

recipes.name: Brownies
recipes.description: Extra-virgin olive oil adds fruity depth that pairs beautifully with dark chocolate. Powdered sugar in the dry mix creates the signature crackly, paper-thin crust on top while the center stays fudgy.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Dark Chocolate Chips (60% cacao or higher)

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 325°F. Spray an 8x8 baking pan and line with parchment paper so it hangs over the edges. Spray the parchment too.
Dry Mix: In a medium bowl, whisk together the sugar, flour, cocoa, powdered sugar, chocolate chips, and salt.
Wet Mix: In a large bowl, whisk eggs, olive oil, water, and vanilla until well combined and slightly frothy.
Combine: Sprinkle the dry ingredients over the wet. Fold gently with a spatula until just combined. The batter will be very thick.
Bake: Spread evenly in the prepared pan. Bake for 40-45 minutes until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
The Finish: Allow to cool completely in the pan for at least 2 hours before slicing. This is mandatory for the structure to set.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, bake

recipes.name: Bibimbap
recipes.description: Bibimbap has roots in Korean royal court cuisine but became a peasant dish in the Joseon Dynasty, when farmers would mix leftover vegetables and rice in a bowl. The name means 'mixed rice,' and it reflects the Korean philosophy of balance - multiple flavors and textures coming together in harmony.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Have all your component recipes ready (Ribeye, Cucumbers, etc.).
Base: Scoop 1 cup of hot rice into each bowl. (Tip: For crispy rice, use the "Cast Iron Skillet Hack" mentioned in the Ribeye recipe).
The Clock: Arrange the prepared vegetables and meat in distinct piles around the perimeter of the bowl, moving clockwise.
The Crown: Place the fried egg in the center.
Sauce: Drizzle the mixed Gochujang sauce over the egg.
Serve: Mix vigorously before eating.

recipes.keywords: Korean, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, rich, weeknight, meal-prep, fry, saute

recipes.name: Big-Batch Chicken Chili Verde
recipes.description: Browned chicken thighs braised in roasted tomatillo and poblano sauce, with a small white-bean addition and measured fresh toppings.
recipeIngredient: 1.35 kg (3 lb) boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 1/2 tsp fine salt, divided and partly added to taste
1.35 kg (3 lb) tomatillos, weighed after removing husks, rinsed and halved
3 poblano peppers, about 450 g before trimming
2 jalapeños, optional or reduced for milder heat
2 cups (480 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, divided, plus up to 1 cup (240 ml) only if needed to loosen
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) plain white beans, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Roast peppers: Heat the broiler and position a rimmed tray about 6 inches from the element, following the oven's guidance. Broil whole poblanos and optional jalapeños, turning regularly, about 12–20 minutes until blistered. Put them in a heatproof bowl and cover for 10 minutes. Peel loose charred skin, remove stems and seed cores, and chop; handle hot chiles with care and wash hands before touching eyes.

Roast tomatillos: Arrange halved tomatillos cut-side down on the tray, retaining their juices. Broil about 10–15 minutes until soft with browned or blistered tops. Use two batches if they cannot fit in one layer. Watch rather than following the clock past burning.

Blend the sauce: Let vegetables cool enough for your blender's warm-liquid guidance. Blend tomatillos and collected juices with peeled peppers and 1 cup of the measured broth, in batches as needed. Vent as the appliance directs; do not seal steaming liquid in a personal blender. Have this sauce ready before beginning the chicken.

Brown chicken: Pat chicken dry and season with two-thirds of the listed salt. Heat 2 tsp oil in a roomy Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown one-third of the chicken on two sides, about 5–6 minutes, then transfer to a bowl. Repeat twice with 2 tsp oil per batch. The centers need the following braise; continue directly.

Build aromatics: Lower heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Cook onion about 6–8 minutes until softened. Add garlic, cumin, coriander and optional cayenne and stir about 30 seconds. Pour in the remaining initial 1 cup broth and scrape up brown residue, then add the blended green sauce and chicken with its juices.

Braise and check: Bring to a gentle simmer, partly cover and cook about 25–35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and are tender. Add a little of the extra broth only if sauce is too thick before the meat is ready. Stir in drained beans for the final 5 minutes to heat through.

Finish: If sauce needs further reduction, remove finished chicken briefly and simmer the sauce alone, then return it. Turn off heat. Taste and add the remaining salt only if needed. Stir in cilantro and start with just a little lime juice, adding more only if the sauce benefits.

Serve and portion: Divide into eight servings. Offer the listed sour cream, radishes and tortilla strips as optional full-batch supplies. Omit sour cream for a dairy-free version and check packaged ingredients. Bread or slaw is prepared separately.

recipes.keywords: Mexican-inspired, savory, spicy, acidic, umami, meal-prep, entertaining, comfort-food, weekend-project, broil, sear, simmer

recipes.name: Soft Black Bean Tacos with Lime Crema
recipes.description: Partly mashed black beans with softened onion, warm tortillas, lime crema and measured fresh toppings.
recipeIngredient: 2 cans (15 oz / 425 g each) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 510 g drained total
1/2 cup (120 ml) low-sodium vegetable broth, plus a little only if needed
1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually to taste
1/2 cup (120 g) Mexican crema or plain Greek yogurt
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus up to 1 tsp more to taste
1/8 tsp fine salt, only if needed
1 tbsp water, only if needed to loosen yogurt
8 soft corn or flour tortillas, about 6 inches across
200 g tomatoes, diced and drained of pooled juice

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare toppings and crema: Shred cabbage, dice and drain tomatoes, chop cilantro and cut the serving lime. Stir crema or yogurt with the initial measured lime juice. Taste before adding the crema's optional salt and reserved juice; thin thick yogurt with up to the measured water allowance. Refrigerate while cooking.

Soften the aromatics: Heat oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Add onion and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent. Add garlic for 30 seconds, then cumin, chili powder and smoked paprika for about 20 seconds. Lower heat if the spices begin to darken.

Build the filling: Add drained beans, broth and half the bean salt. Simmer gently 5–7 minutes, stirring. Mash about one-third of the beans with a fork or masher, then stir into a soft, thick filling. Add a little broth if stiff; simmer briefly if watery. Taste and add the remaining bean salt only if needed, remembering the optional cheese is salty.

Warm the tortillas: Cover beans off heat for the short warming period. In a second dry skillet, warm tortillas over medium-high for roughly 10–30 seconds per side until hot and pliable, then wrap in a clean towel. For one skillet, microwave four tortillas at a time between damp paper towels for 30–45 seconds, adding short bursts if needed.

Fill and serve: Divide beans among eight tortillas. Add cabbage, tomato, cilantro, a little lime crema and optional measured cotija. Serve two tacos per person, with wedges to adjust the lime at the table. Assemble at serving so the cabbage stays crisp and tortillas do not soak through.

recipes.keywords: Mexican-inspired, savory, fresh, zesty, creamy, weeknight, kid-friendly, meal-prep, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Blackout Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: Blackout cake is impossibly rich and moist - the secret is blooming cocoa powder in boiling water (like tea), which extracts flavor and hydrates the powder fully before it meets the batter. Greek yogurt adds tanginess and moisture while keeping the crumb tender.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Instant Espresso Powder (The depth secret)

recipeInstructions.text: Bloom: In a large bowl, whisk the boiling water with the cocoa powder and espresso powder. Let it sit for 2 minutes to bloom the chocolate.
Wet: Whisk in the yogurt, oil, eggs, and vanilla until smooth.
Dry: In a separate bowl, whisk flour, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt.
Combine: Gradually fold the dry ingredients into the chocolate liquid.
Bake: Pour into three 9-inch lined pans. Bake at 350°F for 30-35 minutes. Cool completely.
Frost: Use a rich chocolate ganache or cream cheese frosting.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, holiday, entertaining, weekend-project, comfort-food, bake, boil

recipes.name: Blistered Shishito Peppers
recipes.description: Shishito peppers are mild and sweet with the occasional spicy surprise -- roughly one in ten packs real heat, which makes eating them a fun gamble. The technique is dead simple: screaming hot pan, dry peppers, no oil until the last second.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Shishito Peppers, left whole with stems on

recipeInstructions.text: Heat the Pan: Set a cast-iron skillet over high heat for 2 minutes until it just begins to smoke. You need the pan ripping hot for proper blistering.

Blister: Add the oil, then immediately add the shishito peppers in a single layer. Let them sit undisturbed for 60-90 seconds until the skins blister and blacken in spots. Toss once and cook another 60-90 seconds until charred on a second side.
Season: Transfer peppers immediately to a serving plate. Squeeze lemon over the top, sprinkle with flaky salt and sesame seeds.
Serve: Eat immediately while hot, picking them up by the stems. These do not hold well -- the texture goes soft within minutes.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, smoky, savory, mild, weeknight, appetizer, sear, saute

recipes.name: Blueberry Oatmeal
recipes.description: Layering berries at the bottom prevents a mushy, uniform texture - they stay whole and jammy. Toasted sunflower or pumpkin seeds on top add crunch that contrasts with creamy oats below.
recipeIngredient: 2/3 cup Toasted Sunflower Seeds or Pumpkin Seeds (Nut-Free option)

recipeInstructions.text: Dry: In a bowl, toss oats, seeds, cinnamon, salt, and baking powder.
Wet: Whisk milk, eggs, maple syrup, vanilla, and half the melted butter.
Layer: Arrange 1 cup of blueberries at the bottom of a greased baking dish. Cover with the oat mixture.
Hydrate: Pour the milk mixture over the oats. Wiggle the dish so the liquid sinks in. Top with remaining berries.
Bake: Bake at 375°F for 40-45 minutes until the top is golden and the center is set.
Finish: Drizzle with the remaining melted butter.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, weekend-project, comfort-food, bake

recipes.name: Blueberry Banana Pancake Muffins
recipes.description: These are essentially "Pancakes in a Pan. " The secret to their fluffy, rich texture is the Cottage Cheese Emulsion: when blended, the cottage cheese acts as a high-protein fat source that creates a souffle-like lift in the oven.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Full-Fat Cottage Cheese (The protein secret)

recipeInstructions.text: Emulsify: In a blender, combine bananas, oats, cottage cheese, eggs, syrup, and vanilla. Process until completely smooth.
Portion: Pour the batter into a greased 12-cup muffin tin.
Top: Press 4-5 blueberries into the top of each muffin.
Bake: Bake at 350°F for 25-30 minutes until they are puffed and golden.
Cool: Let sit for 5 minutes before removing.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, snack, quick-lunch, bake, blend

recipes.name: Blueberry Date Oatmeal
recipes.description: Frozen riced cauliflower adds volume and fiber without affecting flavor. Stir frozen blueberries in at the end rather than cooking them - this prevents the oatmeal from turning gray while keeping berries whole and bright.

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: In a medium saucepan (stovetop) or a large microwave-safe bowl, combine oats, cauliflower, water/milk, chopped dates, and coconut oil.
Cook (Stovetop): Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently, until the liquid is absorbed and the oats are creamy.
Cook (Microwave): Heat on high for 3 minutes, stir, then heat for another 2-3 minutes until thickened.
The Berry Finish: Remove from heat. Gently fold in the frozen blueberries. Let sit for 1 minute - the residual heat will thaw the berries while keeping them whole.
Serve: Top with a pinch of sea salt and cinnamon.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, weeknight, quick-lunch, snack, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Blueberry Oat Breakfast Bars
recipes.description: Firmly pressing the mixture into the pan and then refrigerating for at least one hour after baking prevents crumbling. As the coconut oil and nut butter chill and solidify, they bind the oats into clean, portable bars that hold together beautifully.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Greek Yogurt or Coconut Cream

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 340°F (170°C). Line an 8x8-inch baking dish with parchment paper.
Melt: In a large saucepan, melt coconut oil, honey, and nut butter over medium heat. Stir until smooth and combined.
Mix: Remove from heat. Stir in the oats until every grain is coated. Gently fold in the blueberries.
Press: Transfer the mixture to the baking dish. Use the back of a spoon to press down very firmly - the more compact it is, the better it will hold.
Bake: Bake for 15-18 minutes until the edges are just beginning to turn golden brown.
The Finish: Allow to cool in the pan at room temperature, then transfer to the fridge for at least 1 hour (mandatory) to firm up.
Glaze: Whisk together the yogurt and orange juice. Drizzle over the chilled bars.
Slice: Cut into 8 bars and serve cold or at room temperature.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, snack, quick-lunch, kid-friendly, bake

recipes.name: Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.description: Letting the batter rest for 5 minutes after mixing allows flour to hydrate and gluten to relax, creating fluffier pancakes. Honey instead of granulated sugar produces deeper caramelization on the edges.
recipeIngredient: 3 tbsp Unsalted Butter, melted and cooled

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Heat a griddle to 350°F (or a large non-stick skillet over medium-low heat). Lightly grease with butter.
Aeration: In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, and vanilla until light and frothy (about 2-3 minutes). Whisk in the melted butter and honey.
Combine: Sift in the flour, salt, and baking powder. Stir with a spatula until just combined. A few lumps are mandatory - do not overmix!
The Rest: Let the batter sit for 5 minutes. It will thicken and become slightly bubbly.
Pour: Use a 1/4 cup scoop to drop batter onto the hot griddle. Immediately sprinkle 1 tbsp of blueberries onto the wet surface of each pancake.
Flip: Cook for 2 minutes until bubbles form and pop on the surface and the bottom is golden. Flip and cook for another 2 minutes.
Serve: Serve immediately with salted butter and warm maple syrup.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, griddle

recipes.name: Peking Ravioli
recipes.description: Peking ravioli (also called potstickers) were popularized in Boston by Joyce Chen's restaurant in the 1950s-60s. The Boston style is distinctive for its thick, chewy wrapper - more like pasta than delicate dim sum.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups Napa Cabbage, finely minced and squeezed dry
2 tbsp Chinkiang Black Vinegar (or Balsamic fallback)

itemListElement.text: Mix: Place flour in a bowl. Slowly pour in the boiling water while stirring with chopsticks until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Knead for 5-8 minutes until smooth. Cover with a damp cloth and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll: Divide into small balls. Roll each into a circle about 3.5 inches wide. They should be significantly thicker than a standard wonton wrapper (about 1/8 inch).
Squeeze: Ensure the minced cabbage is salted and squeezed in a towel to remove ALL moisture. (Watery cabbage = soggy ravioli).
Mix: Combine all filling ingredients. Stir vigorously in one direction for 3 minutes until the meat is sticky and emulsified.
Portion: Place a large tablespoon of filling in each wrapper.
Seal: Fold in half and pleat only 3-4 times (the Boston style is more rustic and "chunky" than delicate). Press hard to seal.
Sear: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large flat-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Place ravioli in the pan and fry undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until the bottoms are dark golden.
Steam: Pour in 1/2 cup of water and immediately cover with a tight lid. Reduce heat to medium and steam for 6-8 minutes until the water is gone.
Crisp: Remove lid. Add 1 more tsp of oil. Fry for 1 more minute until the bottoms "crackle" and are perfectly crisp.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, weekend-project, entertaining, comfort-food, fry, boil, steam

recipes.name: Boulevardier
recipes.description: Created in 1920s Paris by American expat Erskine Gwynne, editor of a magazine called 'The Boulevardier,' this cocktail embodies the era of Americans living the high life in post-WWI Paris. It's essentially a whiskey Negroni, swapping gin for bourbon or rye, and was popular at Harry's New York Bar, the legendary watering hole of Hemingway and F.

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: Add the bourbon, red Italian bitter aperitif and sweet vermouth to a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir well for 20-30: seconds until properly chilled.
Strain into a chilled: coupe glass or over a large ice cube in an Old Fashioned glass.
Express an orange peel: over the drink and garnish.
Serve immediately.:

recipes.keywords: American, rich, savory, acidic, entertaining, date-night, comfort-food, no-cook

recipes.name: Braised French Lentils
recipes.description: French green lentils (lentilles du Puy) are the only lentils worth braising as a side dish. Unlike their brown or red cousins, they hold their shape beautifully and develop a firm, almost al dente bite.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 cups French Green Lentils (lentilles du Puy), rinsed and picked over
3.5 cups Low-Sodium Vegetable or Chicken Broth

recipeInstructions.text: Build the Base: Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven or heavy saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 6-7 minutes until the vegetables are softened and the onion is translucent. Add garlic and cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Add Lentils and Aromatics: Stir in the lentils, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Pour in the broth and stir to combine. Bring to a boil over high heat.

Braise: Reduce heat to low, partially cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape. They should be creamy inside with a slight bite. Most of the liquid should be absorbed -- if it evaporates too quickly, add a splash of water.
Finish: Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Stir in the Dijon mustard and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Fold in the fresh parsley just before serving.

recipes.keywords: French, earthy, savory, herbaceous, aromatic, weeknight, meal-prep, braise, simmer, saute

recipes.name: Breakfast Burrito
recipes.description: A good breakfast burrito is all about assembly order and restraint -- overfill it and it becomes an unwrappable mess. Cooking the peppers and onions first gives them time to soften and release their moisture before the eggs go in, preventing a soggy tortilla.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Red or Green Bell Pepper, diced small
1 cup Shredded Cheddar or Pepper Jack Cheese
4 slices Cooked Bacon or 1/2 cup Cooked Breakfast Sausage, crumbled
Optional: salsa, hot sauce, sour cream, avocado slices

recipeInstructions.text: Cook Vegetables: Melt butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add bell pepper and onion. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened.

Scramble Eggs: Whisk eggs with milk and salt. Pour into the skillet with the vegetables. Stir gently with a spatula, folding from the edges to the center, until the eggs are just set but still slightly glossy, about 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat immediately.
Warm Tortillas: In a separate dry skillet over medium-high heat, warm each tortilla for 15-20 seconds per side until pliable and lightly toasted.
Assemble: Lay each tortilla flat. Layer in the center: a quarter of the scrambled egg mixture, a quarter of the cheese, and a quarter of the cooked bacon or sausage. Add optional toppings if desired.
Roll: Fold the bottom edge of the tortilla up over the filling, fold both sides in, then roll tightly away from you to seal. The cheese should melt from the residual heat of the eggs.
Serve: Serve immediately with salsa and hot sauce on the side. For meal prep, wrap each burrito tightly in foil before the cheese is added, let cool, and freeze.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, American, savory, spicy, rich, weeknight, meal-prep, quick-lunch, saute, toast

recipes.name: Breakfast Carrot Cake
recipes.description: Breakfast carrot cake splits the difference between muffin and snack cake - whole wheat flour and Greek yogurt give it enough structure and protein to pass as morning food, while the grated carrots keep it moist for days. The trick is grating on the fine holes, not the large ones - larger shreds release too much water during baking and create soggy pockets.
recipeIngredient: 250 g carrots, finely grated; about 2 large carrots at the original batch size

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 375°F / 190°C. Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment paper.
Grate: Finely grate the carrots using the small holes of a grater. Set aside.
Wet ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk large egg, granulated sugar, brown sugar, canola or avocado oil, plain Greek yogurt, and vanilla extract for 3–5 minutes until blended and frothy.
Dry ingredients: Whisk whole wheat flour, ground cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, and sea salt together, then fold gently into the wet mixture with a spatula.
Fold: Add carrots and walnuts or pecans. Fold until just combined; do not overmix.

Bake: Pour into the prepared pan and tap lightly to remove air bubbles. Bake for 25–30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Pan dimensions and baking time do not multiply with the ingredient scale; use additional pans for larger batches.
Cool: Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, weekend-project, bake

recipes.name: Breakfast Egg Cups
recipes.description: Slicing spinach into thin ribbons (chiffonade) prevents large, wet clumps in the finished muffins - the leaves wilt evenly into the egg. Fresh bell pepper adds crisp texture that contrasts with rich egg and melted cheddar.
recipeIngredient: 1 medium Red Bell Pepper, finely diced

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 375°F. Spray a standard muffin tin generously with cooking spray.
The Base: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs and milk until very frothy. Season with salt and pepper.
The Veg: Finely dice the red pepper. To chiffonade the spinach: stack the leaves, roll them tightly like a cigar, and slice thin ribbons.
Combine: Fold the peppers, spinach, and shredded cheese into the egg mixture.
Fill: Pour the mixture into the muffin cups, filling each about 3/4 full.
Bake: Bake for 20-25 minutes until the centers are set and the tops are slightly golden.
Cool: Allow to cool in the tin for 5 minutes before removing. These can be refrigerated for up to 4 days and reheated for 30 seconds in the microwave.

recipes.keywords: American, rich, meal-prep, weeknight, quick-lunch, bake

recipes.name: Breakfast Protein Biscuits
recipes.description: Greek yogurt replaces heavy cream as the primary liquid, creating high-protein biscuits with a tender crumb. Fold spinach and ham in at the end rather than mixing them thoroughly - this ensures distinct pockets of filling in every bite instead of a uniform gray dough.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Wet & Dry: In a medium bowl, whisk together the yogurt and eggs. In a separate large bowl, whisk the flour, flaxseed, garlic powder, red pepper flakes, baking powder, and salt.
Combine: Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet. Stir until a thick, sticky dough forms.
Fold: Fold in the chopped spinach, chives, ham, and two thirds of the measured cheese. Use your hands if necessary to ensure even distribution without overworking the dough.
Shape: Lightly flour your hands. Scoop about 1/3 cup of dough for each biscuit. Form into 1-inch thick disks and arrange on the baking sheet.
The Temperature Method: Sprinkle the remaining cheese on top. Bake at 400°F for 5 minutes (to kickstart the rise), then lower the heat to 350°F for the remaining 20 minutes.
Finish: They are done when the bottoms are golden brown and the cheese on top is bubbly and crisp.

recipes.keywords: American, rich, meal-prep, snack, weekend-project, bake

recipes.name: Breakfast Quesadilla
recipes.description: A breakfast quesadilla should be crispy on the outside, melty on the inside, and ready in under 15 minutes. The key is scrambling the eggs first and slightly undercooking them -- they will continue to cook inside the quesadilla from the residual heat and the time on the griddle.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Shredded Cheddar or Mexican Blend Cheese
Salsa and sour cream for serving
