recipeInstructions.text: Scramble Eggs: Melt butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Whisk eggs with salt and pour into the skillet. Stir gently with a spatula until the eggs are just barely set -- slightly wetter than you would normally eat them. Remove to a plate.

Build the Quesadilla: Wipe the skillet clean. Lay one tortilla flat. Spread half the cheese on one half of the tortilla, top with half the scrambled eggs and jalapenos (if using), then add the remaining cheese on top. Fold the tortilla in half. Repeat with the second tortilla.

Cook: Place the quesadilla in the dry skillet over medium heat. Cook for 2-3 minutes, pressing gently with a spatula, until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Flip carefully and cook for 2 minutes more until the other side is golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Slice and Serve: Transfer to a cutting board. Let rest for 30 seconds, then cut into thirds. Serve with salsa and sour cream on the side.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, American, savory, rich, spicy, weeknight, kid-friendly, quick-lunch, saute, toast

recipes.name: Brisket with Carrots and Onions
recipes.description: Flat-cut brisket braised in tomato juice with carrots, celery and plentiful onions, then sliced across the grain and served with soft vegetables and reduced tomato sauce.

recipeInstructions.text: Heat the oven and prepare the pan: Heat the oven to 350°F / 175°C. Choose a heavy roasting pan that holds the brisket in one layer with the vegetables and has room for the full can of tomato juice below its rim.
Season the brisket: Mix the kosher salt, pepper, garlic and oregano. Rub the mixture over all sides of the brisket.
Layer the braise: Put the brisket in the pan. Arrange all the carrots, celery, onions and bay leaves on and around it.

Add the tomato juice and seal: Pour in the entire 46-ounce can of tomato juice. The pan geometry and vegetables determine how high it comes around the meat; it does not need to reach a fixed mark. Lay two sheets of parchment over the pan, then seal tightly with heavy-duty foil.

Braise until tender: Bake, covered, for about 3 1/2 hours. Check the thickest part with an instant-read thermometer: it must reach at least 145°F / 63°C, followed by a 3-minute rest, and it must also be fork-tender. If the temperature is safe but the fork meets resistance, re-cover and continue in 15-minute intervals until tender.

Rest and reduce: Transfer the brisket to a cutting board and tent loosely with foil. Remove and discard all bay leaves. If the roasting pan is approved for stovetop use across two burners, use it; otherwise transfer all vegetables and sauce to a wide saucepan. Boil over medium-high heat for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until glossy and thickened but still saucy.
Slice and serve: Find the direction of the meat fibers and slice across the grain. Serve the brisket with the reduced sauce, carrots, celery and onions.

recipes.keywords: Jewish, savory, acidic, umami, rich, holiday, bake, roast, braise

recipes.name: Broccoli Cheddar Quinoa Bites
recipes.description: Press the mixture firmly when scooping to ensure eggs and cheese properly bind the quinoa and broccoli - loose scoops crumble apart. Fresh broccoli chopped finely maintains better texture than frozen, staying slightly crisp even after baking.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 375°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and lightly grease with oil spray.
Mix: In a large bowl, toss the cooked quinoa, chopped broccoli, cheddar, and green onions.
Bind: Stir in the beaten eggs, Parmesan, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Mix until every grain of quinoa is coated in the egg mixture.
Compress: Using a small cookie scoop or tablespoon, scoop the mixture and press it firmly against the side of the bowl to compact it. Place on the baking sheet.
Bake: Bake for 20-25 minutes until the edges are golden brown and the bites feel firm to the touch.
The Rest: Let the bites rest on the pan for 5 minutes before moving - this allows the cheese to "set," ensuring they hold their shape.

recipes.keywords: American, umami, herbaceous, entertaining, potluck, kid-friendly, meal-prep, bake

recipes.name: Broccolini, Chicken Sausage, and Orzo Skillet
recipes.description: This is a sheet-pan formula: protein, vegetable, starch, all in one vessel. Broccolini has a more tender stem than regular broccoli, so it cooks through without becoming mushy.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Hot Italian Chicken Sausage, sliced into rounds
1 cup Frozen Peas (replaces broccolini if kids prefer)

recipeInstructions.text: The Sear: Heat oil in a large skillet. Brown the sausage rounds for 3-4 minutes. Remove to a plate.
The Veg: Add broccolini to the same pan. Sauté over high heat for 5 minutes until charred and tender-crisp. Remove and keep with the sausage.
The Toast: Add the orzo and garlic to the pan. Toast for 30-45 seconds until fragrant and the orzo smells nutty.
The Simmer: Pour in the broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to low and cover. Simmer for 10 minutes until liquid is absorbed and pasta is al dente.
The Fold: Stir in the Parmesan, the reserved sausage, and the broccolini.
Finish: If the pasta is too dry, add a splash of hot water. Season with plenty of black pepper.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, spicy, umami, rich, kid-friendly, saute, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Brown Butter Carrot Cake
recipes.description: This is the Bravetart Upgrade to the BA classic. We replace generic vegetable oil with Brown Butter, which provides a nutty, toasted depth that standard carrot cakes lack.
recipeIngredient: 3/4 cup Unsalted Butter, browned and cooled
2 tsp Baking Powder + 3/4 tsp Baking Soda
2 tsp Vanilla Extract, for the cake
1 tsp Vanilla Extract, for the frosting

recipeInstructions.text: Brown the Butter: Melt the butter listed for the cake until dark golden and smelling like hazelnuts. Cool.
Batter: Whisk the brown butter, both sugars, eggs, and the cake vanilla for 4 minutes until pale and thick.
Fold: Whisk together the dry ingredients. Add to the butter mixture in 3 parts, alternating with the buttermilk and carrots.
Bake: Pour into two 9-inch lined pans. Bake at 350°F for 35-45 minutes. Cool completely.
Frosting: Beat cream cheese and butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar and the frosting vanilla.
Assemble: Layer and frost the cakes generously.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, holiday, entertaining, weekend-project, comfort-food, bake, no-cook

recipes.name: Brown Butter-Chocolate Soufflé
recipes.description: This French technique relies on properly whipped egg whites stabilized with cream of tartar, then carefully folded into chocolate ganache to preserve air bubbles. Brushing the chilled dish with brown butter and sugar creates a textured coating that helps batter climb the walls as it rises.

recipeInstructions.text: The Ladder: Cook butter in a skillet over medium heat until it foams and turns nutty brown (4 mins). Chill until spreadable (20 mins). Brush the bottom and sides of a chilled soufflé dish with the brown butter. Coat with 1/4 cup superfine sugar and tap out excess. Chill dish.
The Ganache: Preheat oven to 475°F. Melt chocolate into 1/2 cup steaming heavy cream. Whisk until smooth. Whisk in egg yolks one at a time.
The Flavor Layer: Whisk cocoa powder, rum, salt, and 1/2 cup hot water. Stir this into the chocolate ganache.
The Meringue: Using a mixer, beat egg whites, cream of tartar, and 1/3 cup sugar until glossy, stiff peaks form (5-7 mins). Do not over-whip; they should look like softly whipped cream.
The Fold: Gently fold the chocolate mixture into the egg whites. Use a "cut and fold" motion to preserve the air bubbles.
Bake: Transfer to the prepared dish. Sprinkle 1 tbsp sugar on top. Bake at 475°F for 25-30 minutes until puffed and set with a slight wobble in the center.
Serve: Dust with powdered sugar and serve immediately with extra heavy cream.

recipes.keywords: French, sweet, rich, entertaining, weekend-project, comfort-food, date-night, bake, steam

recipes.name: Brownie Oatmeal
recipes.description: Blending oats directly with wet ingredients creates a smooth, cake-like texture that mimics an actual brownie. Natural acids in the banana react with baking soda to provide rise and texture.
recipeIngredient: 1/4 cup Milk of choice (Almond or Oat preferred)

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a small oven-safe ramekin or baking dish.
Blend: Add oats, banana, egg, milk, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt to a blender. Blend on high until completely smooth.
Topping: Pour the batter into the prepared dish. Sprinkle chocolate chips on top.
Bake: Bake for 15-18 minutes until the center is set but still slightly soft (like a fudgy brownie).
Finish: Sprinkle with a pinch of flaky sea salt and serve warm.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, comfort-food, bake, blend

recipes.name: Brownie Protein Balls
recipes.description: These no-bake bites prep in bulk for lunchboxes, pre-workout snacks, or yogurt toppings. Different protein powders absorb liquid at varying rates, so add milk one teaspoon at a time until dough reaches fresh brownie consistency.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp Ground Flaxseed or Chia Seeds
1-2 tbsp Water or Almond Milk (if needed)

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: In a medium bowl, combine almond butter, protein powder, almond flour, cocoa powder, maple syrup, and sea salt.
Hydrate: Mix with a spatula until a thick dough forms. If it is too crumbly to hold a shape, add 1 tbsp of water or milk. If it's still too dry, add another tbsp.
Texture: Fold in the flaxseed (or chia) and the mini chocolate chips.
Roll: Scoop out 1-tbsp portions and roll between your palms into balls.
Set: Place on a plate and chill in the refrigerator for at least 20 minutes before eating.
Store: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a week.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, snack, quick-lunch, meal-prep, no-cook, assemble

recipes.name: Cooked-Chicken Taco Bar
recipes.description: A measured six-person taco setup using already cooked chicken, warm tortillas, cabbage and fresh toppings, with a cooked-pork variation.
recipeIngredient: 600 g fully cooked chicken, bones and skin removed, shredded into bite-size pieces
1/4 cup (60 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, plus up to 1/4 cup (60 ml) only if needed
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste
1/2 tsp fine salt, only if needed
18 small soft corn or flour tortillas, about 5–6 inches across, total across both types
2 avocados, about 300 g edible flesh, sliced just before serving
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the avocado
1/2 cup (120 g) Mexican crema or sour cream
60 g cotija or queso fresco, crumbled, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the cold components first: Shred cabbage, slice radishes, dice onion and chop cilantro. Portion crema, salsa, optional cheese and hot sauce. Slice the optional jalapeño and cut the serving lime. Keep perishables chilled until the bar is ready; leave the avocado whole for now.

Start the filling: Heat oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Stir cumin for 15–20 seconds, then immediately add the initial measured broth and cooked chicken. Toss, cover and heat gently, stirring every couple of minutes. Add extra broth a tablespoon at a time only if the pan is drying.

Verify and season: After roughly 6–10 minutes, check several portions with a thermometer; continue until the reheated chicken reaches 165°F / 74°C throughout. Remove the lid briefly if liquid pools. Taste before adding any measured lime or salt, since cooked chicken and broth may already be seasoned. Cover off heat for the brief tortilla warming period.

Warm tortillas and finish avocado: Warm tortillas in a dry skillet over medium-high, about 10–30 seconds per side until hot and flexible, wrapping each batch in a clean towel. Alternatively, microwave stacks of four to six between damp paper towels for 30–45 seconds, adding short bursts if needed. Slice avocado and gently toss with its separately measured lime juice. This helps limit browning but does not preserve it indefinitely.

Set the bar and serve promptly: Set out hot filling, warm tortillas and the chilled toppings. Offer three small tacos per person, about 33 g cooked chicken per tortilla before toppings. A thin layer of cabbage and a small spoonful of sauce are enough to start. Taste a bite before adding lime or hot sauce.

Manage any longer serving period: Replenish small dishes rather than leaving all the food out at once. For an extended buffet, keep cooked meat at 140°F / 60°C or above and cold toppings at 40°F / 4°C or below. Refrigerate unheld perishables within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

recipes.keywords: Mexican-inspired, savory, spicy, fresh, acidic, weeknight, entertaining, family-meal, kid-friendly, saute, no-cook

recipes.name: Buttered Egg Noodles
recipes.description: Buttered egg noodles are the ultimate comfort base -- the kind of thing your grandmother made without a recipe. Wide egg noodles have a tender, slightly chewy texture that cradles butter and sauce better than any Italian pasta.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp Kosher Salt (plus more for pasta water)

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a rolling boil. The water should taste like the sea. Add egg noodles and cook according to package directions until al dente, usually 7-8 minutes.
Reserve Water: Before draining, scoop out 1/4 cup of the starchy pasta water and set aside.

Drain and Toss: Drain the noodles and return them to the pot over low heat. Add butter in pieces, reserved pasta water, salt, and pepper. Toss vigorously for 30-60 seconds until the butter melts and emulsifies with the starchy water into a glossy coating on every noodle.
Serve: Transfer to a warm serving bowl, scatter with parsley if using, and serve immediately alongside braises, stews, or saucy mains.

recipes.keywords: American, Eastern European, rich, savory, buttery, mild, weeknight, comfort-food, boil, saute

recipes.name: Buttermilk Cornflake Baked Chicken
recipes.description: Bone-in chicken in a tangy buttermilk marinade, baked with a cornflake, Parmesan and thyme coating. Allow at least three hours for marinating.
recipeIngredient: 3 lbs (1360 g) bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces: 2 breast halves, 2 thighs, 2 drumsticks and 2 wings; back excluded
75 g peeled yellow onion, thinly sliced
12 g fine salt, for the marinade
150 g plain cornflakes, weighed before crushing into small crumbs

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate ahead: Whisk buttermilk, hot sauce, lemon juice and the twelve grams salt in a food-safe container; add onion, smashed garlic and thyme sprigs. Add the chicken without rinsing it. Use a snug covered container or a food-safe resealable bag set in a dish to keep the marinade against the pieces. Refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below for three to twelve hours, turning the closed bag or pieces once if needed for coverage. Wash hands and clean raw-contact surfaces.

Set up the oven: Near the end of the soak, heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C with a shelf in the center. Line an 18-by-13-inch rimmed sheet pan with foil and place an oven-safe rack on top. Brush the rack with one teaspoon of the measured oil. Check the usable rack area before coating; have a second pan and oven-safe rack ready if all pieces cannot fit with the stated gaps. If using two pans, place shelves in the upper and lower thirds and plan to swap their positions halfway through baking.

Prepare the crumbs: Crush the weighed cornflakes in a bag with a rolling pin until mostly small crumbs, with some texture remaining. Mix in the remaining five teaspoons oil, rubbing lightly to distribute it, then add Parmesan, chopped thyme and pepper. Put half in a shallow dish and keep the other half in a clean bowl to add as needed. The marinade, cereal and cheese supply salt; do not automatically salt the coating as well.

Coat and arrange: Lift chicken from the marinade and remove clinging onion, garlic and thyme stems. Let excess buttermilk drip away, leaving a thin film. Press each piece into the crumb mixture on all sides, adding reserved crumbs to the dish as needed. Press on one thin, even coat and leave excess crumbs in the dish; do not heap them on just to use them up. Place skin-side up on the rack with roughly an inch between pieces. Use a second pan if they would touch. Discard remaining raw-contact marinade, aromatics and crumbs; wash hands and utensils before handling side dishes or cooked food.

Bake and check each piece: Bake without turning the chicken. After thirty minutes, check the breasts, wings and legs individually with a thermometer in the thickest meat, avoiding bone; check more than one spot in large breast halves. Continue baking and recheck as needed until every piece reaches at least 165°F / 74°C, commonly thirty-five to fifty-five minutes total. Remove finished pieces to a clean rack over a plate while the others continue. Thighs and drumsticks can stay longer if you prefer softer dark meat, but do not keep finished breasts in the oven for them. If the crust darkens too quickly, loosely shield that piece with foil. With two pans, swap their shelf positions and rotate front to back around halfway, allowing additional time if needed.

Rest and portion: Let the final pieces rest for five minutes, uncovered so steam can escape. Divide the meat among four diners, sharing breast meat and distributing thighs, drumsticks and wings by appetite; two pieces are not automatically equal portions. Serve the chicken beside the vegetables and mash rather than burying its crust under them. Mixed pieces may finish twenty minutes or more apart; a clean uncovered rack protects the crust but does not keep them hot indefinitely. Have the sides ready near the chicken finish. For closer finish times, use similarly sized bone-in thighs as described in the substitution.

recipes.keywords: Southern, American, tangy, savory, herbaceous, comfort-food, family-meal, entertaining, bake

recipes.name: Buttermilk Waffles
recipes.description: Buttermilk's acidity reacts with baking soda for extra lift and tang. Rest the batter for 10-15 minutes before cooking so flour fully absorbs the liquid - this produces waffles that are crispy outside and airy inside.

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Wet Mix: In a separate bowl, whisk the buttermilk and melted butter. Whisk in the eggs until just combined.
Combine: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry. Whisk until just combined - a few small lumps are essential for a light texture. Fold in the vanilla.
The Rest: Let the batter rest at room temperature for 10-15 minutes. It should become slightly bubbly.
Cook: Preheat your waffle iron and grease lightly. Pour about 1/3 to 1/2 cup of batter (depending on your iron size).
Finish: Cook until the steam stops rising from the iron and the waffles are deep golden brown.
Serve: Serve immediately with salted butter, maple syrup, and fresh berries.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, steam

recipes.name: Butternut Squash Fettuccine Alfredo
recipes.description: This modern variation on Roman fettuccine Alfredo adds roasted butternut squash to the traditional butter-and-Parmesan sauce. Roasting the squash at 425°F until deeply caramelized concentrates its natural sugars and prevents a watery sauce - boiling produces inferior results.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Low-sodium Chicken Broth (or Veggie Broth)

recipeInstructions.text: Roast: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss squash cubes and garlic with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 25-30 minutes cook until caramelized and golden brown and caramelized.
The Emulsion: Let squash cool for 10 minutes. Transfer to a blender. Add heavy cream, broth, Parmesan, and nutmeg. Blend on high until completely smooth and velvety.
Pasta: Boil fettuccine in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Combine: Return pasta to the pot. Pour the butternut sauce over the noodles and toss vigorously.
Adjust: If the sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water one tablespoon at a time until it reaches a glossy, coating consistency.
Serve: Garnish with fresh parsley and extra Parmesan.

recipes.keywords: Italian, sweet, umami, rich, herbaceous, comfort-food, bake, roast, boil, blend

recipes.name: Cantonese Steamed Fish
recipes.description: Cantonese steamed fish is a classic from Guangdong province, prized for its delicate simplicity. The fish is steamed with ginger to infuse flavor, then the real magic happens: smoking-hot oil is poured over raw scallions and cilantro on top of the fish.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Whole Fish or Fillet (Tilapia, Flounder, or Sole)
3 Green Onions, thinly sliced (white and green separated)

recipeInstructions.text: Steam: Place the fish on a heat-proof plate. Scatter half the ginger on top. Steam over boiling water for 8-10 minutes until the fish flakes easily.
Drain: Carefully pour off any excess liquid from the plate (this liquid can be "fishy").
Layer: Arrange the remaining ginger, scallion greens, and cilantro in a pile on top of the cooked fish.
The Sauce: Whisk the soy sauce and sugar. Pour it around the base of the fish.
The Sizzle: In a small saucepan, heat the oil until it is literally smoking.
Finish: Carefully pour the hot oil directly over the herbs and ginger. It should sizzle loudly. Serve immediately.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, sweet, savory, umami, herbaceous, weeknight, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, entertaining, boil, steam

recipes.name: Cantonese Shrimp and Pork Wontons
recipes.description: Cantonese wontons from Guangdong province have been made for centuries, traditionally served in clear broth. The key to the bouncy texture is stirring the meat mixture vigorously in one direction until it becomes sticky and emulsified - this develops the protein structure.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Ground Pork (20% fat is ideal)
1/2 lb Shrimp, peeled and deveined (half finely chopped, half kept in chunks)
1/2 cup Water Chestnuts, finely minced (See Chef’s Note for substitution)

recipeInstructions.text: The Paste: In a large bowl, combine the pork, the finely chopped half of the shrimp, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, sugar, white pepper, salt, and egg.
The Texture: Stir the mixture vigorously in one direction for 3-5 minutes until it becomes pale, sticky, and forms a cohesive paste. Do not skip this!
Add Texture: Fold in the water chestnuts (or celery), green onions, and the remaining shrimp chunks.
The Test: Fry a small "tab" of the filling in a skillet. Taste for seasoning and adjust salt if needed.
Assemble: Place 1 tsp of filling in a wrapper. Moisten edges, fold into a triangle, and bring the two side corners together to form a "nurse's cap." Press out all air.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, sweet, savory, umami, weekend-project, entertaining, fry, no-cook

recipes.name: Shumai
recipes.description: Shumai (also spelled siu mai) are open-topped Cantonese dumplings, a dim sum staple from Guangdong province. The distinctive bouncy texture comes from stirring the pork and shrimp mixture vigorously in one direction for several minutes until it becomes sticky - this develops the protein and gives it that characteristic snap.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 lb Shrimp, peeled and deveined (finely chopped)
2/3 cup Dried Shiitake Mushrooms, soaked and minced
1/4 cup Finely diced carrots or Goji berries

recipeInstructions.text: The Paste: In a large bowl, combine pork, chopped shrimp, cornstarch, wine, and seasonings. Stir vigorously in one direction until the meat is pale and very sticky.
Add Texture: Fold in the mushrooms and water chestnuts.
Shape: Place a wrapper in your palm. Scoop 1.5 tbsp of filling. Squeeze the wrapper around the meat to form a "cup" with the meat exposed at the top. Flatten the base so it stands up.
Garnish: Press a tiny amount of diced carrot into the center of each top.
Steam: Place in a bamboo steamer lined with parchment. Steam over boiling water for 8-10 minutes until the internal temp is 165°F.
Serve: Serve immediately with hot chili oil.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, spicy, sweet, savory, umami, weekend-project, entertaining, boil, steam

recipes.name: Cantonese Wonton Broth
recipes.description: Authentic Cantonese wonton broth from Hong Kong should have a subtle seafood note to complement the shrimp in the wontons. Dried shrimp steeped with ginger creates this delicate oceanic flavor.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Dried Shrimp (The traditional source of 'ocean' umami)
2 stalks Green Onion, cut into 3-inch lengths
1 tsp Fish Sauce (Fallback if dried shrimp is unavailable)
Salt and white pepper to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Infuse: In a large pot, combine the chicken broth, smashed ginger, green onion pieces, and dried shrimp.
Simmer: Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Strain: Pour the broth through a fine-mesh strainer to remove the solids. The liquid should be perfectly clear.
Season: Stir in the light soy sauce and fish sauce. Add salt and a pinch of white pepper to taste.
Serve: Keep hot while you boil the wontons in a separate pot of plain water. This ensures your broth stays clear and doesn't get thickened by the starch on the wonton skins.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, savory, umami, comfort-food, weeknight, quick-lunch, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Caramelized Black Pepper Chicken
recipes.description: Peppery chicken thighs in a concentrated brown-sugar and fish-sauce glaze. Learn when to stop reducing a sauce and how to balance it with the rest of the meal.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/2 cup (100 g) packed dark brown sugar
1/4 cup (60 ml) water, plus more as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Pat chicken dry. Mix brown sugar, fish sauce, water, vinegar, ginger, garlic, pepper, and optional chiles in a bowl. Set a separate clean plate aside for the finished chicken.

Brown in batches: Heat half the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the chicken in a single layer and cook about 2–3 minutes per side, until golden in patches. Transfer to a temporary plate. Repeat with the remaining oil and chicken. The chicken is not fully cooked yet; keep its plate and juices away from ready-to-eat food.

Soften the shallot: Reduce heat to medium. Add shallot to the skillet and cook about 3 minutes, stirring, until softened. Add a tablespoon of water if the pan is dry or the browned residue is darkening too quickly.

Start the glaze: Stir in the prepared sauce, scraping up golden residue. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 2–4 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the sauce begins to coat a spoon. Lower the heat if it thickens rapidly.

Finish the chicken: Return chicken and any accumulated juices to the sauce. Simmer gently, turning the pieces, for about 3–6 minutes, until several larger pieces measure 165°F / 74°C at the center. Add water as needed to keep the sauce fluid while the chicken finishes.

Serve: Taste the sauce with a bite of plain rice if serving it. Loosen with water if too concentrated. Fold in cilantro and serve the chicken and a restrained spoonful of glaze with rice and vegetables.

recipes.keywords: Vietnamese, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, weeknight, quick-lunch, sear, simmer

citation.name: Adapted from Charles Phan’s caramelized black pepper chicken, demonstrated with Food52

recipes.name: Carnitas Bowl
recipes.description: True carnitas from Michoacán are braised low and slow, then crisped to create edges that shatter against tender, pull-apart meat. This technique packs pork tightly in a dish so it braises in its own rendered fat - no vat of lard required.
recipeIngredient: 3 lbs Pork Shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
2 ears Corn, charred and cut off cob

recipeInstructions.text: Season: Salt the pork chunks generously. Let sit 30 minutes (or overnight in fridge).
Arrange: Preheat oven to 275°F. Pack pork tightly in a 9x13 baking dish. Squeeze orange quarters over meat and nestle them in. Add onion, garlic, bay leaves, and cinnamon. Drizzle oil over top.
Braise: Cover tightly with foil. Bake 3-3.5 hours until fork-tender.
Strain: Remove aromatics and discard. Drain pork, reserving liquid. Skim fat from liquid and add it back to the meat.
Shred: Pull pork into large chunks with two forks. Season with salt.
Crisp: Spread on a sheet pan. Broil 6 minutes until edges crisp. Stir. Broil 6 more minutes.
Elote Sauce: Mix mayo, sour cream, half the cotija, and chile powder.
Assemble: Rice in bowls. Top with carnitas, black beans, charred corn dressed with elote sauce, pickled onions, cabbage, avocado, pepitas, remaining cotija, cilantro, and lime.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, savory, acidic, smoky, rich, entertaining, meal-prep, weekend-project, braise, roast

recipes.name: Cauliflower Alfredo
recipes.description: Cauliflower replaces some of the cream in traditional alfredo, cutting richness while adding body - the natural starches thicken the sauce. It's a smart weeknight shortcut that tastes more like creamy comfort than a vegetable swap.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Milk of choice (or Chicken Broth for dairy-free)
1/2 cup Parmesan Cheese or Nutritional Yeast

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: In a pot, combine cauliflower and milk/broth. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes until very soft.
Infuse: In a small pan, sauté the garlic in the chosen butter or olive oil for 1 minute until fragrant.
Blend: Transfer the hot cauliflower and its cooking liquid to a blender. Add the garlic and its cooking fat, the chosen Parmesan or nutritional yeast, salt, and nutmeg.
Emulsify: Blend on high for 1 minute until completely smooth and velvety.
Serve: Toss immediately with your favorite pasta or use as a base for roasted veg.

recipes.keywords: Italian, umami, rich, weeknight, quick-lunch, snack, saute, simmer, boil, blend

recipes.name: Cauliflower Rice
recipes.description: Cauliflower rice is a clever low-carb swap, but it needs proper technique to avoid the two common failures: mushy texture and raw cauliflower taste. The solution is high heat and short cooking time - you want to evaporate moisture quickly while keeping some bite.
recipeIngredient: 1 large head Cauliflower (about 2 lbs), cut into florets
2 tbsp Olive Oil or Avocado Oil
2 tbsp Fresh Herbs such as parsley, cilantro, or chives (optional)

recipeInstructions.text: The Rice: Working in batches, pulse cauliflower florets in a food processor until they resemble rice grains. Don't over-process - you want texture, not mush.
The Sauté: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add cauliflower rice in an even layer (work in batches to avoid crowding). Cook undisturbed for 2 minutes, then stir.
The Season: Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, for 3-4 more minutes until lightly golden and tender-crisp. Add garlic in the last 30-45 seconds if using, until fragrant.
The Finish: Remove from heat, season with salt and pepper, and toss with fresh herbs if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, mild, weeknight, meal-prep, light-and-fresh, saute, raw

recipes.name: Chana Begoon
recipes.description: This Indian chickpea and eggplant curry keeps the eggplant from turning mushy by roasting it separately at 425°F until browned and tender, then folding it into the gravy at the end. Chinese eggplant works especially well because it's less watery than globe eggplant.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Chinese Eggplant, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 cans (15 oz) Chickpeas, rinsed and drained
Neutral Oil, as needed for roasting and sautéing
Water, as needed to loosen the gravy

recipeInstructions.text: Roast Eggplant: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss eggplant cubes with enough oil to lightly coat their surfaces and salt to taste. Roast on a sheet pan for 15-20 minutes until golden and tender. Set aside.

The Gravy: In a large skillet over medium heat, heat enough oil to coat the bottom in a thin film. Add the onion and sauté until deep golden brown (10 mins). Add ginger and garlic; sauté for 2 minutes.

Bloom: Add all dry spices and sauté in the oil for 1 minute to bloom. Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until the tomatoes thicken into a gravy; add a splash of water if the spices begin to catch.
Chickpeas: Stir in the chickpeas and a splash of water. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Fold: Gently fold the roasted eggplant into the gravy. Let it sit for 2 minutes to absorb the spices (do not over-stir).
Finish: Stir in cilantro and lemon juice a little at a time, tasting between additions. Adjust salt before serving.

recipes.keywords: Indian, spicy, acidic, comfort-food, meal-prep, bake, roast, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Chana Masala
recipes.description: Tender chickpeas in a concentrated onion-and-tomato masala, with whole cumin, coriander, green chile and the fruity tang of dried mango.
recipeIngredient: 2 (15 oz) cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed; about 250 g drained chickpeas per can
250 g yellow onion, peeled and finely diced
1 tbsp finely grated fresh ginger, peeled
2 green serrano chiles, slit lengthwise but left attached at the stem
1 (14 oz / 400 g) can crushed tomatoes, with all their juice
2 tsp garam masala, a salt-free ground spice blend, divided
1/2 tsp Kashmiri red chile powder, pure ground chile rather than a salted seasoning blend
3/4 tsp fine salt, for the chickpea simmer
1/4 tsp fine salt, reserved for finishing; use only as needed
1 cup (240 ml) water, for the chickpea simmer
1/2 cup (120 ml) hot water, reserved only if the pan or curry becomes too dry
2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro, for finishing
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually to taste
1 tbsp additional fresh lemon juice, only if replacing the amchur

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Drain and rinse the chickpeas and check that one crushes easily. Finely dice the onion, mince the garlic, grate the ginger and slit the serranos. Measure the spices and separate the garam masala into two equal portions. Keep the initial cooking water and the correction reserve separate.

Start with cumin: Heat the oil or ghee in the wide pot over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and stir for about 20–30 seconds, until sizzling and fragrant. As soon as they darken slightly, add the onion; do not wait for black seeds or smoke.

Soften and brown the onion: Cook for about 12–15 minutes, stirring regularly, until soft and evenly golden. Lower the heat if edges brown before the centers soften. If it begins sticking, use a small splash from the hot-water reserve and scrape up the golden residue. Stir in garlic, ginger and serranos for about 1 minute.

Concentrate the masala: Lower the heat. Stir in coriander, turmeric, amchur, ground red chile and half the garam masala for about 15–20 seconds. Immediately add all the crushed tomatoes and their juice. Return to medium heat and cook uncovered for 8–10 minutes, stirring frequently, until thick and aromatic. A spoon should leave a brief trail through the moist base; do not keep frying just to force out a pool of oil.

Simmer and thicken: Add chickpeas, the initial fine salt and all the measured cooking water. Bring to a gentle simmer, allowing a few minutes to heat through, then cover and cook over medium-low for 20 minutes, stirring once or twice. Uncover and mash about one-quarter of the chickpeas against the pan with the spoon. Stir them through and simmer uncovered for 3–5 minutes, until the sauce clings but still moves around the beans. Use the remaining hot-water reserve only if needed to keep it spoonable.

Balance and serve: Stir in the remaining garam masala and simmer for 1 minute, then turn off the heat. Taste before adding lemon. Add the measured lemon juice gradually; if replacing amchur, combine both listed lemon portions and use only as much as needed. Add the reserved salt after tasting a chickpea with its sauce. Remove the serranos or tell diners they are present, then fold in cilantro. Divide into portions of roughly 1 1/4 cups each, with plain basmati or warm naan.

recipes.keywords: Indian, spicy, savory, tangy, aromatic, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Char Siu (Chinese BBQ Pork)
recipes.description: Cantonese-style roast pork with a glossy sweet-savory glaze. Learn to manage sugar, meat temperature, and clean basting.
recipeIngredient: 3 lbs (1.36 kg) boneless pork shoulder, cut into strips about 2 inches thick
1 tsp beet juice, optional for color
1 cup water, for the roasting pan, plus more as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Mix and reserve: Whisk hoisin, honey, soy sauces, wine, sugar, five-spice, garlic, pepper, and optional beet juice. Before touching raw pork, place 3 tbsp in a separate covered container and refrigerate for glazing. Coat pork strips with the remaining marinade and refrigerate, covered, at least 8 hours or overnight.

Prepare the oven: Heat to 425°F / 220°C. Line a rimmed roasting pan with foil and set a rack inside. Add 1 cup water beneath the rack, without touching the meat. Set pork strips on the rack with space between them. Discard raw-contact marinade.
Start roasting: Roast 15 minutes, then turn the strips and reduce oven to 375°F / 190°C. Continue 20 minutes. Check the pan occasionally and carefully add hot water if the bottom is drying out.

Glaze and measure: Brush with the reserved clean glaze. Roast another 10–20 minutes, turning and glazing once more, until the thickest part of each strip reaches at least 145°F / 63°C. Times vary with thickness. Do not use raw marinade or pan drippings as an uncooked finishing sauce.

Char briefly: If the glaze needs more color, broil briefly, checking every 30 seconds and turning as needed, usually 1–3 minutes total. Skip this if the glaze is already dark. Avoid blackening the entire surface.
Rest and slice: Rest for 10 minutes before slicing; whole pork cuts require at least a 3-minute rest after reaching 145°F / 63°C. Slice thinly across the grain and serve with rice and greens.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, sweet, savory, umami, weekend-project, meal-prep, roast, boil, broil

recipes.name: Charred Asparagus with Parmesan
recipes.description: The broiler is the most underused tool for vegetables. It delivers restaurant-quality char in a fraction of the time that roasting takes, and asparagus is the ideal candidate because the spears lie flat and cook in minutes.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Asparagus, woody ends snapped off
2 cloves Garlic, finely grated on a Microplane

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat: Set oven broiler to high. Position an oven rack 4-6 inches from the heating element. Line a baking sheet with foil.

Prep: Snap the woody ends off each asparagus spear by bending from the bottom -- they break naturally at the right point. Choose medium-thick spears; pencil-thin ones burn too quickly under a broiler.
Season: Toss asparagus on the sheet with olive oil, grated garlic, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer.

Broil: Place under the broiler for 4-6 minutes, shaking the pan once halfway through. Watch carefully -- the tips should be charred and blistered, and the stems should be tender-crisp with bright green color.

Finish: Remove from oven. Immediately shower with grated Parmesan (it will melt slightly from the residual heat), lemon zest, lemon juice, and flaky sea salt. Serve within minutes -- asparagus does not wait well.

recipes.keywords: Italian, Mediterranean, savory, umami, herbaceous, weeknight, entertaining, light-and-fresh, broil

recipes.name: Charred Broccoli with Garlic
recipes.description: Skillet-browned broccoli with a tender stem, gently warmed garlic, and a little soy and lemon at the finish.
recipeIngredient: 450 g broccoli florets, with any thick attached stems sliced about 1/4 inch thick
1/4 cup (60 ml) water, divided, plus a small splash if needed
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Wash and dry broccoli thoroughly. Cut florets about 1 1/2–2 inches wide and slice thick attached stems about 1/4 inch thick. Divide into two batches. Slice garlic and measure water and seasonings.

Brown the first batch: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 12-inch lidded skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add half the broccoli in a loose layer with cut faces against the pan where possible. Leave about 2 minutes, then turn and cook another 1–2 minutes until several surfaces brown.

Tenderize and dry: Lower heat to medium, carefully add 2 tbsp water and cover for about 1–2 minutes. Check a thick stem with a knife; it should yield with a little resistance. Add a small splash of water and cover a little longer only if still hard. Uncover and let residual water evaporate, then transfer broccoli to a bowl.
Repeat: Cook the remaining broccoli with the other tablespoon oil and the remaining 2 tbsp measured water, following steps 2–3. Transfer to the bowl.

Finish gently: Lower heat to medium-low. Stir garlic and optional pepper flakes in the oil film remaining in the skillet for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant and pale gold. Return all broccoli, add soy sauce, and fold briefly to warm and coat. Turn off heat and add half the lemon juice. Taste, adding the rest only if wanted. Divide into four side portions and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: International, savory, toasted, acidic, weeknight, light-and-fresh, saute, steam

recipes.name: Charred Guacamole with Pomegranate
recipes.description: Broiling the jalapeños and tomatoes transforms familiar guacamole into something with smoky depth and caramelized sweetness. The charred vegetables add complexity that raw versions can't match - their sugars concentrate and their skins develop bitter-sweet char.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp Cumin Seeds, toasted and ground (or 1 tsp ground cumin, toasted in dry pan)

recipeInstructions.text: The Toast: If using whole cumin seeds, toast in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds until fragrant. Grind in a mortar or spice grinder. (If using ground cumin, toast it in a dry pan for 20 seconds.)

The Char: Position oven rack 6 inches from broiler. Place jalapeño and tomato halves cut-side down on a foil-lined sheet pan. Broil for 5-7 minutes until skins are blistered and blackened in spots. Let cool slightly. Peel off and discard the blackened tomato skins (they can be bitter). Chop the flesh and jalapeños finely.
The Mash: Scoop avocado flesh into a large bowl. Add lime juice and zest immediately and toss to coat. Add olive oil. Mash with a fork to desired consistency - slightly chunky is ideal for texture.
The Fold: Add the chopped charred vegetables, red onion, garlic, cilantro, toasted cumin, and salt. Fold gently until just combined. Taste and adjust salt and lime.
The Finish: Transfer to serving bowl. Drizzle with a little more olive oil. Scatter pomegranate seeds over top. Finish with a pinch of flaky salt.
Serve: Serve immediately with quality tortilla chips. If making ahead, press plastic wrap directly onto the surface and refrigerate up to 2 hours.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, spicy, smoky, acidic, entertaining, game-day, no-cook, broil

recipes.name: Cheese Fondue
recipes.description: Cheese fondue is a fragile Emulsion. If the heat is too high, the cheese will "break" into a stringy ball and a pool of oil.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Dry White Wine (Sauvignon Blanc or Riesling)

recipeInstructions.text: Rub: Rub the inside of a heavy pot (ceramic or cast iron) with the garlic halves. Discard the garlic.
Coat: In a bowl, toss the shredded cheeses with the cornstarch until evenly coated.
Simmer: Add the wine and lemon juice to the pot. Bring to a very gentle simmer over medium-low heat.
Whisk: Add one handful of cheese. Whisk constantly in a Figure-8 motion until melted. Repeat until all cheese is incorporated and the sauce is smooth.
Finish: Stir in the Kirsch, nutmeg, and dry mustard.
Serve: Keep warm over a low flame. Serve with crusty bread, green apples, and blanched broccoli.

recipes.keywords: Swiss, acidic, entertaining, weekend-project, simmer

recipes.name: Chef Kriger’s Recipe Shabbat Brisket
recipes.description: Shabbat brisket is the Friday ritual that defines Jewish home cooking - it goes into the oven before sundown and emerges fall-apart tender hours later. The slow braise at low temperature (275-300°F) breaks down collagen without drying the meat.

recipeInstructions.text: Season: Season the brisket generously with salt and pepper on both sides. Place fat-side up in a heavy foil pan or Dutch oven.
Vegetables: Scatter the onions and carrots over and around the meat.
Sauce: In a bowl, whisk all sauce ingredients together. Pour over the entire brisket, ensuring it is fully covered. Add 1 cup of water around the edges.
Bake: Cover tightly with foil. Bake at 350°F for 1.5 to 2 hours until tender.
The Chill: Remove from oven. Let cool, then refrigerate the entire pan overnight.
Slice: Remove the cold meat from the sauce. Slice very thin against the grain.
Finish: Return the slices to the sauce. Re-bake, covered, at 325°F for 30-45 minutes until hot and the sauce is bubbling.

recipes.keywords: Jewish, sweet, savory, holiday, bake, braise

recipes.name: Chewy Chocolate Meringues
recipes.description: The secret to a meringue that is "Chewy" rather than just "Crispy" is the Sugar Dissolution. By gently heating the egg whites and sugar before whipping, you ensure the sugar crystals are fully dissolved into the protein structure.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Egg Whites, room temperature (about 6-7 large eggs)

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 250°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

Dissolve: In a heat-proof bowl set over a pot of simmering water (double boiler), combine egg whites, sugar, and salt. Whisk gently until the sugar is dissolved and the mixture feels smooth (not gritty) between your fingers.
Whip: Transfer to a stand mixer. Add cream of tartar. Whip on high speed for 8-10 minutes until the whites are stiff, glossy, and the bowl feels cool to the touch.
Fold: Gently fold in the chocolate chips by hand.
Portion: Use a large spoon or cookie scoop to place clouds of batter onto the sheets. They will not spread, so you can place them 1 inch apart.
Bake: Bake for 45-50 minutes. The cookies are done when the outside is firm but the center still feels slightly soft.
Cool: Let cool completely on the baking sheet to allow the shell to set.

recipes.keywords: French, sweet, rich, comfort-food, bake, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Chicken & Spinach Pasta with Lemon
recipes.description: Chicken, spinach, and short pasta in a light lemon-Parmesan sauce. Use pasta water and a gentle cheese finish to make the sauce cling.
recipeIngredient: 12 oz (340 g) dried penne or rigatoni
1 lb (450 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
10 oz (280 g) baby spinach, washed and thoroughly drained
1/4 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
1/4 tsp black pepper, plus more to taste
1 1/2 tsp fine salt, for 3 quarts pasta water
1 cup (240 ml) reserved pasta water, added as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Boil the pasta: Bring 3 quarts water and the pasta-water salt to a boil. Add pasta and stir. Cook until about 1 minute short of the package's suggested time, tasting for a slightly firm center. Reserve 1 cup cooking water before draining.

Cook chicken alongside: Pat chicken dry and season with its measured salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a deep 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Cook in a single layer, turning occasionally, for about 6–9 minutes, until golden in patches and several larger pieces measure 165°F / 74°C. Work in batches if needed. Transfer to a clean plate.

Build the sauce: Reduce heat to medium and add the remaining oil. Stir in garlic for about 30 seconds, until fragrant but not brown. Add wine and scrape up golden residue. Simmer 2–4 minutes, until reduced by roughly half.
Finish the pasta: Add drained pasta and 1/3 cup reserved water to the skillet. Toss over medium-low heat for 1–2 minutes, until the pasta is just tender. Add a splash of water if it sticks.

Wilt the greens: Add spinach in two or three batches, tossing each until it begins to wilt. Return cooked chicken and its juices. Toss just until the chicken is hot and the spinach is fully wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Keep a little liquid in the pan; add reserved water only as needed.

Add cheese and lemon: Remove the skillet from heat and wait until active bubbling stops. Add Parmesan in two additions while tossing. Add the zest and the lower end of the listed lemon-juice range. Taste a complete bite, then add more juice, pepper, or a pinch of salt if needed. Loosen with water by the tablespoon and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Italian, American, acidic, umami, rich, weeknight, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, boil, sear, simmer, toss

recipes.name: Chicken and White Bean Enchiladas
recipes.description: Enchiladas Suizas (Swiss-style enchiladas) originated in Mexico City in the 1950s at Sanborns restaurant, named for their creamy, dairy-rich green tomatillo sauce. This version adds white beans to the chicken filling for extra protein and fiber.
recipeIngredient: 15 oz can Navy or Cannellini Beans, rinsed
12 oz Tomatillo Salsa or Enchilada Sauce
1/2 cup Light Sour Cream or Greek Yogurt

recipeInstructions.text: The Filling: In a bowl, toss the shredded chicken, beans, cumin, and 1/4 cup of the green sauce.
The Sauce: In a blender, combine the enchilada sauce, diced green chiles, cilantro, and sour cream. Pulse until smooth and creamy.
Assemble: Spread 1/2 cup of sauce on the bottom of a 9x13 dish. Fill each tortilla with the chicken/bean mixture, roll tightly, and place seam-side down.
Bake: Pour the remaining sauce over the top. Cover with cheese.
Crisp: Bake at 375°F for 20-25 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and the cheese is golden.
Finish: Top with fresh cilantro and quick Pickled Red Onions.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, rich, comfort-food, meal-prep, bake, poach, no-cook, blend

recipes.name: Chicken and Wild Rice Soup
recipes.description: A brothy chicken soup with nutty wild rice, tender vegetables, and fresh herbs. Cook the grain separately so its timing does not dictate the chicken’s texture.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup (160 g) uncooked wild rice; check the package for processing and cook time
4 cups (960 ml) water, for cooking rice, plus more as needed
8 cups (1.9 liters) low-sodium chicken broth, plus up to 2 cups to adjust consistency
2 lbs (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/4 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the grain: Rinse the wild rice. Combine with the measured rice-cooking water in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook according to the package range, checking early for quick-cook grain. Add hot water if the pan dries before the rice is tender. When many grains open and have a tender, chewy center, drain any excess water.

Soften vegetables: While the rice simmers, heat oil in a 6-quart pot over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery. Cook 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the onion is softened. Add garlic and cook about 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Build the broth: Add the initial measured chicken broth, thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook about 8–10 minutes, until carrots are approaching tenderness; they will cook further with the chicken.

Poach the chicken: Add chicken and return gently to a simmer. Cook about 12–18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until several larger pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and the vegetables are tender. Avoid a rolling boil.

Combine: Stir in the tender, drained rice and heat through. Add extra broth as needed to keep the soup spoonable and brothy. If the rice is not yet ready, keep the soup gently hot while it finishes; do not keep boiling the chicken.

Finish: Add parsley and the lower end of the listed lemon-juice range. Taste the broth with some chicken and rice, then add more lemon, salt, or pepper as needed. Ladle into eight bowls. For planned leftovers, keep the remaining rice and soup separate before chilling promptly.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, rich, herbaceous, comfort-food, saute, simmer, poach

recipes.name: Chicken, Apple, and Butternut Stew
recipes.description: Chicken thighs simmered with squash, parsnip, cider, and sage, with tart apple added late. Learn to stagger ingredients so each finishes at the right texture.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/2 tsp fine salt, divided, plus more to taste
1 cup (130 g) parsnip, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1 1/2 cups (360 ml) unsweetened apple cider (cloudy apple juice, not vinegar or hard cider)
1 1/2 cups (360 ml) low-sodium chicken stock, plus more as needed
3 cups (420 g) butternut squash, peeled, seeded, and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
2 cups (250 g) Granny Smith apple, cored and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
1–2 tsp apple cider vinegar, optional, to finish

recipeInstructions.text: Brown chicken in batches: Pat chicken dry and season with half the salt and the pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown half the chicken for about 3 minutes per side, then transfer to a temporary plate. Repeat with remaining oil and chicken. It need not be cooked through yet.

Soften the base: Reduce heat to medium. Add onion, parsnip, and remaining salt. Cook about 7–9 minutes, stirring, until onion is softened and lightly golden. Add a small splash of stock if the browned residue threatens to scorch. Add sage and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Disperse the flour: Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute. Gradually stir in cider, scraping up golden residue and smoothing out flour pockets. Add stock and bring to a simmer.

Simmer chicken and squash: Return chicken and its accumulated juices. Add squash. Keep at a gentle simmer, partially covered, for about 18–25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Continue until squash and parsnip are tender and several larger chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Add stock if the sauce becomes too thick before the vegetables soften.
Add apple late: Fold in the apple and simmer 5–8 minutes, until hot and just tender but still holding its shape. Stir gently so the squash stays intact.

Balance and serve: Taste a spoonful containing sauce and vegetables. Add optional cider vinegar 1 tsp at a time if the stew needs more tartness, and adjust salt or pepper. Serve in six bowls with a green vegetable or salad.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, holiday, comfort-food, sear, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Hyderabadi-style Chicken Biryani
recipes.description: Marinated chicken and partially cooked basmati finish together in a covered pot. Learn to coordinate rice hydration, gentle heat, and a verified chicken endpoint.
recipeIngredient: 2.5 lbs (1.13 kg) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into pieces about 2 inches across and no more than 1 inch thick
2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste (or 1 tbsp each finely grated ginger and garlic)
1 1/2 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
1/2 cup loosely packed chopped cilantro, divided
1/2 cup loosely packed chopped mint, divided
2 1/2 cups (500 g) aged basmati rice, not parboiled or quick-cooking
10 cups (2.4 liters) water, for boiling the rice
1 tbsp fine salt, for the rice water
3 large yellow onions (about 600 g trimmed total), sliced evenly about 1/8 inch thick
1 cup (240 ml) neutral oil, for frying onions
2 tbsp of the drained onion frying oil, reserved for layering
1 tsp food-grade rose water or kewra water, optional (not concentrated essence or essential oil)
1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, only if needed during cooking

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate 4–24 hours: Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chile powder, turmeric, garam masala, ground cumin, ground coriander, the chicken salt, lemon juice, half the cilantro, and half the mint. Coat the chicken, cover, and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below. Do not leave raw chicken out while preparing the other components.

Fry onions: Heat the neutral oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Fry onions in two batches, stirring frequently, until evenly golden brown, about 12–18 minutes per batch. Lower heat as they color; lift them out before dark brown. Drain in a metal strainer over a heatproof bowl, then spread on a tray lined with paper towels. Reserve 2 tbsp drained onion oil for the biryani; the remaining frying oil is not poured into the dish.

Prepare rice and saffron: While the onions cook, rinse basmati in several changes of cool water, soak for 20–30 minutes, and drain. Steep saffron in the warm milk for at least 15 minutes. Bring the measured rice water to a boil in a large pot with its salt, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaves, and cumin seeds.

Partially cook rice: Add the drained soaked rice to the boiling water. Stir once gently and return to a boil. Begin tasting at 3 minutes; drain when the outside is soft but the center is distinctly firm, often about 4–6 minutes depending on the rice. Do not wait until fully tender. Retain the whole spices with the rice, or remove large whole spices now if preferred.

Layer promptly: Spread the reserved 2 tbsp onion oil over the bottom of the heavy cooking pot. Take chicken from the refrigerator and spread it with all its marinade in an even layer. Scatter one-third of the fried onions over it. Spread the hot, drained rice on top without packing it down. Drizzle with saffron milk, melted ghee, and optional rose or kewra water. Scatter the remaining onions, cilantro, and mint over the top. Cover tightly; use a sheet of foil under the lid if needed for a snug fit.

Cook under steam: Heat over medium until you hear a gentle simmer and see light steam at the lid edge, about 5–8 minutes. Reduce heat enough to maintain that gentle simmer, rather than automatically using the lowest burner setting. Cook covered for 30 minutes, lowering heat if you smell scorching. Keep the lid closed between checks to retain steam.

Verify before resting: Open carefully away from your face. Probe several of the largest chicken pieces at the center and near the pot edge, avoiding the pot itself; each must reach 165°F / 74°C. Check the rice temperature in several places also reaches 165°F / 74°C, and taste a grain for tenderness without a chalky core. If either temperature or texture is short, re-cover and cook another 5–10 minutes before checking again. If rice is drying, sprinkle 2 tbsp hot water over it, with up to the remaining 2 tbsp as needed. Do not use resting time as a substitute for these endpoints.

Rest and serve: Once chicken and rice meet the checks, turn off heat and rest covered for 15 minutes. Lift portions from the bottom with a wide spoon so each serving includes chicken and rice, disturbing the grains as little as possible. Remove any visible whole spices and tell diners that some may remain. Serve with raita or kachumber salad; additional rice is unnecessary.

recipes.keywords: Indian, aromatic, warm, spicy, savory, rich, weekend-project, family-meal, entertaining, make-ahead, meal-prep, marinate, boil, fry, steam

recipes.name: Chicken Chile Enchiladas
recipes.description: Traditional Mexican enchiladas briefly fry corn tortillas before dipping them in sauce to prevent them from becoming soggy during baking. Searing each tortilla in a little oil for just 5 seconds makes them pliable enough to roll without cracking while creating a protective layer that holds their structure.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Shredded Chicken (Rotisserie or Pressure Cooked)
1 can (15 oz) Red Enchilada Sauce (Hatch or homemade)
Sour Cream, Fresh Cilantro, and Sliced Jalapeños

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 375°F. In a bowl, toss shredded chicken with the green chiles and diced red pepper.
Coat: Heat a splash of oil in a small skillet. Flash-fry each tortilla for 5 seconds per side just until pliable.
Dip & Roll: Dip a warm tortilla into the red sauce. Place a large scoop of chicken in the center, sprinkle with a little cheese, and roll tightly. Place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Bake: Pour the remaining sauce over the top and cover generously with cheese.
Melt: Bake for 15-20 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and the edges of the tortillas are slightly crisp.
Serve: Top with cold sour cream and cilantro to balance the heat.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, spicy, rich, comfort-food, bake, fry, blend

recipes.name: Coq au Vin with Chicken Thighs
recipes.description: Bone-in chicken gently braised with red wine, bacon, and mushrooms, with a glossy butter finish.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs (900 g) bone-in skin-on chicken thighs
4 oz (113 g) bacon or lardons, diced
1 tbsp neutral oil, only if needed to supplement rendered fat
1/2 tsp fine salt, plus more only if needed
8 oz (225 g) fresh cremini mushrooms, halved or quartered if large
3 medium carrots (about 250 g total), cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup (240 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus a little more if needed
2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and render: Pat chicken dry and season with the measured salt and pepper. Cook bacon in a wide Dutch oven over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until it releases fat and begins to crisp. Transfer bacon to a bowl. Leave about 2 tbsp fat in the pot, adding some of the optional neutral oil if there is too little.

Brown mushrooms: Add mushrooms and cook over medium-high heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until moisture evaporates and golden surfaces develop. Transfer to a separate bowl for the end of the braise.

Brown chicken: Keep about 2 tbsp fat in the pot. Sear chicken in two batches, skin-side down for 6–8 minutes, then 2 minutes on the other side. Transfer to a plate. Adjust heat if the browned residue darkens too far. Spoon out excess rendered fat, leaving about 2 tbsp.

Cook vegetables: Lower heat to medium. Add onion and carrots and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring, until onion softens. Add garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute. Scrape away any black burned residue rather than incorporating it into the sauce.

Reduce wine: Take the pot briefly off the burner to add wine. Return to medium-high heat, scrape up golden browned residue, and simmer uncovered until the wine reduces by roughly half, about 10–15 minutes.

Braise gently: Return chicken, accumulated plate juices, and bacon. Add stock and thyme. Liquid should come about halfway to two-thirds up the thighs, not cover them; add a little stock only if needed. Bring to a simmer, cover, and lower heat to maintain gentle bubbles. Cook about 45–60 minutes, adding the reserved mushrooms for the last 10 minutes. Check meat away from the bone reaches at least 165°F / 74°C and feels tender near the joint; continue in 10-minute increments if still firm.

Concentrate and finish: Transfer tender chicken to a clean platter. Remove thyme stems and skim excess surface fat. Simmer the uncovered sauce about 5–10 minutes until it lightly coats a spoon. Turn off heat, let vigorous bubbling stop, and swirl in cold butter. Taste before adding any extra salt.
Serve: Return chicken to the warm sauce, spoon sauce over it, and finish with parsley. Serve with one starch such as mashed potatoes and a green vegetable.

recipes.keywords: French, savory, umami, rich, herbaceous, comfort-food, weekend-project, sear, braise, simmer

recipes.name: Chicken Fingers
recipes.description: Set up the breading ingredients separately so each piece of chicken gets an even coating. By using Panko and Parmesan instead of crackers, we achieve a much lighter, crispier texture that doesn't turn greasy.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Chicken Tenderloins or Breasts cut into strips
2 large eggs, beaten with the separately measured water
1 tbsp water, for beating with the eggs

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 425°F. Place a wire cooling rack on top of a large baking sheet. Spray the rack with oil.
Station: Set up three shallow bowls: - Bowl 1: Flour, salt, and pepper. - Bowl 2: Beaten eggs. - Bowl 3: Panko, Parmesan, garlic powder, and oregano.
Bread: Dip each chicken strip in flour (shake off excess), then egg, then press firmly into the panko mixture until fully coated.
Roast: Arrange on the wire rack. Spray the tops of the chicken lightly with oil.
Crisp: Bake for 12-15 minutes until golden brown and the internal temp is 165°F. (No need to flip if using a wire rack!).
Finish: Serve hot with a squeeze of lemon or your favorite dipping sauce.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, umami, kid-friendly, weeknight, comfort-food, bake, roast, fry

recipes.name: Korean-inspired Chicken Glass-Noodle Salad
recipes.description: Chewy sweet-potato noodles with savory chicken, crisp pepper, and a sesame-vinegar dressing made separately from the cooking sauce.
recipeIngredient: 10 oz (280 g) dangmyeon (Korean sweet-potato glass noodles)
2 tbsp water, plus more for loosening noodles
1 bell pepper, seeded and thinly sliced
1/2 cup loosely packed cilantro leaves, roughly chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Mix two sauces: In a large serving bowl, dissolve 1 tbsp brown sugar in the vinegar and 2 tbsp soy sauce, then whisk in the sesame oil. In a small bowl, mix the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, remaining 1 tbsp sugar, and 2 tbsp water for the chicken.

Cook the noodles: Boil dangmyeon according to its package, tasting for a chewy texture without a hard center. Drain, rinse briefly under cool running water, and drain thoroughly. Cut long strands with clean kitchen shears. Toss promptly with the dressing in the serving bowl.

Cook the chicken: Heat the neutral oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and break it into small pieces. Cook about 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until most visible moisture has evaporated and some edges are golden.

Glaze: Lower heat to medium. Add garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds. Add the small bowl of cooking sauce and simmer 2–3 minutes, stirring. Check several thick clusters of chicken reach 165°F / 74°C, keeping the thermometer tip off the pan. Continue cooking if needed. Leave a thin glaze rather than cooking the meat dry.

Toss and finish: Add the cooked chicken to the noodles. Fold in pepper, cilantro, and sesame seeds. If the noodles stick, loosen with water a tablespoon at a time. Divide among four bowls and top each with 2 tbsp prepared oi muchim if using. Serve promptly, warm or cool.

recipes.keywords: Korean, savory, sweet, acidic, herbaceous, weeknight, meal-prep, saute, boil

recipes.name: Chicken Katsu Curry
recipes.description: Crisp panko-coated chicken cutlets with a separately simmered vegetable curry sauce, served alongside rice prepared separately.
recipeIngredient: 30 g all-purpose flour, reserved only for the sauce
2 cups (480 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus a little water if needed
150 g potato, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch dice
4 boneless skinless chicken breast portions, about 6 oz (170 g) each
60 g all-purpose flour, for coating chicken
500–750 ml neutral frying oil, or enough for 1/2-inch depth in your skillet

recipeInstructions.text: Start the sauce: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and cook about 6–8 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Stir in garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Add the 30 g sauce flour and stir for 2 minutes. Lower the heat, stir in curry powder and tomato paste, and cook about 30 seconds without scorching.

Simmer vegetables: Gradually whisk in stock, then soy sauce and mirin. Add carrot and potato. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 18–22 minutes, stirring the bottom regularly, until both vegetables are tender and sauce coats a spoon. Add peas and simmer 2 minutes more. Add a small splash of water if the sauce is too thick. Cover and take off heat while frying; rewarm before serving.

Prepare cutlets: While the sauce simmers, put each chicken portion between sheets of food-safe wrap and pound with a meat mallet to an even 1/2-inch thickness. Pat dry and season with the measured salt and pepper. Keep raw chicken and its tools away from the sauce and cooked food.

Bread: Set out separate shallow dishes of the 60 g coating flour, beaten eggs, and panko. Coat each cutlet lightly in flour and shake off excess. Dip in egg, let excess drip away, then press both sides into panko. Place on a clean tray and refrigerate until the oil is ready. Discard leftover coating ingredients that touched raw chicken.

Heat oil: Set a wire rack over a rimmed tray. For holding the first batch briefly, heat the oven to 225°F / 110°C. Add oil to a deep skillet to reach about 1/2 inch, keeping the pan less than half full. Heat to about 350°F / 175°C. Use the pan depth as the guide; the required oil volume varies with its shape.

Fry in batches: Lower in two cutlets without overlapping. Fry about 3–4 minutes per side, adjusting heat to keep oil around 325–350°F / 165–175°C. Check each cutlet from the side for 165°F / 74°C in its thickest center; cook longer if needed. Transfer to the rack and hold the first batch in the low oven while the second fries. Skim loose crumbs and let the oil return to temperature between batches.

Finish and serve: Rest the last cutlets on the rack for about 3 minutes. Rewarm the sauce, adding a little water if needed. Slice chicken into strips and divide sauce among four plates, pouring it alongside rather than over the whole crust. Serve with rice prepared separately.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, savory, sweet, spicy, umami, weeknight, entertaining, saute, simmer, pan-fry

recipes.name: Chicken Lettuce Wraps
recipes.description: A moist hoisin-ginger chicken filling with crisp celery, served in cold, dry lettuce leaves. Learn to reduce a glaze without drying out the meat.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb (450 g) ground chicken or ground turkey
1/2 cup sliced scallions, whites and greens separated
2 tbsp water, plus more if needed
1 large head butter lettuce, leaves separated (about 12 usable leaves)
1/2 cup purchased ready-to-eat crispy rice noodles, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare leaves and sauce: Wash and dry the lettuce leaves and chill them. Mix hoisin, soy sauce, vinegar, and water in a small bowl. Separate scallion whites from greens.

Start the chicken: Heat neutral oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken and break into small pieces. Cook 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until released liquid mostly evaporates and some edges begin to brown.
Add crunch and aromatics: Add celery and scallion whites and cook 2 minutes. Lower heat to medium, add ginger and garlic, and stir for 30 seconds, keeping the garlic from scorching.

Glaze and check: Add the hoisin mixture. Simmer, stirring, for 2–3 minutes until it coats the filling. Check several thick clusters reach 165°F / 74°C, keeping the thermometer tip off the hot pan. Continue cooking if necessary; add a spoonful of water if the glaze becomes sticky.

Finish and serve: Turn off heat and stir in sesame oil and scallion greens. Transfer to a serving bowl and let stand briefly until no longer fiercely steaming. Spoon small portions into the lettuce at the table, adding ready-to-eat crispy noodles if desired. Keep the rest of the leaves unfilled until needed.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, American, savory, sweet, acidic, umami, weeknight, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, entertaining, fry

recipes.name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.description: Golden chicken cutlets in a mushroom and dry Marsala pan sauce, finished gently with butter.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, opened flat
1/2 cup (60 g) all-purpose flour, for dredging
8 oz (225 g) fresh cremini mushrooms, wiped clean and thickly sliced
3/4 cup (180 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus more for loosening
2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the cutlets: Open thighs flat, trim loose fat, and gently pound only the thick sections to about 1/2 inch between sheets of plastic wrap. Season with half the measured salt and the pepper. Spread flour in a shallow dish, dredge lightly, and shake off excess. Discard leftover flour after raw chicken contact.

Brown in batches: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook half the chicken about 3–4 minutes on the first side and 2–3 minutes on the second, until golden; it can finish cooking later in the sauce. Transfer to a plate. Repeat with the remaining oil and chicken. Reduce heat if the flour browns too quickly; discard any black, burned bits.

Brown mushrooms: Lower heat to medium. Add prosciutto and stir for 1 minute. Add mushrooms and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their liquid has evaporated and they begin to brown. If the pan becomes dry and sticks before the mushrooms release moisture, add a tablespoon of stock and scrape gently.

Make the sauce: Take the pan briefly off the burner to pour in the Marsala. Return to medium heat and scrape up the golden pan residue. Simmer until the wine reduces by about half, roughly 4–6 minutes. Add stock and simmer 2–3 minutes; the sauce should still be pourable.

Finish cooking the chicken: Return the chicken and its plate juices to the pan. Simmer gently for about 3–5 minutes, turning once, until the thickest parts reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue if needed, adding stock if the sauce gets too thick. Transfer the cooked chicken to a clean serving platter.

Finish with butter: Turn off heat and let vigorous bubbling subside. Swirl in the cold butter a few pieces at a time. Add parsley, taste, and use the reserved salt only if needed. Spoon sauce and mushrooms over the chicken and serve. Choose mashed potatoes or pasta, with a green vegetable alongside.

recipes.keywords: Italian, American, savory, umami, rich, weeknight, date-night, entertaining, comfort-food, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Chicken Milanese
recipes.description: Thin chicken cutlets with a crisp Parmesan-panko coating, served with freshly dressed arugula and lemon.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, for thin cutlets
1 cup (240 ml) neutral oil, approximately, for a 1/8-inch layer in the skillet
1 batch [Everyday Arugula Salad](/mise/recipes/everyday-arugula-salad), using the linked recipe’s original yield; keep undressed until serving

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare chicken and salad: Slice the breasts horizontally into four cutlets, then pound between sheets of plastic wrap to an even 1/4 inch. Season both sides with the measured salt and pepper. Prepare one four-portion batch of Everyday Arugula Salad, keeping its dressing and cheese separate from the dry leaves. Set a rack over a sheet pan. Heat the oven to 200°F / 95°C if holding the first batch briefly.
Set the coating station: Place flour in one shallow dish, eggs in a second, and panko mixed with Parmesan, oregano, and garlic powder in a third.

Coat: Dredge each cutlet lightly in flour, dip in egg and let excess drip off, then press into crumbs on both sides. Keep coated cutlets in one layer. Discard coating ingredients left after raw chicken contact and wash hands and utensils.

Heat and fry: Pour enough neutral oil into a large skillet to reach about 1/8 inch deep; the amount depends on its flat base. Heat over medium to medium-high to about 350°F / 175°C. Lower two cutlets carefully into the oil, away from you. Fry about 2–3 minutes per side, adjusting the heat so the coating turns golden without burning. Do not crowd or stack them.

Check and drain: Insert a thermometer horizontally from the side of each cutlet; the meat must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue cooking as needed. Move cooked cutlets to the rack and hold briefly in a 200°F / 95°C oven while frying the next batch. Skim burned crumbs, replenish oil if needed, and let it reheat before adding more chicken.

Serve promptly: Toss and finish the arugula salad according to its recipe. Divide among four plates with the hot cutlets and lemon wedges. Add salad on top only just before eating, or serve it alongside to preserve the crust.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, umami, herbaceous, weeknight, date-night, entertaining, pan-fry, assemble

recipes.name: Phở Gà (Chicken Pho)
recipes.description: A gently simmered chicken broth with toasted aromatics, rice noodles, and sliced chicken that is removed early to preserve its texture.
recipeIngredient: 1 chicken (about 3.5 lbs / 1.6 kg each), cut into quarters, giblets removed
2 lbs (900 g) chicken wings or backs
450 g yellow onions, halved with skin on
5 quarts (4.7 liters) water, plus more to adjust the strained broth
1/4 cup (60 ml) fish sauce, added gradually to taste
1 1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually to taste
1 lb (450 g) dried flat rice noodles (bánh phở)
200 g bean sprouts, optional, cooked thoroughly before serving
1 cup loosely packed Thai basil leaves, optional
3 tbsp hoisin sauce, optional at the table
3 tbsp sriracha, optional at the table

recipeInstructions.text: Toast aromatics: Put onion halves and ginger cut-side up on a rimmed sheet pan under the broiler, watching closely and turning as needed, for about 10–15 minutes until softened with charred patches. Cool enough to handle, remove loose blackened onion skin, and scrape off any burned debris. Toast star anise, cinnamon, and coriander in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 1 minute until fragrant.

Start broth: Put chicken quarters, wings or backs, aromatics, and spices in a 12-quart stockpot with the measured water. Bring just to a boil, skim surface foam, and reduce to a gentle simmer with only occasional bubbles. Do not wash raw chicken in the sink.

Remove serving meat when cooked: Begin checking quarters after about 30 minutes of simmering. Probe the thickest breast and thigh meat away from bone; remove each quarter only after it reaches 165°F / 74°C. Pieces may need 40 minutes or longer. Transfer to a clean tray and let stand about 10 minutes until safe to handle. Remove meat from bones, put the meat in a shallow covered container, and refrigerate promptly. Return the bones to the stockpot.
Continue the broth: Simmer bones and aromatics gently for about 2 more hours, skimming occasionally. Add a little water if needed to keep bones submerged. Avoid vigorously stirring the pot.

Strain and balance: Strain carefully through a fine-mesh sieve into another large pot and discard solids. Skim excess fat, leaving some for flavor. Aim for roughly 3.5–4 liters broth; reduce if weak or add water if overly concentrated. Stir in sugar and start with half the fish sauce and half the salt. Taste and add the remainder gradually only as needed.

Prepare noodles and toppings: Cook bánh phở according to its package until tender but not falling apart; different widths require different soaking or boiling methods. Drain and divide among six large bowls. Prepare scallion, cilantro, lime, and optional basil, chile, and cooked sprouts.

Warm meat and assemble: Slice the refrigerated chicken. Add it to simmering broth and heat through to 165°F / 74°C. Distribute meat among the noodle bowls, then ladle in about 500–600 ml broth per bowl. Finish with scallion and cilantro and offer the remaining toppings and sauces at the table. Refrigerate any unused broth promptly.

recipes.keywords: Vietnamese, aromatic, savory, herbaceous, comfort-food, broil, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Chicken Piccata
recipes.description: Thin chicken cutlets with a bright lemon-caper pan sauce. This unfloured version finishes with butter off the heat.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, for thin cutlets
1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted chicken broth, plus more if needed
2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
2 tbsp brined capers, drained and briefly rinsed
