recipes.description: Golden, lightly floured chicken cutlets with a measured temperature endpoint. Learn to balance crust development with a juicy center.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, butterflied into 4–6 cutlets about 1/2 inch thick
1/2 cup (60 g) all-purpose flour, for dredging; excess will be discarded

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Butterfly thick breasts into 4–6 cutlets about 1/2 inch thick, evening them gently if necessary. Pat dry with paper towels. Wash hands and clean surfaces after handling raw chicken.
Dredge lightly: Mix flour, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and herbs in a shallow dish. Coat each cutlet and shake off excess. Discard flour that contacted raw chicken.

Sear in batches: Heat 1.5 tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add only enough cutlets to fit without touching. Cook about 3–4 minutes until the bottom is golden; lower heat if flour specks darken rapidly.

Finish by temperature: Turn and cook about 2–4 minutes more, adjusting heat as needed. Insert a thermometer from the side into the thickest part and remove each cutlet when it reaches 165°F / 74°C. Thick pieces may take longer. Set on a clean plate. Carefully remove scorched residue, add remaining oil, and repeat with the second batch.

Rest and serve: Rest the cooked chicken for 5 minutes, loosely covered. Serve with lemon wedges. The rest is for serving quality; do not remove under-temperature chicken in the hope that resting will make it safe.

recipes.keywords: American, rich, weeknight, quick-lunch, meal-prep, sear

recipes.name: Spinach Gnocchi
recipes.description: These are properly called "gnudi" - Italian for "naked" - because they're essentially the filling of ravioli without the pasta wrapper. They originated in Tuscany, where ricotta and spinach were abundant.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/4 cups Whole-Wheat Flour (plus extra for dusting)

recipeInstructions.text: The Squeeze: Defrost spinach and squeeze in a kitchen towel until no liquid remains.
The Mix: In a food processor, pulse the dry spinach, ricotta, Parmesan, flour, egg, nutmeg, and salt until a sticky dough forms. Do not over-process.
The Shape: Transfer dough to a floured board. Sprinkle with more flour until it no longer sticks to your hands. Divide into 4 logs (1-inch thick).
Cut: Slice logs into 1-inch chunks. Toss lightly with flour.
Boil: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Drop gnocchi in. They are done when they float to the surface (3-5 mins).
Serve: Drain gently. Serve immediately with a high-quality tomato sauce or brown butter and sage.

recipes.keywords: Italian, umami, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, snack, boil, blend

recipes.name: Egg Fried Rice
recipes.description: Separate grains, tender egg, and a light savory coating. Learn how moisture and batch size shape a home stir-fry.
recipeIngredient: 3 cups (about 450 g) cooked rice, safely chilled and gently separated
3 scallions, whites and greens separated and sliced
1/2 cup frozen peas and diced carrots, thawed and drained
1.5 tbsp soy sauce, plus more to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Gently separate the cold rice with clean fingers or a fork. Beat eggs. Drain thawed vegetables. Measure soy sauce and sesame oil separately; set out garlic, scallion whites, greens, and pepper.

Cook the eggs: Heat a large wok or skillet over medium-high, then add 1 tbsp neutral oil. When shimmering, add eggs and stir until set with no liquid egg remaining. Transfer to a clean plate. Do not intentionally smoke oil or overheat empty nonstick cookware.

Fry the rice: Add remaining oil and rice. Spread briefly, then toss and gently break remaining clumps. Cook 4–6 minutes, adjusting heat to maintain a sizzle. If liquid collects or the pan is crowded, work in two batches.

Add vegetables and aromatics: Make space in the pan. Add garlic and scallion whites; stir for about 15 seconds until fragrant, then add drained vegetables. Toss for 1–2 minutes until vegetables are hot.

Season and heat through: Return eggs. Add soy sauce around the rice and toss thoroughly. Continue until the rice is steaming throughout and reaches 165°F / 74°C in several spots. Add sesame oil and white pepper. Taste before adding more soy sauce.
Finish: Fold in scallion greens and transfer to bowls. Add optional sesame seeds. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, Cantonese, savory, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, stir-fry

recipes.name: Egg in a Hole
recipes.description: Egg in a hole (also called toad in the hole, egg in a basket, or one-eyed jack) is one of the simplest and most satisfying breakfast preparations. The trick is using enough butter to get the bread golden and crispy while the egg cooks within the cutout.
recipeIngredient: 2 slices Thick-Cut Bread (sourdough, white, or whole wheat)
Optional: shredded cheese, hot sauce, everything bagel seasoning

recipeInstructions.text: Cut the Holes: Using a round cookie cutter, biscuit cutter, or the rim of a drinking glass (2.5-3 inches), press and twist to cut a circle from the center of each bread slice. Reserve the cutout rounds.
Heat the Pan: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Swirl to coat the entire surface evenly.
Toast and Fry: Place the bread slices and the cutout rounds in the skillet. Cook the bread for about 1 minute until the bottom is golden. Crack one egg into each hole. Season with salt and pepper.

Cook: Cook undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until the egg white is mostly set on the bottom and the bread is deeply golden. Flip the bread carefully with a spatula. Cook for another 30-60 seconds for a runny yolk, or 1-2 minutes for a more set yolk. Flip the cutout rounds when golden.
Serve: Transfer to plates. Serve the toasted rounds alongside for dipping into the yolk. Add shredded cheese, hot sauce, or everything bagel seasoning if desired.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, buttery, rich, weeknight, kid-friendly, quick-lunch, fry, toast

recipes.name: Pork and Cabbage Skillet (Egg Roll in a Bowl)
recipes.description: Browned ground pork with cabbage, carrot, ginger and a measured soy-sesame finish; a filling-inspired skillet meal.
recipeIngredient: 500 g green cabbage, shredded into thin ribbons
100 g carrot, cut into fine matchsticks
3 scallions, whites and greens sliced separately
2 tbsp water, plus 1 tbsp only if needed
1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, plus 1 tsp more only to taste
2 tsp chili crisp or sriracha, optional and served separately

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare everything: Shred cabbage, cut carrot into fine matchsticks, grate ginger and mince garlic. Slice scallions, keeping whites separate from greens. Mix soy sauce with 2 tbsp water. Measure the sesame oil, vinegar and garnishes.

Brown and cook the pork: Heat neutral oil in a deep 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Add pork in flattened clumps, leave about 2 minutes to color, then turn and break into crumbles. Cook another 4–5 minutes, or until several substantial clumps reach 160°F / 71°C. Spoon off excess rendered fat if it pools, leaving about 1 tbsp in the pan.
Add the aromatics: Lower to medium. Stir ginger, garlic and scallion whites into the pork for about 30 seconds, until fragrant but not scorched.

Cook the vegetables: Add carrot and half the cabbage and toss for about 1 minute. Add the remaining cabbage and soy-water mixture. Cook uncovered 3–5 minutes, stirring, until cabbage is hot and tender with a little bite. Add the extra tablespoon water only if the pan dries while vegetables are firm; if watery, let the excess evaporate briefly.

Finish and portion: Turn off heat, stir in toasted sesame oil, scallion greens and 1 tsp vinegar. Taste before the optional second teaspoon. Divide among four bowls and sprinkle with measured sesame seeds; offer chili crisp or sriracha separately. Serve promptly. If serving with Steamed White Rice, allow that recipe's full preparation and cooking time separately.

recipes.keywords: Chinese-American-inspired, spicy, savory, umami, weeknight, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, saute

recipes.name: Garlic-Ginger Eggplant
recipes.description: Tender eggplant browned in two batches, softened with a little covered steam and coated in a measured garlic-ginger sauce.
recipeIngredient: 600 g Chinese or Japanese eggplant, ends trimmed, cut into 2-inch-long batons about 1/2 inch thick
4 tbsp water, for covered cooking, divided, plus up to 2 tbsp more if needed
120 ml [Garlic-Ginger Stir-Fry Sauce](/mise/recipes/chinese-garlic-sauce-base), made with vegetarian mushroom sauce; half its recipe
1 tsp sambal oelek chili paste, optional, plus up to 1 tsp more to taste
1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, optional, only if needed after tasting

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the sauce: Make half the linked Garlic-Ginger Stir-Fry Sauce recipe, using vegetarian mushroom sauce, for a finished 120 ml. Alternatively, measure 120 ml from a previously prepared batch and keep its original storage date in mind.
Cut the vegetables: Trim eggplant and cut into roughly 2-inch batons about 1/2 inch thick. Slice scallions. Divide eggplant into two equal batches.

Brown and soften in two batches: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a lidded skillet over medium-high. Add half the eggplant in one layer and cook 3–4 minutes, turning to color several surfaces. Reduce to medium, add 2 tbsp water, cover and cook another 3–5 minutes until a fork enters the center easily. Add a little more water only if the pan dries while centers are firm. Uncover to evaporate remaining water, then transfer to a plate. Repeat with the remaining tablespoon oil, eggplant and 2 tbsp water.

Coat gently: Return all eggplant to the pan with the 120 ml sauce and optional initial amount of chili paste. Fold gently over medium heat for about 1–2 minutes until bubbling and evenly coated. If using refrigerated sauce, check the finished dish reaches 165°F / 74°C. Thin a very tight coating with a tablespoon of hot water if needed.

Finish: Take off heat, fold in scallions and taste. Add optional vinegar or the additional chili-paste allowance only if wanted. Divide into four vegetable sides with rice and a separate main or protein component.

recipes.keywords: Chinese-American-inspired, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, rich, weeknight, quick-lunch, saute, steam

recipes.name: Elderberry Syrup
recipes.description: This spiced elderberry-and-honey syrup is a culinary preparation. Use food-grade dried ripe elderberries and follow their cooking instructions; raw or unripe berries and other plant parts can cause illness.

recipeInstructions.text: Concentrate: In a medium saucepan, combine water, elderberries, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves.
Simmer: Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover. Simmer for 45-60 minutes until the liquid has reduced by half.
Mash: Remove from heat. Use a flat utensil or potato masher to crush the berries, releasing any remaining juice.
Strain: Pour the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a clean glass jar. Press firmly on the solids. Discard the berries.
Sweeten: Let the liquid cool until it is lukewarm (below 110°F). Stir in the raw honey until completely dissolved and integrated.

Freeze for storage: Cool promptly in small, clean containers and freeze in portions suitable for later use, leaving freezer-safe headspace. Thaw only the portion needed in the refrigerator. Do not can this syrup or try to make it shelf-stable by adding alcohol or citric acid.
Serve as a food: Use a little for flavor in a drink or with food if desired. This homemade syrup has no established standard medicinal dose for children or adults.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, kid-friendly, simmer, boil, blend

recipes.name: Elote-Style Corn on the Cob
recipes.description: Elote (Mexican street corn) is simplicity perfected: charred corn, creamy sauce, crumbly cheese, and bright cilantro. The magic happens when you char the corn first to caramelize the kernels - this takes just 8-10 minutes under the broiler or on a hot grill.
recipeIngredient: 4 ears Fresh Corn on the cob
3 tbsp Mexican Crema (or sour cream thinned with 1 tbsp milk)

recipeInstructions.text: Prep Corn: Remove husks and silk. Pat corn dry with a paper towel.

Char: Option A (Broiler - easier for families): Place corn on a foil-lined baking sheet. Broil 4-6 inches from the heat for 8-10 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes, until the kernels are lightly charred in spots. Option B (Grill): Place directly on a hot grill grates and turn every 2-3 minutes for 8-10 minutes.
Make Sauce: Whisk together crema, 1/4 tsp salt, and a pinch of black pepper in a small bowl.
Assemble: Carefully remove corn from heat. Hold corn vertical over a shallow bowl or plate. Use a brush or spoon to coat the entire corn with a thin layer of crema.
Top: Roll in (or sprinkle with) crumbled queso fresco, coating all sides. Sprinkle with fresh cilantro and a pinch of chili powder or chile-lime seasoning.
Finish: Serve with lime wedges to squeeze over. Eat immediately while warm.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, creamy, savory, spicy, tangy, weeknight, entertaining, grill, broil

recipes.name: Enchiladas Suizas
recipes.description: Enchiladas Suizas (Swiss-style) refers to the generous use of cream and cheese, a style that originated in Mexico City in the 1950s. The dish balances tart, roasted tomatillos with rich heavy cream.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Monterey Jack or Chihuahua Cheese, shredded

recipeInstructions.text: Roast: Place tomatillos, jalapeños, onion, and garlic on a baking sheet. Broil for 5-7 minutes until charred and softened.
Blend: Place the roasted veg in a blender with the cilantro and heavy cream. Blend until smooth. Season with salt.
Prep Tortillas: Heat 1/4 inch of oil in a small skillet. Dip each tortilla in the oil for 5-10 seconds per side (until pliable but not crisp). Drain on paper towels.
Assemble: Dip a tortilla in the green sauce, fill with shredded chicken and a sprinkle of cheese, and roll tightly. Place in a baking dish.
Bake: Pour the remaining sauce over the top and cover with the rest of the cheese. Bake at 375°F for 15-20 minutes until the cheese is bubbling.
Finish: Top with pickled red onions and fresh cilantro.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, spicy, rich, comfort-food, bake, roast, fry, poach, no-cook, blend

recipes.name: Everyday Arugula Salad
recipes.description: Peppery arugula with lemon, olive oil, and Parmesan. Dress just before serving so the leaves stay light and crisp.
recipeIngredient: 20 g Parmesan, shaved (about 1/3 cup loose shavings)
1/8 tsp fine salt, plus more only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Dry the greens: Wash arugula if needed and spin or pat dry. Place in a wide mixing bowl. Shave the cheese.
Mix dressing: Whisk oil, lemon juice, measured salt, and pepper together in a small bowl.

Toss just before eating: Add about three-quarters of the dressing to the leaves and lift gently with clean hands or salad servers. Add the remaining dressing only if the leaves need it; they should look lightly glossy rather than wet.
Finish: Add Parmesan and toss once or scatter it over the top. Taste a leaf with cheese before deciding whether it needs any additional salt. Divide among four plates and serve immediately.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, umami, rich, weeknight, light-and-fresh, quick-lunch, no-cook

recipes.name: Extraordinary Chocolate Chip Cookie
recipes.description: The secret to extraordinary texture is chilling the dough for 24 hours. Refrigerating the dough overnight is mandatory; it allows the starch to fully hydrate and the sugars to undergo enzymatic breakdown, resulting in a cookie with deep, butterscotch-like flavor.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/4 cups (2 1/2 sticks) Unsalted Butter, room temp
4 1/2 cups Semisweet Chocolate Chips (The "Maximum Chocolate" Method)

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: Whisk together flour, salt, baking powder, and baking soda. Set aside.
Cream: In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, cream butter and both sugars on medium speed for exactly 4 minutes until pale and aerated. Add eggs one at a time, followed by vanilla.
Combine: On low speed, add the flour mixture until just combined. Fold in the chocolate chips by hand to avoid breaking them.
The Chill: Press plastic wrap against the surface of the dough and refrigerate for at least 24 hours (ideally 36).
Portion: Preheat oven to 350°F. Using a 2 1/4-inch scoop, drop dough balls onto parchment-lined sheets, 3 inches apart.
Bake: Bake for 15-17 minutes until the edges are golden brown and the centers are set but still look soft.
Cool: Let sit on the sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, bake

recipes.name: Falafel
recipes.description: Small chickpea-and-herb falafel with a crisp crust and a tender, finely textured center. Grind soaked, uncooked chickpeas and fry one test piece before committing the batch.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups (400 g) dried chickpeas, sorted and rinsed; weigh before soaking
10 cups (2.4 L) cold water for soaking, plus more if needed to keep the chickpeas covered
1 cup (30 g) fresh parsley leaves and tender stems, washed and thoroughly dried
1 cup (30 g) fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems, washed and thoroughly dried
1 small yellow onion (120 g peeled), roughly chopped
4 medium garlic cloves, peeled and roughly chopped
6 g salt, weighed (about 1 tsp fine salt), plus up to 3 g more only after tasting a fried test piece
Refined canola or sunflower oil for frying: about 8 cups (1.9 L), with the actual amount set by pot width and required depth

recipeInstructions.text: Soak ahead: Put the sorted and rinsed dried chickpeas in a large bowl with the soaking water. Cover and refrigerate for 12–24 hours, allowing plenty of room for expansion and adding water if needed to keep them covered. Drain and rinse. The beans should be plump and hydrated but still firm; do not boil them. Cut open a few: the inside should be evenly hydrated rather than showing a hard, dry core. If needed, continue the refrigerated soak within the stated twenty-four-hour window. Spread on a clean towel and blot away surface water.

Prepare herbs and spices: Wash and thoroughly dry the herbs, then roughly chop them. Put cumin and coriander seeds in a small dry skillet over medium-low heat. Stir for about 1–2 minutes, until fragrant but not smoking or blackened. Tip out promptly, cool, and grind finely. Peel and roughly chop onion and garlic.

Grind in batches: Put chickpeas, herbs, onion, and garlic in the processor. Divide the chickpeas, herbs, onion and garlic evenly between processor batches if needed, so the bottom does not become paste while the top stays coarse. Pulse, stopping to scrape, until finely and evenly chopped with no large chickpea fragments. A spoonful pressed between your palms should hold a rough mound. Combine all processor batches in a large bowl.

Season and chill: Mix in the ground toasted spices, baking powder, measured salt, and pepper evenly. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes. The rest makes the mixture easier to handle; it does not cook the chickpeas. Season by tasting a cooked test piece in step 6, rather than the raw mixture.

Prepare one test portion: After chilling, weigh one 25 g portion and press gently into a small ball, closing large cracks without compressing it into a hard lump. About 1 1/2 inches across is a guide; weight governs if the two differ. Keep the remaining mixture covered and refrigerated while the oil heats.

Heat, test and adjust: Set a wire rack over a rimmed sheet. Add oil to the deep pot to a two-inch depth with at least three inches of clear space above it. Heat to 350°F / 175°C under supervision, with the thermometer sensing in the oil rather than against the pot bottom. Lower the test with a dry metal slotted spoon. Fry about four to five minutes, turning as needed, until evenly brown. Drain on the rack, turn off the burner and leave the stable pot in place. Stay nearby while the test cools enough to split and taste: its center should be tender and finely crumbed, without hard fragments or dense wet paste. Add some of the reserved salt to the remaining mixture only if the test needs it. Correct any breakup or undercooked center and fry another test before shaping the rest; do not carry the hot oil pot to another work area.

Shape the remaining batch: With the burner off and the pot undisturbed, shape 25 g portions at an adjacent clear work surface away from the oil. Stay in the kitchen with the pot in view and keep splashing water away. Expect about forty to forty-five pieces in total, depending on hydration; close cracks gently. Refrigerate the shaped portions while bringing the oil back to 350°F / 175°C, allowing another five to ten minutes.

Fry in small batches: Cook five or six pieces at a time for about four to five minutes, turning for even color. Monitor the oil and reduce the next load if its temperature drops sharply or recovers slowly. Let it return to 350°F between rounds and skim loose crumbs. Check another center when batch size or browning changes. Keep waiting portions refrigerated, drain cooked pieces in one layer, and serve successive batches promptly. After the final round, turn off the burner and let the oil cool in place before handling or disposal.

Serve with accompaniments: Divide the actual batch among six diners, usually six or seven small falafel each, sharing extras; an eaten test piece reduces the number for the table. Offer about two tablespoons tahini sauce each, or three-quarters of a cup total, plus warm pita and vegetables. Six pocket breads require more warming rounds than the linked four-bread recipe. For six generous fattoush sides, make one and a half batches of that recipe, including its separately counted crisp pita; account for that bread alongside the pocket breads. Hummus can be a small optional dip. These accompaniments are additional recipes and time.

recipes.keywords: Middle Eastern, herbaceous, savory, crispy, entertaining, weekend-dinner, toast, blend, fry

recipes.name: Farfel Muffins
recipes.description: This dish comes from a home cooking tradition where technique and respect for ingredients matter more than complexity. This is meant to be reliable and honest - quality ingredients cooked with care, nothing fancy, just right.

recipeInstructions.text: Hydrate: Preheat oven to 400°F. In a large bowl, pour the boiling water over the matzo farfel. Stir once and let sit until the water is fully absorbed and the mixture is cool to the touch.
The Emulsion: Stir in the melted butter. Add the eggs one at a time, stirring vigorously after each addition until the batter is glossy and uniform. Season with salt.
Fill: Spoon the batter into a well-greased muffin tin, filling each cup about 3/4 full.
Bake: Bake at 400°F for 20 minutes until the tops are deep golden brown and the muffins feel light when lifted.
Serve: Best served warm with plenty of salted butter.

recipes.keywords: Jewish, rich, holiday, comfort-food, bake, boil

recipes.name: Fattoush Salad
recipes.description: Fresh vegetables, herbs, sumac, and crisp toasted pita with a lemon-pomegranate dressing. Add bread at the table to control its texture.
recipeIngredient: 120 g pita bread, split into thin layers and torn into bite-sized pieces
2 tbsp olive oil, for the pita
1 tsp ground sumac, for the pita
400 g ripe tomatoes, cut into bite-sized pieces
200 g Persian or English cucumber, sliced
1 cup loosely packed parsley leaves, roughly chopped
1/2 cup loosely packed mint leaves, torn
150 g romaine or Little Gem lettuce, washed and dried, then torn
3 tbsp olive oil, for the dressing
2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus up to 1 tbsp more to taste
1 tsp ground sumac, for the dressing

recipeInstructions.text: Toast pita: Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Toss pita with its 2 tbsp oil and teaspoon of sumac. Spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet pan. Bake about 8–10 minutes, turning once, until golden and dry. Cool uncovered; thick pieces may need a little longer.
Mix dressing: Whisk the dressing oil, initial 2 tbsp lemon juice, pomegranate molasses, garlic, dressing sumac, salt, and pepper. Set aside the optional extra lemon.
Prepare vegetables: Combine tomatoes, cucumber, radishes, scallions, dry lettuce, parsley, and mint in a large bowl. Keep refrigerated if the meal is not ready.

Dress and taste: Just before serving, add about three-quarters of the dressing and toss gently. Taste a bite and add the rest only as needed. Add some of the reserved lemon if it needs more brightness.
Add bread: Fold in cooled pita just before dividing among four plates, or offer it separately for diners to add themselves. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Middle Eastern, acidic, herbaceous, savory, light-and-fresh, quick-lunch, entertaining, bake, no-cook

recipes.name: Cream Cheese Frosting
recipes.description: This is our go-to cream cheese frosting for all cakes. The secret to frosting that isn't runny is temperature control: both the butter and cream cheese must be softened to the same temperature before starting.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Full-fat Block Cream Cheese, softened
3 cups Confectioners’ Sugar (plus extra if needed)

recipeInstructions.text: Cream: In a large bowl using a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, beat the cream cheese and butter on high speed for exactly 2 minutes until perfectly smooth and creamy.
Incorporate: Reduce speed to low. Add 3 cups of confectioners’ sugar, vanilla, and salt.
Aeration: Once the sugar is mostly mixed in, switch to high speed and beat for 2-3 minutes. The frosting should be light, fluffy, and hold a stiff peak.
Adjust: If you prefer a thicker consistency for piping, add the additional 1/4 cup of sugar.
Store: Use immediately or refrigerate for up to 5 days. If chilled, let sit at room temp for 30 minutes and beat briefly before using to restore the "Bounce."

recipes.name: Pumpkin Oatmeal Muffins
recipes.description: These are nutritious breakfast muffins. We blend the rolled oats into a smooth, nutrient-dense flour directly with the wet ingredients.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Milk of choice (Soy or Almond preferred)

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin or use silicone liners.
Blend: Combine oats, pumpkin puree, milk, maple syrup, eggs, spices, baking soda, vanilla, and salt in a high-powered blender.
Pulverize: Blend on high for 60 seconds until the batter is perfectly smooth and the oats have transformed into flour.
Fill: Divide the batter evenly among the muffin cups (about 3/4 full). If using chocolate chips, sprinkle them onto the top of each muffin now for a visual "High Note."
Bake: Bake for 20-22 minutes until firm to the touch and the edges are lightly golden.
Cool: Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes to allow the oat structure to set.
Store: These keep in the fridge for 5 days or the freezer for 3 months.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, umami, meal-prep, kid-friendly, snack, bake, blend

recipes.name: Fennel and Carrot Soup
recipes.description: This soup showcases deep flavor development. The secret is the low-slow sauté: we cook the vegetables in butter for a full 45-60 minutes before adding the broth.
recipeIngredient: 1 small Yukon Gold Potato, peeled and halved

recipeInstructions.text: Sweat: In a large heavy pot, melt 4 tbsp butter over medium. Add fennel, onion, carrots, and potato. Season with salt and pepper.
Low & Slow: Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 45-60 minutes. Stir occasionally. The vegetables should be very soft and aromatic but not browned.
Simmer: Add broth, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes until the potato is falling apart. Remove herbs.
The Emulsion: Working in batches, puree the soup in a blender until perfectly smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for an even more elite texture.
Toast: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp butter in a small pan. Add chopped chestnuts and cook until the butter is nutty brown and the nuts are fragrant.
The Crown: Whisk the crème fraîche and maple syrup together.
Serve: Ladle soup into bowls. Top with a swirl of maple crème fraîche and the brown-butter chestnuts.

recipes.name: Flourless Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: This is the classic flourless chocolate cake for Passover and gluten-free celebrations. The key to its texture is melting high-quality chocolate directly into hot cream off the heat to create a mirror-shiny glaze that provides a contrast to the dense, fudgy cake.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Semisweet or Bittersweet Chocolate Chips

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: Preheat oven to 375°F. In a microwave-safe bowl, melt 1 cup chocolate chips and the butter in 30-second bursts until smooth.
Flavor: Whisk in the espresso powder, vanilla, and salt. Add the eggs one at a time, beating briefly until the batter is glossy.
Incorporate: Sift in the cocoa powder and sugar. Fold gently until just combined.
Bake: Grease an 8-inch round pan and line with parchment. Pour in the batter. Bake for 25 minutes until the top forms a thin, crackly crust and the internal temp is 200°F.
Cool: Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then invert onto a serving plate. Allow to cool completely before glazing.
The Glaze: Heat 1/2 cup heavy cream until steaming. Pour over 1 cup chocolate chips. Let sit for 5 minutes, then whisk until mirror-glossy.
Finish: Pour the ganache over the center of the cake, encouraging it to drip down the sides for Textural Balance.

recipes.name: Soft Scrambled Eggs
recipes.description: Small, moist curds made with steady stirring and gentle heat. Learn to control protein setting and carryover cooking.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp crème fraîche or sour cream
1/8 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk: Beat the eggs and salt in a bowl until the whites and yolks are fully combined. Melt butter in a nonstick skillet over low to medium-low heat; it should foam gently without browning.

Stir gently: Add eggs and continuously sweep a flexible spatula across the bottom and sides. As small curds form, keep folding them through the liquid. If the eggs set rapidly or stick in a dry layer, lift the pan off the heat briefly and lower the burner. Expect about 5–7 minutes, depending on the pan.

Finish cooking: Stir in the crème fraîche when most of the eggs have formed curds. Continue gently until the eggs are set with no liquid egg pooling and reach 160°F / 71°C. Measure in the eggs without touching the pan. The curds can remain moist without being runny.
Serve promptly: Transfer to plates immediately. Taste and adjust salt and pepper, then add chives. The hot pan would continue to firm the eggs if you left them in it.

recipes.name: Freezer Banana Bread
recipes.description: This banana bread is designed for freezer storage. The key to a perfect slice every morning is using Greek yogurt instead of butter to create a dense, moist texture that survives the freezing process without becoming crumbly.

recipeInstructions.text: The Emulsion: Preheat oven to 350°F. In a blender, combine bananas, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, egg, yogurt, and milk. Blend on high for 30 seconds until perfectly smooth.
Dry Mix: In a large bowl, whisk together the whole-wheat flour, baking soda, and baking powder.
Combine: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry. Stir with a spatula until just combined (do not over-mix, or the whole-wheat will turn tough).
Bake: Pour into a greased loaf pan. Bake for 50-55 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool: Let cool in the pan for 15 minutes before slicing.
The Freeze: To store, slice the loaf into 1/2-inch rounds. Place parchment between slices and freeze in a zip-top bag. Reheat individual slices in the toaster for a Crunch finish.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, weekend-project, bake, blend

recipes.name: Freezer Date Cookies
recipes.description: These are nutritious cookies designed for long-term freezer storage. The key to their texture is processing the Medjool dates directly with the melted butter in a food processor to create a smooth, caramel-like paste that acts as the primary sweetener.

recipeInstructions.text: The Date Paste: Place the pitted Medjool dates and melted butter in a food processor. Pulse on high until a completely smooth, thick paste forms.
The Emulsion: Add the egg, yogurt, and vanilla to the processor. Pulse for 10 seconds until perfectly integrated.
Dry Mix: In a separate bowl, whisk together buckwheat flour, whole wheat flour, oats, baking soda, and cinnamon.
Combine: Pour the date mixture into the dry ingredients. Mix with a spatula until a thick, sticky dough forms.
Shape: Preheat oven to 350°F. Roll the dough into small balls (about 1 tbsp each). Place on a greased cookie sheet and press down firmly with your palm to create a 1/2-inch thick disk.
Bake: Bake for 12-15 minutes until the edges are lightly browned.
The Freeze: Let cool completely. Transfer to a freezer bag. These are at their Kitchen Standard when eaten straight from the freezer.

recipes.name: Slow Cooker French Dip Sandwiches
recipes.description: The French Dip is all about the Jus (the juice). Most home versions are watery; we fix this by using Soy Sauce instead of just salt to provide a deep, dark umami base that mimics a 24-hour restaurant stock.

recipeInstructions.text: Sear (Optional but better): Sear the beef roast in a hot skillet with a little oil until browned on all sides. Place in the slow cooker.
Combine: Add the sliced onion, garlic, stock, soy sauce, Worcestershire, and rosemary to the slow cooker.
Slow Cook: Cook on LOW for 8 hours (or high for 4-5 hours) until the beef pulls apart with a fork.
Shred: Remove beef to a cutting board. Shred into large chunks or slice thin.
Strain: Pour the liquid from the slow cooker through a sieve into small individual dipping bowls (ramekins).
Assemble: Split the rolls. Pile the beef onto each roll and top with a slice of provolone.
Toast: Place the sandwiches under the BROILER for 1-2 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and the bread is toasted.
Serve: Serve immediately with the hot Jus on the side for dipping.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, umami, comfort-food, slow-cook

recipes.name: French Toast
recipes.description: The secret to restaurant-quality French toast is the bread choice. We exclusively use challah or brioche for their high egg and butter content, which creates a custardy texture that regular white bread cannot mimic.

recipeInstructions.text: The Spice: In a small bowl, whisk cinnamon, nutmeg, and warmed honey until no clumps remain.
The Custard: In a shallow dish (like a pie plate), whisk together the honey-spice mix, eggs, milk, and vanilla until perfectly smooth.
The Sear: Heat 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium.
Dip: Working in batches, dip a slice of bread into the custard for exactly 2 seconds per side. Let the excess drip off.
Cook: Immediately place in the skillet. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden brown and slightly crisped at the edges.
Serve: Serve immediately with warm maple syrup and fresh berries for the mandatory Acid/Sweet Finish.

recipes.keywords: French, sweet, acidic, rich, comfort-food, fry

recipes.name: Fresh Cabbage, Cucumber and Radish Kimchi
recipes.description: This is fresh kimchi ready to eat immediately. The key to crisp, non-watery kimchi is salting the vegetables heavily for an hour to draw out excess moisture that would otherwise dilute the spice paste.
recipeIngredient: 3 lbs Napa Cabbage, halved and cut into 2-inch pieces
1 1/4 lbs Daikon Radish, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1/4 cup + 2 tbsp Rice Vinegar (The Finishing Touch)

recipeInstructions.text: The Cure: In four separate large bowls, divide the cabbage, cucumbers, daikon, and radishes. Sprinkle 2 tbsp of salt into each bowl and toss well. Let stand for 1 hour at room temperature.
The Paste: In a high-powered blender, combine ginger, garlic, gochugaru, rice vinegar, sesame oil, fish sauce, scallions, and sugar. Puree until almost smooth.
The Rinse: Drain the vegetables thoroughly. Gently squeeze each handful to remove all remaining water.
The Bind: In one massive bowl, toss all the vegetables with the kimchi paste until every piece is uniformly coated in the deep red glaze.
The Finish: Transfer to glass jars. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (ideally 24) to allow the flavors to meld and the fermentation to begin.
Serve: This fresh kimchi (Geotjeori style) is at its best within the first week.

recipes.keywords: Korean, sweet, acidic, weekend-project, make-ahead, blend

recipes.name: Fresh Egg Pasta
recipes.description: A yolk-enriched dough for rolled ribbons, with measured water adjustments, a covered rest, and thickness cues that work across pasta machines.
recipeIngredient: 290 g all-purpose flour, plus a little for dusting
1/4 tsp fine salt, for the dough
2 tbsp cool water, only as needed for the dough
2 tbsp fine semolina or all-purpose flour, for dusting cut pasta
4 quarts (3.8 liters) water, for cooking pasta
1 tbsp fine salt, for the pasta water

recipeInstructions.text: Mix: Pulse the measured flour and dough salt in a food processor. Beat eggs, yolks, and oil together, add, and pulse until evenly crumbly. Squeeze a small handful: if it holds together, stop. If it falls into dry crumbs, add the measured water a teaspoon at a time, pulsing briefly and checking again. You may not need all of it. Do not taste the raw mixture.

Knead: Tip onto a clean work surface and press together. Knead for about 5–8 minutes until firm and reasonably smooth. Use very little dusting flour. If still dry and cracked, knead with lightly damp hands; if tacky, dust sparingly.

Rest covered: Wrap tightly or place in a covered container so the surface cannot dry out. Rest for 1 hour at ordinary room temperature. Refrigerate instead if the kitchen is very hot or preparation will be delayed.

Roll gradually: Divide into four pieces and keep three covered. Flatten one piece, dust lightly, and pass through the roller's widest setting. Fold in thirds and repeat once or twice to form an even strip. Progress through narrower settings without skipping several at once, stopping at about 1 mm for fettuccine. Rest a resistant piece covered for 5–10 minutes rather than forcing it.

Cut: Let a tacky sheet sit just briefly until its surface no longer sticks, then cut into ribbons. Dust with the measured semolina or flour, shake off excess, and arrange in loose nests on a lined tray. Repeat with the remaining dough. Cook promptly, or refrigerate/freeze as described below.

Boil and finish: Bring the cooking water and its salt to a full boil. Add noodles, separating them gently, and cook until no floury center remains, generally 2–5 minutes depending on thickness and drying. Taste only after cooking. Reserve a little cooking water before draining, then combine promptly with the chosen sauce.

recipes.name: Pasta Dough
recipes.description: Traditional pasta dough from Northern Italy uses just flour and eggs - the simplicity lets you taste the quality of each ingredient. The 30-60 minute rest period is essential: it allows the gluten to relax fully so the dough rolls smoothly without springing back.

recipeInstructions.text: The Mix: Place flour and salt in the bowl of a stand mixer. Create a well in the center. Add the eggs and olive oil.
The Hook: Use the dough hook on speed 2. Run until a shaggy dough forms and starts to climb the hook (about 3-4 mins).
The Knead: Continue on speed 2 for 8-10 minutes. The dough should transform from lumpy to completely smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky.
The Rest: Remove from the bowl. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap. Let rest for at least 30 minutes (up to 24 hours in the fridge) before rolling.
Shape: Cut, roll, and shape as desired. See Fresh Egg Pasta for rolling settings.

recipes.name: Strawberry Vinaigrette
recipes.description: A berry-forward dressing with balsamic vinegar, honey and olive oil, blended after a short rest to soften the sliced fruit.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare fruit: Wash the strawberries, remove their hulls, slice and measure the listed amount.
Rest: Stir vinegar and honey together in a bowl, coat the berries with the mixture and leave for 30 minutes. Keep all the released juice.

Blend: Transfer berries and liquid to a small processor or suitable blender vessel. Add olive oil and a little salt and pepper; blend until the fruit is finely broken down, stopping to scrape safely if needed.

Taste and dress: Taste a small amount on a leaf. Adjust with a little honey if sharply tart or a little vinegar if too sweet, then check salt and pepper. Toss into dry greens gradually just before serving and reserve excess dressing for another salad.

recipes.name: Wonton Wrappers
recipes.description: Homemade wonton wrappers have a delicate, silky texture that's hard to match with store-bought. The dough should be quite firm after kneading, then rested for 30-60 minutes to relax the gluten so you can roll it paper-thin.
recipeIngredient: Cornstarch (for dusting - Do not use flour for dusting!)

recipeInstructions.text: Mix: In a large bowl, whisk the flour and salt. Make a well in the center. Add the egg and water. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Turn out onto a clean surface and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be quite firm.
Rest: Wrap in plastic and let rest at room temperature for at least 30-60 minutes. This relaxes the gluten so you can roll it paper-thin.
Roll: Divide dough into 4 pieces. Use a pasta machine (recommended) or a heavy rolling pin. Roll until the dough is thin enough to see your hand through it (Setting 6 or 7 on most pasta machines).
Cut: Dust generously with cornstarch. Cut into 3.5-inch squares.
Store: Stack with plenty of cornstarch between layers. Wrap tightly in plastic. (Can be refrigerated for 2 days or frozen for 3 months).

recipes.name: Fried Sweet Plantains (Maduros)
recipes.description: Maduros are the sweet cousin of tostones — ripe plantains pan-fried until the sugars caramelize into a glossy, jammy interior with crisp edges. The single thing that matters is ripeness: the plantains should look nearly ruined, with skins that are mostly black with yellow patches.
recipeIngredient: 3 very ripe Plantains (skins should be mostly black with yellow patches)
3 tbsp Neutral Oil (vegetable, canola, or coconut)

recipeInstructions.text: Check ripeness: The plantains should yield to gentle pressure and the skin should be mostly black. If still firm and yellow, leave them on the counter another day or two.
Peel and slice: Score the skin end-to-end with a knife, peel back (easier than a banana once ripe). Slice on a sharp diagonal into 1/2-inch pieces.
Heat the pan: Add oil to a large skillet over medium heat. When it shimmers, add plantain slices in a single layer — don't crowd, or they steam instead of caramelize.
Fry: Cook 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and the sugars have caramelized into a sticky crust. Flip once — they're delicate when soft.
Drain and season: Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate. Sprinkle with a small pinch of salt (it amplifies the sweetness). A dusting of cinnamon is optional.
Serve immediately: Maduros lose their magic as they cool — crisp edges soften and the caramelization dulls. Plate straight from the pan.

recipes.name: Frozen Blueberry Muffins
recipes.description: Keep blueberries frozen when folding into batter - thawed berries bleed juice that turns muffins muddy purple. Frozen berries also maintain better texture during baking.

recipeInstructions.text: The Emulsion: Preheat oven to 375°F. Grease two 12-cup muffin tins. In a large bowl, cream the butter and 2 cups minus 2 tbsp of the sugar until light and fluffy (3-5 mins). Add eggs one at a time, followed by milk and vanilla.
Dry Mix: Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Combine: Fold the dry ingredients into the wet until just combined. A few streaks of flour are fine.
The Fold: Gently fold in the frozen blueberries. Do not over-mix.
The Topping: In a small bowl, whisk the remaining 2 tbsp sugar with the nutmeg.
Bake: Divide the batter among the cups (about 2/3 full). Sprinkle the nutmeg sugar over the tops. Bake for 20-25 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool: Let sit in the pan for 10 minutes to allow the fruit structure to set before removing to a wire rack.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, entertaining, weekend-project, bake

recipes.name: Funfetti Cake
recipes.description: Whipping egg whites separately and folding them in at the end creates light, airy texture. Use long cylindrical jimmies rather than round nonpareils - nonpareils bleed their color and turn batter gray, while jimmies provide colorful pops throughout.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour three 8-inch round pans.
The Emulsion: In a stand mixer, beat 9 tbsp butter, sugar, and oil on medium-low until creamy. Stir in vanilla.
Dry Mix: Whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Combine: Alternately add the dry mix and the milk to the butter mixture, beginning and ending with the dry. Stir until just combined.
Aeration: In a clean bowl, beat egg whites until stiff peaks form.
The Fold: Gently fold the whipped whites and sprinkles into the batter using a spatula. Do not over-mix.
Bake: Divide among pans. Bake for 35-40 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pans for 15 minutes, then invert onto racks.
The Frosting: Beat 1 lb butter until creamy. Gradually add sugar, then heavy cream and vanilla. Beat on high for 3 minutes until billowy.
Assemble: Layer the cooled cakes with frosting. Do a thin "crumb coat" and freeze for 10 minutes before applying the final thick layer of buttercream for a professional Crunch finish.

recipes.name: Gambas al Ajillo
recipes.description: Gambas al ajillo is the ultimate proof that Spanish cooking is about restraint and great ingredients rather than complex technique. The entire dish cooks in under 5 minutes, so everything must be prepped and within arm's reach before you heat the pan.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Large Shrimp (16-20 count), peeled and deveined, tails on
2 Dried Guindilla Peppers (or 1 tsp red pepper flakes)
1 tsp Smoked Paprika (pimenton de la Vera)
2 tbsp Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley, roughly chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Prep Everything First: Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels and season with 1/2 tsp salt and the smoked paprika. Have the sliced garlic, dried peppers, sherry, parsley, and lemon juice ready beside the stove. This dish moves fast.

Heat the Oil: Pour the olive oil into a cast-iron skillet or cazuela over medium heat. When the oil begins to shimmer, add the sliced garlic and dried guindilla peppers. Cook for 30-45 seconds, swirling constantly, until the garlic is pale golden. Do not walk away.
Add the Shrimp: Increase heat to medium-high. Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 1 minute without moving them. Flip and cook for 30 seconds more.
Deglaze: Pour in the sherry. It will bubble vigorously. Cook for 30 seconds to burn off the raw alcohol while the shrimp finish cooking through.
Finish: Remove from heat immediately. The shrimp should be just pink and curled into a C-shape (not a tight O, which means overcooked). Squeeze the lemon juice over the pan and scatter with parsley.
Serve: Bring the sizzling skillet directly to the table. Serve with plenty of crusty bread to mop up the garlicky, paprika-stained oil. The bread-dipping is the best part.

recipes.keywords: Spanish, savory, spicy, umami, rich, date-night, entertaining, quick-lunch, saute

recipes.name: Garlic Bread
recipes.description: A measured garlic, parsley and Parmesan butter on a crusty loaf, baked until the edges crisp while the middle stays tender.
recipeIngredient: 400 g crusty Italian-style bread or baguette
4 cloves garlic, finely grated or minced
1/4 tsp fine salt, or less if bread and cheese are salty

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare oven and bread: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Halve the loaf lengthwise and put both pieces cut-side up on a rimmed baking sheet. Use already softened butter; allow extra time if starting with a cold block.
Mix spread: Stir butter, garlic, parsley, Parmesan and the measured salt until uniform. Use less salt if the bread and cheese are already strongly seasoned.
Spread evenly: Divide all the butter mixture across the two cut surfaces, reaching the edges in a thin, even layer. Avoid large isolated clumps of garlic.
Bake: Bake about 12–15 minutes until the edges are golden and the center is hot with melted butter. Thick loaves may need a few more minutes; cover loosely with foil if the edges brown too soon.

Optional top color: If wanted, broil briefly for about 20–60 seconds, watching continuously and stopping as soon as the top colors. Keep the pan at least 6 inches from the element and follow the oven's broiler guidance. Do not put parchment close to a broiler.

Portion: Cut each half into six pieces, making twelve pieces total, or two pieces per side portion. Serve hot. For a small accompaniment to a pasta-containing soup, make half a batch and share its six pieces among six diners.

recipes.keywords: Italian-American, savory, rich, herbaceous, comfort-food, weeknight, entertaining, potluck, bake, broil

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Pearl Couscous
recipes.description: Small semolina pasta toasted in butter, simmered with broth and finished with parsley and optional lemon zest.
recipeIngredient: 225 g (about 1 1/2 cups) dry pearl couscous, not fine instant couscous
2 1/4 cups (540 ml) low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth, with package-specific adjustment if needed
1/4 tsp fine salt, added only as needed
1 tsp finely grated lemon zest, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Toast gently: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a 2-quart saucepan over medium. Add pearl couscous and stir 2–3 minutes until a few pearls turn golden. Reduce heat if the butter darkens quickly.

Add garlic and broth: Stir garlic for about 30 seconds, then carefully pour in the measured broth. Add black pepper. Bring to a simmer; hold the salt until you know how salty the broth tastes after cooking.

Cover and cook: Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer about 10–15 minutes, or according to the package’s absorption method, until tender with slight chew. Check near the end. If dry and firm, add hot water 2 tbsp at a time; if tender with excess liquid, uncover briefly to reduce it without overcooking.
Rest and finish: Take off heat and leave covered 5 minutes. Fluff gently, fold in the remaining tablespoon butter, parsley and optional zest. Taste and add the measured salt only if needed.
Portion: Divide into four normal sides or use the smaller portion specified by a composed meal. This recipe already contains its finishing butter; add no extra oil automatically at the table.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean-inspired, savory, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, entertaining, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Green Beans
recipes.description: French cooks master this in two minutes - the trick is high heat and constant motion so the garlic perfumes the butter without browning and turning bitter. This is the sauté technique that works: start with cold butter and garlic together so the garlic gently infuses as the butter melts.

recipeInstructions.text: Blanch (optional but smart): Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add green beans and cook for 3-4 minutes until barely tender-crisp. Drain and set aside. This step can be done ahead.
Toast Almonds: In a large skillet over medium-low heat, toast the sliced almonds for 2-3 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant. Transfer to a plate.

Butter and Garlic: Return skillet to medium heat. Add cold butter and thinly sliced garlic. Stir constantly for 60-90 seconds until the garlic is soft and fragrant but not browned. Smell it - you'll know when it's ready.

Combine: Add the green beans (or fresh uncooked beans if skipping the blanch step, cooking for 7-8 minutes over medium-high heat with constant tossing). Toss constantly for 1-2 minutes to coat with the garlic butter. Season with salt and pepper.
Finish: Add the toasted almonds back in. Toss once more. Transfer to a serving dish and finish with flaky sea salt. Serve immediately.

recipes.keywords: French, American, savory, herbaceous, nutty, weeknight, entertaining, comfort-food, saute

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Salmon with Potatoes and Asparagus
recipes.description: Garlic-lemon butter salmon with roasted baby potatoes and asparagus. Give the potatoes a head start, then remove each component when it is ready.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/4 lb skinless salmon fillet, cut into 4 similar portions
1 lb baby Yukon Gold potatoes, halved; quarter larger ones into pieces about 1 inch across
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided equally between potatoes and asparagus
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from Carolyn Casner’s recipe at EatingWell.

itemListElement.text: Heat and cut: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Halve baby potatoes; quarter larger ones so the pieces are about 1 inch across. Pat salmon dry and check for pin bones. Keep it refrigerated while the potatoes start.

Start potatoes: Toss potatoes with half the olive oil, salt and pepper. Spread cut-side down on the rimmed tray. Roast for about 20–25 minutes, checking at 15, until nearly tender with some browning. If the knife still meets a hard center, continue before adding fish.

Prepare asparagus and butter: While potatoes roast, toss trimmed asparagus with the remaining olive oil, salt and pepper. Stir melted butter, lemon juice and garlic together. Season the salmon lightly with salt and pepper.

Arrange: Move potatoes to one side without piling them deeply. Put salmon in the center and asparagus alongside, using a second tray if needed to prevent overlap. Spoon garlic butter over salmon and asparagus. For very thin asparagus, add it about 5 minutes after the salmon instead.

Finish independently: Roast about 10–15 minutes, checking fish at 10 minutes. Measure the thickest center of each salmon portion from the side for 145°F / 63°C. Check that potatoes are fully tender and asparagus has the bite you like. Lift each finished component to a clean plate while the rest continues; do not leave fish baking solely for the potatoes.
Serve: Divide salmon, potatoes and asparagus among the plates. Spoon over pan butter and scatter with parsley. This includes its own starch and green vegetable; an additional salad is optional.
