recipes.name: Jeri's Lentil Soup
recipes.description: This traditional recipe was a wedding gift from Pat Miller and Sean Kilpatrick, passed down from Jeri, a Broadway dancer turned nutritionist. Adding sherry vinegar at the end brightens earthy lentils - the acidity wakes up the palate.
recipeIngredient: 16 oz Dry Green or Brown Lentils, rinsed
1 tbsp Sherry Vinegar or Fresh Lemon Juice
Salt and Black Pepper to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Sauté: Heat oil in a large skillet. Sauté onions and carrots with the Italian seasoning for 5-8 minutes until translucent.
The Pot: Transfer the vegetables to a slow cooker. Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, and broth.
Slow Cook: Cook on LOW for 5 hours (or on high for 3 hours) until lentils are tender but not mushy.
Infuse: Stir in the white wine and parsley. Cook for another 30 minutes.
Texture (Optional): Use an immersion blender to pulse the soup a few times to create a thicker body.
The Acid Balance: Stir in the sherry vinegar or lemon juice. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, rich, herbaceous, comfort-food, meal-prep, weeknight, saute, slow-cook, blend

recipes.name: Jerk Pork Shoulder
recipes.description: Jerk-seasoned pork shoulder with allspice, thyme, hot chile and citrus, braised until it shreds. A clean, separately refrigerated portion of marinade provides the fresh finish.
recipeIngredient: 6 scallions, roughly chopped, white and green parts
1–2 Scotch bonnet or habanero peppers, stemmed; remove seeds and membranes for less heat
2 tbsp fresh thyme leaves or 2 tsp dried thyme
Hot water, only if needed to prevent the braise drying out

recipeInstructions.text: Blend and reserve: Blend all marinade ingredients until mostly smooth. Before handling the pork, measure 1/4 cup into a clean covered container, label it for finishing and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or colder.
Marinate: Score the pork about 1/4 inch deep. Coat it with the remaining marinade, cover and refrigerate for 8–24 hours. Keep the clean finishing portion in its separate container.
Heat the oven: Heat to 325°F / 165°C. Keep the pork refrigerated until ready to sear; it does not need to reach room temperature.

Sear: Scrape excess marinade from the pork into a bowl reserved for the braise. Heat the Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the pork, turning to brown its broad surfaces, about 3–4 minutes per side. Lower the heat if the sugary coating starts to blacken.

Braise: Add the scraped raw-contact marinade, stock and orange juice around the pork. Cover and cook in the oven about 3–3 1/2 hours, until a fork easily separates the meat. Check that liquid remains; add a little hot water if needed. The thickest part must reach at least 145°F / 63°C, but shreddable tenderness requires further cooking. Continue covered if still firm.

Rest and reduce: Move the pork to a board and rest for 20 minutes. During the rest, skim fat from the braising liquid and simmer it uncovered until glossy but still pourable, about 10 minutes. The rest also exceeds the 3-minute minimum after reaching the pork safety temperature.

Shred and finish: Shred the meat, discarding large pockets of fat. Toss with the reduced sauce and the clean 1/4 cup marinade reserved before raw contact. Do not use any unbraised scraped marinade here.

Serve or reheat: Serve in eight portions, or cool promptly for later meals. To reheat, spread pork and sauce in a covered baking dish at 325°F / 165°C until the center reaches 165°F / 74°C. Start checking after 20–25 minutes; a cold, deep dish takes longer.

recipes.name: Kachumber Salad
recipes.description: Small-diced cucumber, tomato, and onion with lemon, fresh herbs, and toasted cumin, dressed just before serving.
recipeIngredient: 300 g cucumber, washed and cut into 1/4-inch dice
250 g firm ripe tomatoes, cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus more only if needed
1/4 tsp chaat masala, optional; check ingredients for dietary needs

recipeInstructions.text: Toast and cool cumin: Shake cumin seeds in a small dry skillet over medium-low heat for about 1–2 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker. Transfer to a plate, cool briefly, and crush with a mortar or the back of a spoon.

Cut vegetables: Dice cucumber and tomato into roughly 1/4-inch pieces and cut onion more finely. Remove tough cucumber skin or large watery seed cores as needed. Mince optional serrano; omit it for a milder salad. Combine vegetables with cilantro and mint.

Mix dressing: Stir lemon juice, cooled crushed cumin, measured salt, pepper, optional olive oil, and optional chaat masala together. If not serving yet, refrigerate vegetables and dressing separately.
Dress at serving: Toss gently with dressing. Taste a spoonful and add a little extra lemon only if the vegetables need more acidity. Divide into six small side portions and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Kalbi
recipes.description: Kalbi is Korean barbecue short ribs. The secret to tender meat with crisp edges is rubbing the ribs with sake and sugar for 15 minutes before adding the soy sauce.
recipeIngredient: 5 lbs Flanken-style Beef Short Ribs (1/2-inch thick)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Let the cooked ribs rest for 5 minutes before cutting and serving.

itemListElement.text: The Prep: Rinse the ribs in cold water to remove any bone fragments. Pat bone-dry with paper towels.
The Tenderizer: In a large bowl, toss the ribs with the sake and white sugar. Massage the mixture into the meat and let stand for 15 minutes.
The Marinade: In a separate jar, whisk together the soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, scallions, pepper, and oil until the sugar is dissolved.
The Soak: Pour the marinade over the ribs. Ensure every slice is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours (overnight is mandatory for the Kitchen Standard).
Thermal Prep: Bring the ribs to room temperature for 30 minutes before cooking. Discard the marinade.

The Sear: Light a charcoal grill to medium-high heat. Wipe off excess marinade from the ribs to prevent the sugars from burning, then place directly over the coals. Grill for 2-3 minutes per side until seared and charred.
Finish: Move to the cooler side of the grill for 5 minutes until the fat is rendered and "Snappy."
Serve: Use kitchen shears to cut the ribs into bite-sized pieces.

recipes.name: Kale Caesar with Crispy Chickpeas
recipes.description: This Caesar replaces the traditional breadcrumbs and anchovies with crispy roasted chickpeas that add both crunch and plant-based protein. The massage is critical - working salt and a bit of oil into the shredded kale breaks down the tough fibers, transforming them into something tender and sweet.
recipeIngredient: 1 large bunch Lacinato (Dino) Kale, stems removed and shredded
1 can (15 oz) Chickpeas, drained and patted very dry
1 tsp White Miso or Soy Sauce
1/4 tsp Anchovy Paste (optional, for traditional Caesar depth)
1/3 cup Shaved or Grated Parmesan Cheese

recipeInstructions.text: Roast the Chickpeas: Preheat oven to 425°F. Pat the drained chickpeas very dry with a clean kitchen towel - any moisture will prevent them from crisping. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, paprika, garlic powder, and pepper on a sheet pan. Spread in a single layer and roast for 20-25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until golden and crispy. Set aside to cool - they will continue to crisp as they cool.

Massage the Kale: Place the shredded kale in a large bowl. Drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Using your hands, massage the leaves vigorously for 2 minutes until they turn dark green and soften significantly. This breaks down the cell walls and makes the kale tender.

Make the Dressing: In a blender or small food processor, combine the 1/4 cup olive oil, grated garlic, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, miso (or soy sauce), anchovy paste if using, water, salt, and pepper. Blend until completely smooth. The dressing should have the consistency of heavy cream. Adjust water if needed.
Toss: Pour the dressing over the massaged kale and toss well to ensure every leaf is evenly coated.
Assemble: Top with the crispy roasted chickpeas, shaved Parmesan, and a light dusting of lemon zest.
Rest: Let the salad sit for 5 minutes before serving. Unlike delicate greens, kale actually improves as it absorbs the dressing - it doesn't wilt.

Make-Ahead: The crispy chickpeas can be made up to 2 days ahead and stored in an airtight container. The dressing keeps refrigerated for up to 3 days. Massage the kale and dress it just before serving for the best texture.

recipes.name: Kale Salad with Mango, Avocado and Feta
recipes.description: Chopped kale with mango, avocado, feta and toasted seeds in an orange, honey and olive-oil dressing.
recipeIngredient: 1 bunch curly kale, tough ribs removed, leaves washed, dried and finely chopped
1 large ripe but firm mango, peeled, pitted and cubed
1 large ripe avocado, peeled, pitted and diced
1/2 cup toasted hulled pumpkin seeds or sunflower seeds
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for softening kale
3 tbsp + 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil, for dressing
Salt and black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare kale: Remove tough ribs, wash leaves, dry thoroughly and chop finely. Put in a wide bowl and add the oil labeled for softening kale with a small pinch of salt. Rub gently for about 1–2 minutes until darker and more flexible, stopping before the leaves become wet and limp.

Prepare fruit and dressing: Peel, pit and cube mango. Finely dice onion and crumble feta. Zest and juice the orange; whisk its juice and zest with the oil labeled for dressing, garlic, Dijon and honey. Taste and add salt and pepper as needed.

Combine gradually: Toss kale with about half the dressing, then gently fold in mango, onion and feta. Taste a leaf with fruit and cheese. Add more dressing only if needed for a light coating and reserve the rest.
Finish: Dice avocado just before serving and fold it in gently. Scatter with toasted seeds, divide among side plates and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Katharine Hepburn’s Brownies
recipes.description: This is the classic Katharine Hepburn brownie recipe. The secret to its fudgy texture is the ultra-low flour ratio: using only 1/4 cup of flour ensures the structure remains gooey and fudge-like rather than cakey.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Walnuts or Pecans, coarsely chopped

recipeInstructions.text: The Bloom: Preheat oven to 325°F. Grease an 8x8-inch square pan. In a medium saucepan, melt the butter over low heat. Whisk in the cocoa powder until smooth and glossy. Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes.
Emulsify: Whisk the eggs into the cocoa-butter mixture one at a time. Stir in the vanilla and salt.
The Fold: In a separate bowl, whisk the sugar and flour. Add the dry mix and the nuts to the saucepan. Stir with a spatula until just combined.
Bake: Pour the batter into the prepared pan. Bake for 30-35 minutes. The Kitchen Standard Test: The center should still have a slight jiggle and a toothpick should come out with moist crumbs.
Cool: Let cool completely in the pan before slicing. These brownies are elite when refrigerated and eaten cold.

recipes.name: Keto Egg Muffins
recipes.description: These are ideal for high-protein, low-carb meal prep. The secret to avoiding the rubbery sponginess of many egg muffins is placing the raw chorizo at the bottom of the tin so it renders its spicy fat directly into the egg, creating a crispy finish on the bottom.
recipeIngredient: 5 oz Spanish Chorizo or Salami, finely diced

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Generously grease a 12-cup muffin tin with butter (do not use paper liners, as the eggs will stick).
The Base: Divide the diced chorizo and scallions evenly among the 12 muffin cups.
Aeration: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs with the pesto, salt, and pepper until very frothy and well-integrated.
Fold: Stir in 3/4 of the shredded cheese.
Fill: Pour the egg mixture into the muffin cups, filling each about 3/4 full. Sprinkle the remaining cheese over the tops for a golden "Bounce."
Bake: Bake for 15-20 minutes until the centers are set and the tops are slightly golden.
Serve: Let cool for 5 minutes before popping them out with a knife.

recipes.name: Key Lime Pie Ice Cream
recipes.description: This frozen dessert mimics the exact flavor profile of our Key Lime Pie. The secret to a smooth, professional churn is the condensed milk: the sugar and fats act as a powerful stabilizer, preventing the formation of large ice crystals and ensuring a silky texture.
recipeIngredient: 1 can (14 oz) Fat-free Sweetened Condensed Milk
1/2 cup Fresh Key Lime Juice (Nellie & Joe’s is the Kitchen Standard)

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: In a large bowl, whisk together the condensed milk, key lime juice, 2% milk, cream, and salt until perfectly smooth.
The Churn: Pour the mixture into your ice cream maker. Churn according to the manufacturer's instructions (usually 20-25 minutes).
The Crunch: During the last 2 minutes of churning, add 1/3 cup of the coarsely crushed graham crackers.
The Finish: Transfer the soft-serve consistency ice cream to a chilled, freezer-safe container. Cover and freeze for at least 4 hours (ideally overnight) to firm up.
Serve: Scoop into bowls. Top with the remaining reserved graham cracker crumbs and a fresh lime wedge for the mandatory Acid Balance.

recipes.name: Key Lime Pie
recipes.description: This is classic Key lime pie for the holiday table. The key to its texture is whisking the egg yolks into the condensed milk before adding the lime juice.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup + 2 tbsp Fresh Key Lime Juice

recipeInstructions.text: The Crust: Preheat oven to 350°F. Stir together crumbs, sugar, and melted butter until it looks like wet sand. Press firmly into the bottom and up the sides of a 9-inch glass pie plate. Bake for 10 minutes. Let cool.
The Emulsion: In a large bowl, whisk the condensed milk and egg yolks until pale and thick.
The Bind: Slowly whisk in the key lime juice - the mixture will noticeably thicken.
Bake: Pour the filling into the cooled crust. Begin checking after 15 minutes and continue until the center reaches 160°F / 71°C, with set edges and a slight central wobble.
The Finish: Cool completely on a rack, then refrigerate for at least 8 hours (mandatory).
The Crown: Just before serving, whip the heavy cream and powdered sugar until stiff peaks form.
Serve: Mound the cream over the pie. Garnish with lime zest for the final aromatic High Note.

recipes.name: Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
recipes.description: Kimchi jjigae is Korean comfort food in its rawest form - kimchi is already fermented and pungent, so when you braise it with pork in stock, it becomes even more funky and complex. This is not a refined dish; it's what Korean mothers make on cold nights when they have leftover kimchi and want something warming and bold.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups Kimchi, coarsely chopped (plus 2 tbsp kimchi juice)
8 oz Pork Belly or Shoulder, thinly sliced (or tofu for vegetarian)
4 oz Mushrooms, sliced (shiitake, oyster, or cremini)
2 tbsp Doenjang (Korean soybean paste, optional but recommended)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description:
Kimchi Quality: Use kimchi that's at least a few days old - the older and funkier the better. Store-bought kimchi is fine; homemade is better.

Pork Options: Pork belly is traditional because it becomes tender and adds richness. But pork shoulder, beef, or tofu all work.

Heat Level: Gochugaru and gochujang can be intense. Start with the amounts listed and taste before adding more. You can always add heat; you can't take it out.

Doenjang Note: Doenjang (soybean paste) adds deep umami and is traditional but optional. If using, dissolve it in a bit of stock before adding to avoid lumps.

Make-Ahead: Kimchi jjigae tastes better the next day as flavors deepen. Store in the refrigerator for up to 4 days and reheat gently.

itemListElement.text: Prepare Ingredients: Chop the kimchi into roughly 1-inch pieces, reserving 2 tbsp of the brine. Slice the pork belly thinly (it will cook fast). Slice the onion and mushrooms. Mince the garlic.
Heat the Pan: Place a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add 1 tbsp vegetable oil and let it get hot.

Cook the Pork: Add the sliced pork and let it sit for 1-2 minutes without stirring to develop color. Stir and cook another 1-2 minutes until the pork is mostly opaque. Don't fully cook it - it will finish cooking in the braise.
Add Aromatics: Add the minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the sliced onion and mushrooms, cooking for 2 minutes until they begin to soften.

Build the Flavor Base: Add the gochugaru and gochujang, stirring quickly so they coat the vegetables and heat in the hot pan (about 30 seconds). This blooms the chili flavors. If using doenjang, add it now.
Add Kimchi: Add the chopped kimchi and stir everything together. Cook for 2 minutes so the kimchi heats through and releases its pungent aroma.

Braise: Add the stock and kimchi brine, stirring well. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Once simmering, reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 12-15 minutes so the flavors meld and the pork becomes tender. The liquid should reduce slightly and taste deeply savory and spicy.

Taste and Season: Taste carefully. Add fish sauce for more umami, sugar to balance heat and salt, or gochugaru if you want more spice. The balance should feel bold but balanced - no single flavor should overwhelm.
Finish: Drizzle with 1 tbsp sesame oil. Remove from heat.
Serve: Ladle into individual bowls over warm rice. Garnish with chopped green onions and sesame seeds. Serve with kimchi on the side and extra rice.

recipes.keywords: Korean, spicy, savory, umami, complex, weeknight, comfort-food, entertaining, simmer, braise

recipes.name: Gochujang-Glazed Oven Wings
recipes.description: Rack-roasted wings with a thin gochujang, honey and sesame glaze added just before serving.
recipeIngredient: 1.35 kg (3 lb) chicken wing drumettes and flats, fully thawed, tips excluded
1 tbsp aluminum-free baking powder, not baking soda
2 tsp neutral oil, for lightly greasing the racks

recipeInstructions.text: Dry and season: Pat fully thawed drumettes and flats dry. Lightly oil two oven-safe racks and set them over rimmed trays. Toss wings thoroughly with the baking powder and salt so there are no concentrated powder patches.

Refrigerate to dry: Arrange in a single spaced layer on the racks. Refrigerate uncovered for 8–24 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below, on a low shelf with the trays containing drips. Include this time within the usual 1–2-day refrigerated raw-poultry storage window.

Roast and check: During the last 15 minutes of refrigerated drying, heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Roast about 25 minutes, then turn wings and swap tray positions. Roast another 20–30 minutes, checking until skin is browned and several large pieces reach at least 165°F / 74°C away from bone. Around 175°F / 79°C is a useful tenderness target for wings. Remove smaller finished pieces earlier if necessary.

Make glaze: During roasting, combine gochujang, honey, soy, vinegar, water, garlic and ginger in a small saucepan. Simmer gently about 3–4 minutes, stirring, until garlic smells mellow and the glaze flows from a spoon. Turn off heat and stir in sesame oil. Keep warm; do not reduce to a stiff paste.

Coat at service: Put cooked wings in a clean bowl and toss with about two-thirds of the glaze. Add more only if needed for a thin coating; reserve the rest in a separate serving bowl. Do not broil the honey-coated wings or coat them repeatedly for a long hold.

Serve: Finish with scallions, sesame seeds and optional measured gochugaru. Divide into four main portions with separately prepared rice and cucumbers, or offer eight smaller appetizer portions. The 1.35 kg weight includes bones, not that much edible meat.

recipes.keywords: Korean-American, savory, sweet, spicy, umami, entertaining, game-day, roast, simmer

recipes.name: Sukju Namul
recipes.description: Seasoned mung bean sprouts are a Korean side dish served at almost every meal - tender, nutty, and finished with sesame oil and toasted sesame seeds. The bean sprouts cook just until tender but still have a slight crunch.

recipeInstructions.text: Thermal Prep: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 1 tsp salt. Prepare an ice-water bath.
Blanch: Rinse sprouts in cold water. Add to boiling water and cook for 1-2 minutes until just translucent but still firm.
Shock: Drain immediately and submerge in the ice water for 2 minutes to stop the cooking.
The Squeeze: Squeeze the cold sprouts with your hands until no more liquid drips out. They should feel like a dense, dry mass.
Toss: In a large bowl, whisk the scallion, garlic, salt, and sesame oil. Separate the sprouts and toss vigorously with the dressing and sesame seeds.
Serve: Best served chilled or at room temperature.

recipes.keywords: Korean, savory, weeknight, light-and-fresh, boil

recipes.name: Oi Muchim (Korean Cucumber Salad)
recipes.description: Sliced cucumbers tossed with gochugaru, garlic, sesame, and a sharp-sweet dressing. A brief salt-and-drain step limits dilution.
recipeIngredient: 600 g English or Persian cucumbers, ends trimmed
1 tbsp gochugaru (Korean red chile flakes), or less to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Slice: Wash cucumbers and cut into rounds about 1/4 inch thick. If an English cucumber is very wide, halve it lengthwise first and slice into half-moons.

Salt and drain: Toss with the measured salt in a colander over a bowl. Leave for 20 minutes, tossing once halfway through. Discard the drained liquid and gently blot the slices with a clean towel; do not wring them dry. Taste a slice: if unusually salty, rinse briefly, drain, and blot again.
Mix dressing: During the wait, combine gochugaru, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, and garlic in a serving bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves.

Toss and serve: Add drained cucumbers, scallions, and sesame seeds. Toss gently and serve promptly. If using as a noodle-salad topping, lift portions out with a slotted spoon so excess dressing does not flood the noodles.

recipes.name: Korean Style Tacos
recipes.description: These Korean-Mexican fusion tacos were popularized by LA's Kogi BBQ truck in 2008, combining Korean gochujang-based sauce with traditional Mexican tortillas. The sauce whisks together gochujang, sesame oil, soy sauce, and sugar into a sweet-spicy glaze.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Cooked [Pulled Pork](/mise/recipes/pulled-pork) or Shredded Chicken

recipeInstructions.text: The Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together the Gochujang, sugar, soy sauce, vinegar, and sesame oil until smooth. Set aside.
The Pickle: In a separate bowl, toss cucumber slices with vinegar, sugar, chili, and salt. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour (but no more than 3) to maintain the "Snap."
The Sear: Heat a large skillet over high heat. Add the cooked pork or chicken and 1/4 cup of the Kogi sauce. Toss vigorously for 3-4 minutes until the edges are crispy and the meat is lacquered.
Toast: Warm the tortillas over an open flame or in a dry pan until charred in spots.
Assemble: Place a generous scoop of the glazed meat into each tortilla.
Finish: Top with a pile of the chilled cucumber pickles and extra scallions. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Lamb Keema Matar
recipes.description: The secret to a great Keema is Deep Browning. You must sear the ground lamb until it develops a dark, savory crust before adding the aromatics.

recipeInstructions.text: Sear: Heat a large skillet over high heat. Add the lamb and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until deeply browned and slightly crispy.
Aromatics: Add the diced onion to the lamb fat. Cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the ginger and garlic and sauté for 30-45 seconds.
Bloom: Add the cumin seeds, turmeric, chili, and tomato paste. Stir constantly for 1 minute until fragrant.
Simmer: Add a splash of water (about 1/4 cup) to keep it saucy. Stir in the frozen peas. Cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Finish: Stir in the Garam Masala, lemon juice, and cilantro.
Serve: Serve with warm Naan or over rice.

recipes.name: Lavender London Fog Cocktail
recipes.description: A chilled Earl Grey and gin cocktail with oat milk, vanilla and a restrained hint of lavender, shaken and served in a coupe.
recipeIngredient: 2 oz (60 mL) Earl Grey concentrate, thoroughly chilled (from the batch below)
1/2 oz (15 mL) plain barista-style oat milk, chilled and shaken in its carton; preferably unsweetened
1/2 oz (15 mL) lavender–vanilla syrup, chilled (from the batch below)
Solid ice cubes, enough to fill the shaker
4 g loose Earl Grey black tea
120 mL water at 95°C / 203°F, plus enough to restore the strained tea to 120 mL

recipeInstructions.text: Brew the concentrate: Steep the 4 g Earl Grey tea in 120 mL water at 95°C / 203°F for 4 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh strainer, then add enough water to bring the strained tea back to 120 mL. This makes two 60 mL cocktail portions.

Make the syrup: Stir the 60 g sugar into 60 g hot water until dissolved. Off the heat, add the culinary lavender and steep for 3 minutes. Strain finely, then stir in the vanilla extract. Expect approximately 90–100 mL syrup, enough for about six cocktails after straining losses.
Chill: Transfer the tea and syrup to separate clean containers and refrigerate until thoroughly cold, allowing about 1 hour, or longer as needed. Chill a 7 oz coupe glass before mixing.

Measure one cocktail: Shake the oat milk carton. Add 1 1/2 oz (45 mL) gin, 2 oz (60 mL) cold tea concentrate, 1/2 oz (15 mL) oat milk and 1/2 oz (15 mL) cold syrup to the shaker. The remaining tea and syrup are for additional cocktails; do not add the whole batches.

Shake and strain: Fill the shaker with solid ice cubes and shake firmly for 10–12 seconds, until the shaker is very cold and often frosted. Strain through both the cocktail strainer and a fine-mesh strainer into the chilled coupe. Look for a lightly cloudy tea-beige drink with fine bubbles on the surface; the amount of foam depends on the oat milk.
Serve: Serve immediately, without ice or garnish. Taste before increasing lavender in a future syrup batch; the bergamot should remain clear.

recipes.name: Lemon Basil Shrimp Risotto
recipes.description: Risotto originated in Northern Italy (Milan and the Veneto) where short-grain rice has been grown since the 15th century. The technique requires patience - adding hot broth one ladle at a time and stirring constantly releases the rice's starch (amylopectin), which creates the signature creamy texture without needing excessive butter or cream.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lbs Large Shrimp (U10), peeled and deveined
5-6 cups Chicken or Vegetable Broth, heated

recipeInstructions.text: The Crunch: In a large wide skillet, melt butter over medium-high. Add shrimp in a single layer. Sear for 2 minutes per side until just opaque. Remove to a plate.
Foundation: In the same pan, add onions and sauté for 2-3 minutes until translucent. Add garlic and sauté for 30-45 seconds.
Toast: Add the Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes until the edges of the grains look translucent (The Toast Method).
Deglaze: Pour in the wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
The Bind: Add the hot broth one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until each ladle is fully absorbed before adding the next. This will take 18-22 minutes.
The Texture: Once the rice is al dente, stir in the heavy cream, Parmesan, lemon juice, and zest.
Combine: Fold the seared shrimp and fresh basil into the risotto. Toss for 1 minute until the shrimp are warmed through.
Serve: Garnish with extra basil and a "High Note" crack of black pepper.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, umami, rich, herbaceous, date-night, entertaining, weekend-project, saute

recipes.name: Lemon Broccoli Tortellini
recipes.description: Cheese tortellini with roasted broccoli, wilted spinach and a lemon-butter finish.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb refrigerated or frozen cheese tortellini
1 1/2 lb fresh broccoli, cut into similar bite-sized florets, thick stems sliced thinner
4 cloves garlic, minced, divided equally between broccoli and sauce
1 large lemon, zested before juicing, juice divided between broccoli and finish
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1/2 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from Two Peas & Their Pod’s Lemon Broccoli Tortellini.

itemListElement.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Cut broccoli into similar bite-sized florets and slice thick stems thinner. Mince shallot and garlic, zest then juice the lemon, and set a large pot of water on to boil.

Roast broccoli: Toss broccoli with olive oil, half the garlic and half the lemon juice, salt and pepper. Spread on a rimmed half-sheet pan in one layer, using a second tray if crowded. Keep garlic among the florets rather than scattered on bare metal. Roast 20–25 minutes, turning once, until stems are tender and edges browned. Remove any pieces that finish early.

Start the sauce: Near the end of roasting, melt butter in a large deep skillet over medium-low. Soften shallot for about 3–5 minutes. Add the remaining garlic and pepper flakes for 30–45 seconds, then spinach. Turn gently for about 2 minutes until wilted. Lower heat or turn it off while waiting for pasta.

Cook tortellini: Time this stage by the package so it finishes near the vegetables. Season the boiling water moderately, add tortellini and cook as directed, avoiding a violent boil. Meet any specified filling temperature. Reserve the listed amount of cooking water before draining.

Combine gently: Add drained tortellini and broccoli to the spinach skillet. Add zest and about half the reserved water. Fold over low heat just until hot, then remove from the burner. Add Parmesan gradually and half of the remaining lemon juice. Fold gently, adding further water only until lightly coated. Taste before adding the rest of the lemon juice, salt or pepper. Serve promptly.

recipes.name: Lemon Chicken Orzo Soup
recipes.description: Diced chicken and small pasta in a lightly thickened vegetable broth, finished with lemon zest, juice and parsley.
recipeIngredient: 680 g boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
1 1/2 cups (360 ml) additional chicken broth, only as needed to loosen
1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
3 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually to taste
Water, only for the optional separate-orzo make-ahead method, per pasta package

recipeInstructions.text: Soften vegetables: Heat butter and oil in a 5-quart pot over medium heat. Add onion, small carrot and celery pieces, and pepper. Cook about 7–9 minutes, stirring, until the vegetables soften; deep browning is not required.

Disperse flour: Add garlic and thyme and stir about 30 seconds. Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute. Add the initial 6 cups broth gradually, stirring to prevent flour clumps and loosen any brown residue.
Heat and add chicken: Bring to a steady simmer. Add diced chicken, stir to separate pieces, and return to a simmer. Keep the extra broth separate for later adjustment.

Cook orzo and check: Add orzo and simmer gently about 10–12 minutes, stirring across the bottom frequently. Check that pasta is just tender and several thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Extend if needed, lifting cooked chicken out briefly if the pasta needs significantly longer.

Set consistency and season: Add additional broth in small amounts if needed for a spoonable soup and return to a gentle simmer. Taste and add salt gradually only if needed. Turn off heat, add parsley, lemon zest and half the juice, then taste before adding the remainder.
Serve: Divide among six bowls and serve promptly. For making ahead, cook the orzo separately in boiling water according to its package and add it to each serving; keep it separate from stored soup.

recipes.name: Lemon-Garlic Broccolini
recipes.description: Italian cooks know the rule: bright greens stay bright only if cooked hot and fast. Broccolini (which is less sulfurous than broccoli) sautés in under 5 minutes over high heat with just garlic, oil, and lemon.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Zest the lemon and set zest aside. Cut the lemon into wedges for serving.
Heat: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add thinly sliced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté for 30-45 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add Broccolini: Add the broccolini to the pan and toss constantly for 3-4 minutes until the stems are tender-crisp and some leaves are slightly browned. Season with salt and a pinch of black pepper.
Brightness: Squeeze half the lemon juice over the broccolini and toss once more. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Finish: Transfer to a serving dish. Garnish with lemon zest and serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, herbaceous, bright, weeknight, quick-lunch, saute

recipes.name: Lemon and Herb Instant Couscous
recipes.description: Fine instant couscous hydrated off heat and finished with lemon, olive oil, parsley and mint.
recipeIngredient: 250 g plain instant couscous; not pearl couscous
420 ml low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth, adjusted to the chosen package instructions
2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, divided and partly added to taste
1/4 tsp fine salt, added only as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and heat: Chop parsley and mint, grate lemon zest and measure the juice. Check the package’s liquid guidance for the measured couscous quantity; use the listed broth amount for the starting formula. Bring the broth to a full boil in a 2-quart saucepan.
Hydrate off heat: Remove from heat, stir in couscous, and cover immediately. Let stand about 5 minutes, or the package’s stated time. Keep the lid on during this initial rest.

Check and fluff: Uncover and taste a grain. It should be tender without a dry center and there should be no free liquid. If still dry, use the small hot-water correction in troubleshooting. Fluff with a fork, lifting rather than pressing.

Dress: Fold in olive oil, half the measured lemon juice, zest and pepper. Let excess steam escape for a minute, then fold in parsley and mint. Taste before adding the remaining lemon juice and measured salt; broth and optional feta may already supply enough salt.
Serve: Divide into four sides and add the optional feta. Pair with a main and vegetables; the couscous is the starch component of the plate.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean-inspired, herbaceous, acidic, savory, weeknight, meal-prep, entertaining, boil, steam

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Quinoa
recipes.description: Tender quinoa with lemon, olive oil, parsley, mint and dill. A covered rest separates cooking from dressing, so the grains stay light and the herbs taste fresh.
recipeIngredient: 2.5 cups water or low-sodium vegetable broth, plus hot water as needed if the grains remain firm

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and drain: Rinse the dry quinoa in a fine-mesh strainer under cool running water for about 30 seconds, then shake and drain thoroughly. Follow any specific preparation directions on the package.

Toast, if wanted: Put the drained quinoa in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir until excess surface water has evaporated and the grains smell lightly nutty, about 2 minutes or a little longer if still wet. Skip this step for a milder flavor.

Simmer and check: Add the measured water or broth and salt. Bring to a boil, cover tightly and lower the heat to a gentle simmer. Cook about 15 minutes without repeatedly lifting the lid. Taste a grain and check for pooled liquid; the grain should be tender without a hard center. If firm and dry, add a little hot water and continue covered. If firm with liquid remaining, continue simmering without adding more.
Rest: When the grain is tender and free liquid has absorbed, remove from heat and leave covered for 5 minutes.

Dress: Fluff gently with a fork. Add olive oil and measured lemon juice, then fold in zest, parsley, mint, dill and black pepper. Taste before adding any more salt. Divide into four generous side portions; serve warm, or cool promptly for a chilled serving.

recipes.keywords: American, Mediterranean, acidic, herbaceous, fresh, savory, weeknight, meal-prep, light-and-fresh, boil, simmer

recipes.name: Lemon-Miso Tofu with Broccoli
recipes.description: Miso-glazed tofu is a Japanese izakaya staple adapted for weeknight cooking - the miso-lemon-maple glaze hits all five taste receptors at once (salt, sweet, acid, umami, and a touch of bitter from the char). The key is pressing the tofu bone-dry and dredging in cornstarch before frying - this creates the shatteringly crisp shell that holds the glaze without going soggy.
recipeIngredient: 14 oz Extra-firm Tofu, pressed dry and cubed
1 lb Fresh Broccoli, cut into small florets

recipeInstructions.text: The Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk miso, lemon juice, maple syrup, 1 tbsp cornstarch, and hot water until smooth.
The Crunch: Toss dry tofu cubes in 1/3 cup cornstarch, salt, and pepper until "dusty."
Sear Tofu: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Fry tofu for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and very crisp. Remove to a plate.
Sear Veg: In the same pan, sauté broccoli for 6-7 minutes until tender and charred at the edges. Remove and set aside.
The Glaze: Wipe the pan. Add sesame oil, garlic, and ginger; sauté for 30 seconds. Pour in the miso-lemon mixture. Simmer for 3 minutes until thick and glossy.
Bind: Return tofu and broccoli to the pan. Toss vigorously for 30 seconds to coat.
Serve: Garnish with scallions and serve hot over rice.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, fry, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Lemon Pepper Oven Wings
recipes.description: Dry-roasted wings tossed lightly with lemon-zest butter, coarse pepper and a measured splash of juice.
recipeIngredient: 1.35 kg (3 lb) chicken wing drumettes and flats, fully thawed, tips excluded
1 tbsp aluminum-free baking powder, not baking soda
2 tsp neutral oil, for lightly greasing the racks
1 tbsp finely grated lemon zest, yellow part only
1/8 tsp fine salt, only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Pat thawed wings dry. Lightly oil two oven-safe racks and place over rimmed trays. Toss wings evenly with baking powder and the wings' measured salt; avoid clumps. Spread them out with space between pieces.

Dry in the refrigerator: Refrigerate uncovered for 8–24 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below, on a low shelf with trays catching any drips. Count this within the 1–2-day raw-poultry refrigerated storage window.

Roast: During the last 15 minutes of refrigerated drying, heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Roast about 25 minutes, turn wings and exchange tray positions, then roast another 20–30 minutes. Check several large pieces away from bone: all need at least 165°F / 74°C, with about 175°F / 79°C a useful tenderness target. Skin should be browned and rendered. Remove smaller done pieces if needed while larger ones finish.

Warm the butter: Near the end of roasting, melt butter gently in a small saucepan over low heat. Remove from heat and stir in zest, juice, pepper and garlic powder. Taste and add the butter's optional salt only if needed. Whisk before using; a little separation is normal.

Toss lightly: Transfer cooked wings to a clean bowl. Add about two-thirds of the warm butter mixture and toss. Add the rest only if needed for an even light coating, or serve it separately. Keep the wings uncovered and serve promptly rather than holding them in a pool of butter.

Finish: Scatter with the measured parsley and serve optional lemon wedges. Divide into four main portions with separately prepared sides, or eight smaller appetizer portions. Bones are included in the purchase weight.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, acidic, peppery, entertaining, game-day, roast

recipes.name: Lemon Ricotta Pasta
recipes.description: A generous olive-oil and ricotta sauce with Pecorino, lemon and basil, tossed with hot pasta in a bowl.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, including any finishing drizzle
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from Delish’s Lemon Ricotta Pasta.

itemListElement.text: Start water and sauce: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and season moderately with salt; the Pecorino will also season the dish. Zest then juice the lemon. If you want a finishing drizzle, set aside a little of the measured oil first. In a large heatproof bowl, whisk ricotta, the remaining oil, Pecorino, zest, half the lemon juice and pepper flakes.

Cook to tenderness: Add pasta and stir as it softens. Follow package timing, tasting a strand near the end. Cook until tender with a little bite and no hard center. Before draining, scoop out the listed cooking-water reserve. Drain without rinsing.
Loosen the sauce: Whisk about one-quarter of the reserved water into the ricotta mixture. Add more a little at a time only if it is still too stiff to fold through the pasta.

Toss and finish: Add hot pasta to the bowl and toss thoroughly, adding further warm cooking water in small splashes until coated and slightly loose. Fold in basil and black pepper. Taste a complete bite, then add remaining lemon juice and salt only as needed. Use any oil deliberately reserved for finishing and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Lemony Broccoli Pasta
recipes.description: Spaghetti with broccoli and peas, coated in olive oil, Parmesan and fresh lemon.
recipeIngredient: 5 cups fresh broccoli florets, cut into small bite-sized pieces, thick stems sliced thinner
1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from The Kitchn’s Lemony Broccoli Pasta.

itemListElement.text: Prepare: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cut broccoli into small bite-sized florets and slice thick stems thinner. Zest and juice the lemon, grate Parmesan and measure the oil. Season the boiling water moderately with salt.

Cook pasta and broccoli: Add spaghetti and stir as it softens. Follow package timing. Add broccoli when about 3–5 minutes remain, return to a gentle boil and check both for tenderness. If pasta is ready first, lift it out with tongs and let broccoli finish. Before draining, reserve the listed cooking water; drain without rinsing.

Cook peas and prepare the finish: While pasta cooks, cook peas according to package directions and drain. In a large heatproof serving bowl, combine olive oil, lemon zest and half the lemon juice. Have Parmesan and warm cooking water ready.

Toss away from heat: Add hot spaghetti, broccoli and cooked peas to the bowl. Sprinkle in Parmesan in several additions while tossing, adding about one-quarter of the reserved water initially and more in small splashes only as needed. Stop when everything is coated and moist, not swimming in water.
Season and serve: Add black pepper and taste a complete bite. Add the remaining lemon juice and salt only as needed, then divide into the intended portions and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Lime & Honey Glazed Salmon
recipes.description: Lime-honey salmon with warm black beans, charred corn and peppers over fresh spinach, finished with cilantro and toasted pepitas.
recipeIngredient: 2.25 lb (about 1,020 g) skinless, boneless salmon, cut into seven similar portions
1 1/2 tsp mild chili powder blend, without added salt
1 tsp fine salt, divided, plus up to 1/4 tsp more for the salad after tasting
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the glaze
1 tsp olive oil, for the foil
5 medium ears fresh sweet corn, husked and kernels cut off; about 600 g kernels
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the skillet
1 medium red bell pepper, cored, seeded and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, optional, for the salad
2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, rinsed and well drained; about 500 g drained
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the salad, plus up to 1 tbsp more after tasting
8 loosely packed cups baby spinach, washed and dried; about 240 g
1 avocado, diced just before serving, optional
1 lime, cut into eight wedges for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare everything and heat the oven: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C with a middle rack and a second rack positioned so the fish surface will sit 7–9 inches below the broiler. Cut corn from the cobs, chop onion, pepper, garlic and cilantro, and rinse and drain beans. Prepare the spinach and measure the pepitas. Line the metal half-sheet pan with foil and spread its teaspoon of oil where the fish will sit. Pat salmon dry, check for pin bones and divide into seven similar portions. Season with chili powder, smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp salt and all the black pepper. Keep chilled while charring corn. Whisk honey with the 2 tbsp glaze lime juice in a clean bowl; set aside the separate salad juice and serving wedges. Wash raw-fish tools and hands before returning to vegetables.

Char corn in two batches: Heat the deep, well-seasoned skillet over medium-high heat for about 2–3 minutes. Add half the dry corn without oil and spread into a shallow layer. Let it sit briefly, then stir occasionally for about 5–7 minutes, until juicy and tender with scattered browned patches. Lower heat if it starts blackening. Transfer to a large bowl. Let the pan recover its heat and repeat with the remaining corn; remove any burnt loose residue afterward.

Start baking the fish: Arrange salmon on the prepared pan with about an inch between portions. Bake on the middle rack while making the salad in the next two steps. Start checking the fish after 8 minutes; allow roughly 10–15 minutes for the specified thickness, aiming for about 135–140°F / 57–60°C before the glaze finish. This is an intermediate temperature, not the serving endpoint. If ready before the salad, remove the pan briefly to a heatproof surface.

Soften the aromatics: Reduce skillet heat to medium and add the tablespoon of olive oil, onion, bell pepper and remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cook, stirring, about 6–8 minutes until the onion softens and pepper is tender with a little bite. Add garlic, the remaining 1 tsp cumin and optional red pepper flakes; stir 30–45 seconds until fragrant.

Warm and finish the salad: Fold the beans and all the corn into the skillet. Cook over medium heat for about 4–6 minutes, turning gently, until hot throughout. Remove from heat and fold in cilantro and the first tablespoon of salad lime juice. Taste and add some or all of the reserved lime and extra salt if wanted. Cover loosely and turn off the skillet before broiling.

Glaze and watch the broiler: Remove salmon from the oven if it is still inside and switch to high broil, allowing the element to heat according to the oven's instructions. Spread all the honey-lime mixture over the seven fillets in an even coating, without deliberately pooling it on the foil. Broil with the fish surface 7–9 inches below the heat for about 1–3 minutes, watching continuously; rotate the pan if needed. The glaze should bubble and develop golden patches without turning black. Check each fillet sideways in its thickest center and finish to 145°F / 63°C, with flesh that flakes under gentle pressure. If the glaze colors first, use the gentler oven finish in troubleshooting. Use clean utensils for serving and discard glaze left in the brushing bowl; it is not a cold sauce.

Serve seven complete portions: Divide all the spinach among seven wide bowls, then divide the warm bean-and-corn salad over it. Add one fillet per bowl. Dice the optional avocado and divide it among the bowls, then scatter the pepitas. Offer lime wedges for squeezing to taste. The spinach remains a fresh bed, lightly softened by the warm toppings.

recipes.name: Chicken Lo Mein with Shiitake and Bok Choy
recipes.description: Springy egg noodles with chicken, shiitake and bok choy, cooked in fragrant scallion-shallot oil in two manageable pan batches, with a separate shrimp variation.
recipeIngredient: 450 g (1 lb) fresh raw lo mein egg noodles, not dried noodles or pre-cooked noodles
450 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced across the grain about 1/4 inch thick
1 tsp neutral oil, for the chicken
1 tsp light soy sauce, for the chicken
1/8 tsp ground white pepper, for the chicken
1/4 cup (60 ml) low-sodium chicken broth or water
3 tbsp (45 ml) prepared strained scallion-shallot oil, divided (preferred; or shallot oil or neutral oil)
4 scallions, whites thinly sliced and greens cut into 1-inch lengths
225 g fresh shiitake caps, tough stems removed, sliced 1/4 inch thick
340 g baby bok choy, washed and thoroughly dried, stems and leaves separated
150 g mung bean sprouts, rinsed and drained
2 tsp toasted sesame oil, divided between finishing batches
1 tsp Chinkiang black vinegar or unseasoned rice vinegar, optional, divided between finishing batches
1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, only as needed to loosen noodles
15 g crisp fried shallots and scallions from the oil recipe, or prepared fried shallots, optional garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Coat the chicken and prepare the sauce: Toss chicken with its cornstarch, 1 tsp oil, 1 tsp light soy and white pepper; refrigerate while preparing everything else. Whisk the six sauce ingredients together and divide into two equal portions.

Set up the vegetables: Keep mushroom slices, bok choy stems, leaves, sprouts and scallion greens separate. Cut stems into 1/2-inch pieces and large leaves into manageable pieces. Mix garlic, ginger and scallion whites. Divide every vegetable and aromatic group, the Shaoxing wine, sesame oil and optional vinegar into two portions for the final rounds.

Prepare noodles for this product: Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a full boil. Add fresh raw noodles, separate gently and cook according to their package range, tasting early until cooked through but springy. Rinse briefly with cold water, drain thoroughly and toss with 1 tsp of the measured pan oil. Divide into two loose piles and proceed promptly; start the pan work as soon as the noodles are ready.

Cook the chicken fully in two batches: Heat the wok or deep skillet over medium-high to high as appropriate for the pan, then add 2 tsp pan oil. Spread half the chicken in a layer. Leave about 1 minute for color, then turn and stir for another 2–3 minutes or until the thickest slices reach 165°F / 74°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat with another 2 tsp oil and the remaining chicken. Keep the cooked chicken divided for the two finishing rounds.

Cook the first vegetable portion: Add 2 tsp of the remaining oil. Cook half the mushrooms 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until some surfaces brown. Add half the aromatics for 20–30 seconds, then half the wine and bok choy stems. Stir-fry about 2 minutes, adding a little measured hot water if needed for the stems to soften. Add half the leaves, sprouts and scallion greens and cook another 2–3 minutes, stirring, until thoroughly hot and cooked rather than raw-crisp.

Finish the first noodle batch: Add half the noodles and one portion of sauce. Fold from the bottom for about 1–2 minutes, using a little measured hot water only if needed to separate strands. Add half the cooked chicken and toss over the heat until everything is hot and evenly coated. Turn off the heat and fold in half the sesame oil and optional vinegar. Transfer to a warm serving platter and cover loosely for the short second round.

Repeat and serve: Use the last 2 tsp pan oil and the remaining vegetables, aromatics, wine, noodles, sauce and chicken to repeat steps 5–6. Finish with the remaining sesame oil and optional vinegar. Divide both batches among five bowls and add the optional 15 g crisp fried alliums from the oil recipe or prepared fried shallots. Serve promptly.

recipes.name: Omelet Muffins
recipes.description: These are ideal for breakfast meal prep. The secret to avoiding the rubbery, watery texture of most egg muffins is squeezing the thawed spinach in a towel until bone-dry before adding to the eggs.
recipeIngredient: 3 tbsp Frozen Spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray a 12-cup muffin tin generously with oil spray.
The Base: Divide the bacon, dry spinach, tomatoes, onions, and peppers evenly among the 12 cups.
Aeration: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, salt, and pepper until very frothy and no streaks remain.
Assemble: Pour the egg mixture into the cups, filling each about 3/4 full. Sprinkle the cheese over the tops.
Bake: Bake for 20-25 minutes until the centers are firm and the tops are slightly golden and puffed.
Store: Let cool for 5 minutes before removing. These can be frozen for up to 3 months and reheated in 45 seconds.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, meal-prep, quick-lunch, snack, bake, no-cook

recipes.name: Made-In-The-Pan Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: This cake is pure American efficiency - everything mixes right in the pan, no bowls to clean. The trick is understanding what each ingredient does: vinegar reacts with baking soda to create lift and crumb structure, cocoa powder needs cold water to bloom properly, and the whole formula relies on mixing order so ingredients emulsify correctly into a smooth, lump-free batter.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp Apple Cider Vinegar for richness

recipeInstructions.text: The Dry Mix: Preheat oven to 325°F. In an 8x8-inch square baking dish, whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, and salt until uniform. Use your fingers to crush any cocoa lumps.
The Wells: Make three wells in the dry mix. Pour the oil into one, the vanilla into the second, and the vinegar into the third.
Combine: Pour the cold water over everything. Using a fork or small whisk, stir in circular motions until a smooth batter forms. Scrape the corners of the pan carefully.
Bake: Sprinkle the chocolate chips over the top. Wipe the edges of the dish with a damp towel for a clean "Kitchen Standard" look.
Cook: Bake for 28-33 minutes until a toothpick comes out with just a few moist crumbs.
Finish: Dust with confectioners' sugar once cool for the mandatory High Note visual.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, weeknight, kid-friendly, comfort-food, quick-lunch, bake

recipes.name: Mandarin/Pineapple Orange Salad
recipes.description: Citrus salads are a Southern and Caribbean tradition - canned or fresh fruit with a bright dressing and sometimes nuts for crunch. The trick is draining fruit well so the salad doesn't turn watery.

recipeInstructions.text: Dissolve: In a large bowl, whisk the Orange Jello and sugar into the boiling water until no crystals remain.
Emulsify: Add the sour cream to the hot liquid. Whisk vigorously until the mixture is completely smooth and pale orange.
Texture: Fold in the crushed pineapple (with its juice) and the drained mandarin oranges.
The Finish: Pour the mixture into a glass bowl or a decorative mold.
Chill: Refrigerate for at least 4 hours (ideally overnight) until perfectly congealed and firm.
Serve: Serve chilled as a bright side dish or a light dessert.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, holiday, potluck, entertaining, boil

recipes.name: Mango Cabbage Slaw
recipes.description: Thin cabbage shreds, ripe mango, bell pepper and herbs in a lime-honey dressing with a pinch of allspice. A short chilled rest softens the cabbage just enough to bend while keeping its crunch.
recipeIngredient: 4 cups green cabbage, cored and very thinly shredded
2 cups red cabbage, cored and very thinly shredded
1 large ripe but firm mango, peeled and cut into matchsticks
1 red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and thinly sliced
3 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus more to taste
1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Core and thinly shred the cabbages, then measure them into a large bowl. Peel the mango and cut the flesh away from the pit into thin matchsticks. Prepare the bell pepper, onion, cilantro and scallions.
Whisk the dressing: Whisk the measured lime juice, oil, honey or agave, mustard, measured salt, pepper and allspice in a small bowl until well combined. Whisk again if it separates before use.
Toss gently: Add the mango, pepper, onion, cilantro and scallions to the cabbage. Pour over the dressing and lift gently from the bottom to coat everything without crushing the mango.

Rest and taste: Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes, or up to 30 minutes for softer cabbage. Toss gently and taste a forkful, adding a little extra lime or salt only if needed. Serve as six generous side portions, lifting out of any pooled liquid.

recipes.keywords: Caribbean, bright, sweet, tangy, fresh, herbaceous, weeknight, family-meal, bbq, picnic, no-cook, toss

recipes.name: Mango-Rita Green Smoothie
recipes.description: A green smoothie with mango and lime is tropical and tart - the acid cuts through the sweet fruit and mild greens. The trick is using ripe mango (it should yield slightly to pressure) so the smoothie is thick and creamy without needing yogurt or ice cream.
recipeIngredient: Tiny pinch of Sea Salt (The "Trust Me" Note)

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: In a high-powered blender, combine the spinach, coconut water, and orange. Blend on high for 30 seconds until the greens are completely pulverized.
The Bulk: Add the frozen mango, frozen pineapple, lime juice, and the pinch of sea salt.
Process: Blend on high for 60 seconds until perfectly velvety.
Adjust: If the smoothie is too thick, add a splash more coconut water. If you want more "Snap," add extra lime juice.
Serve: Pour into two chilled glasses. Garnish with a lime slice and serve immediately.
