recipes.name: Maple-Roasted Sweet Potato Wedges
recipes.description: Sweet potatoes are naturally sweet, so the trick is high heat roasting to caramelize their edges before the inside overcooks. Cutting them into wedges (not fries) means more surface area for caramelization.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut: Cut each sweet potato into wedges about 1/2-inch thick, lengthwise (like you're cutting a log into planks). Pat dry with paper towels - moisture prevents crisping.
Oil and Season: Toss wedges with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on the sheet, skin-side down. Do not crowd - they need space to caramelize.
First Roast: Bake for 18-20 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy.
Glaze: Flip the wedges. Brush the tops with maple syrup (use a pastry brush). Sprinkle with smoked paprika if using.
Finish Roast: Return to oven for 8-10 minutes until the glaze is bubbling and caramelized. The edges should be dark brown and crispy.
Serve: Remove and finish with a pinch of flaky sea salt. Serve warm.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, caramelized, weeknight, comfort-food, entertaining, roast

recipes.name: Mapo Tofu
recipes.description: Mapo tofu is defined by its ma la -- the numbing tingle of Sichuan peppercorn combined with the deep, complex heat of doubanjiang. The biggest mistake home cooks make is using silken tofu, which disintegrates.
recipeIngredient: 1 block (14 oz) Medium-Firm Tofu, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
1 tbsp Fermented Black Beans, rinsed and roughly chopped
1 tbsp Sichuan Peppercorns, toasted and ground
2 Green Onions, white and green parts separated, thinly sliced
1 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with the separately measured slurry water
2 tbsp water, for the cornstarch slurry

recipeInstructions.text: Parcook the Tofu: Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to a gentle boil. Carefully slide in the tofu cubes and simmer for 2-3 minutes. This firms the tofu and removes any raw bean flavor. Drain very gently and set aside.
Cook the Pork: Heat the neutral oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add the ground pork and cook for 3-4 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned and the fat has rendered.

Fry the Doubanjiang: Push the pork to the side. Add the doubanjiang and fermented black beans to the oil in the wok. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until the oil turns a deep red and the paste is very fragrant. This is the critical step.
Build the Sauce: Add the garlic, ginger, and green onion whites. Stir-fry for 30 seconds. Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.

Add the Tofu: Gently slide the parcocked tofu into the sauce. Do not stir aggressively. Instead, gently push the tofu around with the back of a ladle or by shaking the wok. Simmer for 5 minutes to let the tofu absorb the sauce.
Thicken: Give the cornstarch slurry a stir and drizzle it into the wok in two additions, gently swirling between each. The sauce should coat the tofu in a glossy, clinging glaze.
Finish: Drizzle with sesame oil and chili oil. Sprinkle generously with the ground Sichuan peppercorn and green onion greens. Serve immediately over steamed white rice.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, spicy, savory, umami, rich, weeknight, comfort-food, saute, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Marinated Flank Steak Salad
recipes.description: Flank steak is an outstanding cut for salads due to its robust beefy flavor, but its long, fibrous grain requires deliberate technique. We score the steak in a shallow diamond pattern to sever surface fibers, allowing a bright soy-dijon marinade to penetrate and tenderize the meat.
recipeIngredient: 3 tbsp Soy Sauce (use Tamari for gluten-free)
1 tbsp Neutral Cooking Oil (or shallot oil, for searing)
1 large head Romaine Lettuce, washed and torn
1 head Butter Lettuce, washed and torn

recipeInstructions.text: Score the Steak: Lay the flank steak flat on a cutting board. Using a sharp knife, lightly score the surface in a diagonal diamond pattern on both sides, cutting about 1/8-inch deep. This prevents the steak from curling in the pan and helps the marinade penetrate.

Marinate: In a small bowl, whisk together the marinade ingredients: 1/4 cup olive oil, soy sauce, 1 tbsp dijon mustard, minced garlic, and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Place the steak in a shallow dish or zip-top bag and pour the marinade over it. Seal and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or up to 12 hours.

Bring to Temp: Remove the steak from the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking to take the chill off. This ensures even cooking. Pat the steak dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture so it sears rather than steams.

Make the Vinaigrette: In a jar or small bowl, combine the vinaigrette ingredients: 1/3 cup olive oil, 3 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp dijon mustard, minced shallot, salt, and pepper. Shake or whisk vigorously until emulsified.

Sear the Steak: Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat until it is smoking hot. Add 1 tbsp of neutral oil (or leftover shallot oil). Lay the steak in the skillet and sear undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes per side for medium-rare (targeting an internal temperature of 130°F).
Rest: Transfer the steak to a clean cutting board and let it rest undisturbed for 10 minutes to allow the juices to redistribute.
Slice: Using a sharp carving knife held at a 45-degree angle, slice the rested steak as thinly as possible against the grain.

Assemble: In a large serving bowl, toss the romaine and butter lettuces with half of the vinaigrette. Arrange the sliced cucumbers, diced avocado, and shaved radishes on top. Arrange the sliced steak over the greens. Drizzle with the remaining vinaigrette.
Finishing Touch: Generously scatter the Crispy Shallots and toasted pepitas over the top just before serving to preserve their crunch.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, bright, savory, clean, crispy, umami, weeknight, everyday, kid-friendly, marinate, sear, toss

recipes.name: Bulgogi
recipes.description: The secret to authentic Bulgogi is the thickness of the cut. It should be paper-thin.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Ribeye Beef, very thinly sliced (The "Super H-Mart" Shortcut: Buy pre-sliced or pre-marinated "Bulgogi" beef)
1/2 Pear (Bosc or Asian), grated (The enzyme that tenderizes the meat)

recipeInstructions.text: The Meat: Pat beef dry with paper towels. If not pre-marinated, whisk all marinade ingredients in a bowl. Add the thinly sliced ribeye and toss to coat. Let marinate for at least 30 minutes (or overnight).
The Pan: Heat a cast-iron skillet or wok over high heat until smoking. Add a tiny splash of oil.
The Sear: Spread the beef in a single layer. Do not crowd the pan (work in batches). Let it sear undisturbed for 1-2 minutes until you get charred, crispy edges.
Finish: Flip and cook for 30 more seconds. Remove immediately.

recipes.keywords: Korean, sweet, savory, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, sear, smoke

recipes.name: Massaman Curry
recipes.description: Tender beef, potatoes and onion in a rich coconut curry with whole peanuts, warming spices and a sweet-tart tamarind finish.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb boneless beef chuck, cut into 1-inch / 2.5 cm cubes; trim tough outer silverskin but retain marbled fat
2 tbsp neutral cooking oil, divided between browning and the curry paste
3 tbsp prepared massaman curry paste; start with less if particularly hot or salty
1 tsp whole green cardamom pods, measured before lightly cracking, optional
3–4 whole dried red chiles, optional for extra heat
1 (14 oz) can full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, stirred together
Hot water, only as needed to maintain the braising liquid
2 medium waxy or all-purpose potatoes, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch / 2 cm cubes
1 large yellow onion, peeled and cut into 1-inch / 2.5 cm chunks
1/2 cup unsalted or lightly salted roasted peanuts
2 tbsp fish sauce, divided and added to taste
1 tbsp finely chopped palm sugar or packed brown sugar
1 tbsp unsweetened Thai-style tamarind purée made from pulp and water, plus more only if needed after tasting
Additional palm or brown sugar, only if needed after tasting

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the beef and aromatics: Cut the trimmed chuck into 1-inch / 2.5 cm cubes and pat dry. Chop garlic and ginger and measure the paste, milk and stock. Reserve one-third of the oil for the paste; use the remaining two-thirds for browning. Keep raw-meat tools separate from serving utensils and wash them after preparing the beef.

Brown in batches: Heat the browning oil in portions over medium-high in the heavy pot. Brown the beef in an uncrowded layer, about two batches for the full recipe, using an equal share of that oil for each batch. Leave two broad faces against the pot for about 2–3 minutes per face, turning once browned. Transfer to a plate; it is still raw inside. Allow the pot to regain heat between batches and lower the heat if the coating starts to blacken.

Build the curry: Lower to medium-low. Add the reserved oil, optional cracked cardamom pods and whole dried chiles; stir for about 20 seconds. Add massaman paste and cook 1–2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant but not scorched. Stir in garlic and ginger for about 30 seconds. Gradually stir in the coconut milk, then stock and half the fish sauce, scraping up brown residue. There is no need to wait for coconut oil to separate. Return the beef and all its plate juices to the pot.

Braise the beef: Bring to a gentle simmer. Liquid should come just about to the top of the beef in the pot; add a little hot water if needed. Cover, lower the heat and braise gently for about 1 1/2–2 1/2 hours, beginning tenderness checks after 75 minutes. Every 20–30 minutes, stir along the bottom and check the liquid, adding hot water as needed to keep the beef mostly surrounded by sauce. A fork should enter the meat with only slight resistance before you continue. Toward the end of this stage, peel and cut the potatoes and onion.

Add potatoes and onion: Stir in the vegetables, cover and simmer about 20–30 minutes, stirring gently once or twice. The potatoes should be tender through the center and the beef should yield easily to a fork. Check a thick beef cube reaches at least 145°F / 63°C; tenderness usually requires cooking beyond that minimum. The off-heat rest comes before serving. If either needs longer, keep cooking gently and maintain enough liquid to prevent sticking. Lift out any potatoes that finish before the beef and return them at the finish.

Finish the sauce: Stir in peanuts, the starting amount of sugar and the starting amount of tamarind purée. Simmer 3–5 minutes. If the sauce is watery, simmer uncovered for another 5–10 minutes before final seasoning; it should coat a spoon but still flow around the meat. Taste with a piece of potato, then add the remaining fish sauce and optional extra sugar or tamarind in small amounts as needed. If using lime instead of tamarind, add it only after turning off the heat. Remove the cardamom pods and whole chiles before serving.

Rest and serve: Rest off heat for 5 minutes. Serve with a modest portion of separately prepared Basmati Rice. The potatoes already supply some starch. Coconut Jasmine Rice is a richer accompaniment. Add cilantro and lime wedges at the table.

recipes.keywords: Thai, savory, rich, warming, tangy, weekend, dinner-party, braise, simmer

recipes.name: Sushi Rice (Shari)
recipes.description: Vinegar-seasoned short-grain rice with tender, distinct grains that cling together lightly. Includes soaking, resting, seasoning and short cooling time.
recipeIngredient: 400 g Japanese short-grain white rice, not glutinous rice
480 ml cold water, plus water for rinsing
1 piece dried kombu, about 5 cm square

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and soak: Rinse the rice several times, gently swishing and draining until the water is less cloudy. Drain well, transfer to a heavy 3-quart saucepan and add the measured cooking water. Wipe away visible grit from the kombu with a barely damp cloth and add it. Soak for 30 minutes.
Heat and cook: Bring toward a boil over medium heat with the lid slightly ajar. Remove the kombu when the water starts bubbling. Close the lid, reduce to low and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes.

Rest and check: Move off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Check a grain for a tender center. If grains are still firm and water remains, cover and cook on low for 3–5 minutes, then rest off heat for 5 minutes and check again. If the pot is dry but the center is hard, use the measured-water correction in troubleshooting. Already mushy rice will not become firm through extra stirring or cooking.

Mix the seasoning: While the rice cooks, stir four fifths of the measured vinegar, the sugar and two thirds of the measured salt in a small bowl. Warm briefly if needed to dissolve, without boiling. Reserve the remaining vinegar and salt.

Season and cool briefly: Transfer hot rice to a wide nonreactive bowl. Distribute the seasoning over it and gently lift and fold with a rice paddle. Fan as steam escapes, about 5–10 minutes; judge by the rice rather than expecting a fixed temperature after two minutes. Taste, dissolve any reserved salt needed in the reserved vinegar, then fold in that vinegar whether or not extra salt is used. For poke, let the portion being used become only barely warm before topping with cold fish and serving immediately.

Use or refrigerate: Cover loosely with a clean damp towel only during brief assembly. Measure the amount required by the main recipe; this batch makes approximately 5 1/2–6 cups. Refrigerate extra rice promptly rather than leaving the whole batch out while eating.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, acidic, sweet, salty, entertaining, weekend-project, boil, simmer, steam

recipes.name: Mediterranean Chicken Bowls
recipes.description: This modular grain bowl treats each component as an independent element. Marinating chicken thighs in oregano and lemon, then searing over high heat develops a charred, crispy crust characteristic of Greek souvlaki.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs Chicken Thighs, boneless and skinless
2 cups Cooked Yellow Rice or Quinoa

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate: In a large bowl, toss chicken thighs with olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, and garlic. Let sit for at least 15 minutes (ideally 2 hours).
The Sear: Heat a large skillet or grill to medium-high. Cook chicken for 5-6 minutes per side until deeply charred and the internal temp is 165°F.
Rest: Transfer to a board and let rest for 5 minutes. Slice into thin strips.
Assemble: In four deep bowls, spread a generous base of hummus. Top with a scoop of warm rice or quinoa.
Layer: Arrange the sliced chicken, cucumbers, and tomatoes in distinct "stacks" around the bowl.
Finish: Top with crumbled feta and a massive pile of Pickled Red Onions. Serve with a lemon wedge for the final High Note.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, acidic, rich, weeknight, meal-prep, grill, no-cook

recipes.name: Lemon-Oregano Chicken with Roasted Peppers
recipes.description: Boneless thighs in a measured lemon, garlic and oregano marinade, with peppers and onions roasted on a separate tray.
recipeIngredient: 900 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, excess loose fat trimmed
3 tbsp olive oil, for the marinade
3/4 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
1/2 tsp ground black pepper, for the chicken
400 g bell peppers, cored and cut into 3/4-inch strips
200 g red onion, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch wedges
1 tbsp olive oil, for the vegetables
1/4 tsp fine salt, for the vegetables
1/4 tsp ground black pepper, for the vegetables
1 tbsp chopped parsley, optional finishing herb

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate cold: Whisk marinade oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, chicken salt and chicken pepper. Toss with chicken, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for a longer preparation window. Keep the chicken’s original storage/use-by limit in mind; marinating does not reset it.

Prepare trays and vegetables: During the marinade, heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Toss peppers and onion with their separate oil, salt and pepper and spread on one rimmed half-sheet pan. Lift the thighs from the marinade, allow excess to drip off, open them flat and space them on a second pan. Discard the raw-contact marinade; do not use it as a serving sauce. Wash raw-meat utensils and hands.

Roast and check separately: Put chicken below the vegetable tray. Roast for about 25–35 minutes, turning the vegetable pieces and rotating each tray front to back after fifteen minutes. Start checking chicken at twenty-five minutes: insert a thermometer into the thickest part of every thigh and continue until each reaches at least 165°F / 74°C. Remove finished pieces to a clean board. Vegetables should be soft through the thick onion wedges with browned edges; let them continue separately if needed.

Rest and portion: Rest the cooked chicken for five minutes, then slice across the meat. Divide the full chicken and vegetable batches among four plates. Scatter the optional measured parsley over the vegetables. This recipe supplies the protein and roasted vegetables; bread, grains and sauces are additional components.

recipes.keywords: Greek-inspired, Mediterranean-inspired, savory, acidic, herbaceous, weeknight, entertaining, meal-prep, roast

recipes.name: Mediterranean Grain Salad
recipes.description: This salad bridges lunch and dinner - hearty enough with farro's chewy texture to anchor a meal, but light enough for summer eating. Farro is the grain of ancient Rome and remains central to Mediterranean cooking because it has more fiber and protein than wheat, and a nutty flavor that holds up to bold olive oil and vinegar.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt (plus more to taste)
1 cup Kalamata Olives, pitted and halved

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the Farro: Rinse the farro under cold water. In a medium pot, bring broth and salt to a boil. Add farro, stir once, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes until tender but still chewy (not mushy). Drain any excess liquid and spread on a sheet pan to cool to room temperature - this keeps the grains from clumping.
Prepare the Vegetables: While the farro cools, dice the cucumber, tomatoes, and bell pepper into roughly 1/2-inch pieces. Finely dice the red onion. Place all in a large bowl with the olives.
Make the Dressing: In a small jar or bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, grated garlic, and black pepper. Taste and adjust acidity - it should be bright and tangy.
Combine: Add the cooled farro to the bowl with the vegetables. Pour the dressing over and toss well to coat every grain and vegetable.
Finish: Just before serving, fold in the crumbled feta, parsley, mint, and dill. Taste and adjust salt and lemon juice. Serve at room temperature or chilled.

Make-Ahead: This salad tastes even better the next day as flavors meld. Store covered in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Add the feta and fresh herbs just before serving to prevent them from getting soggy.

recipes.keywords: Greek, Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, acidic, herbaceous, savory, fresh, weeknight, meal-prep, light-and-fresh, entertaining, boil, no-cook

recipes.name: Mediterranean Pinwheels
recipes.description: These quick appetizers or lunch components require proper technique to avoid falling apart. Blending cream cheese with flavored oil from sun-dried tomatoes creates a tacky, flavor-rich spread that binds the fillings to the tortilla.
recipeIngredient: 6 large Spinach or Sun-dried Tomato Tortillas
2 tbsp Oil (reserved from sun-dried tomato jar)
6 oz Sun-dried Tomatoes in oil, chopped
10 oz Frozen Spinach, thawed and squeezed bone-dry

recipeInstructions.text: The Bind: In a food processor, blend cream cheese, garlic, a few sun-dried tomatoes, and 2 tbsp of the tomato oil until completely smooth.
Prep: Lay out the 6 tortillas. Spread a thick, even layer of the cream cheese mixture over each, leaving a 1/2-inch border at the top.
Layer: Scatter the chopped spinach, remaining sun-dried tomatoes, Parmesan, and feta over the cream cheese. Place a single line of fresh basil leaves across the center of each tortilla.
The Roll: Starting from the edge parallel to the basil, roll the tortilla very tightly, squeezing gently as you go to ensure the "Emulsion" binds the layers.
The Finish: Wrap each log tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (mandatory for clean slicing).
Cut: Using a sharp serrated knife, slice into 1-inch pinwheels.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, umami, rich, herbaceous, entertaining, quick-lunch, blend

recipes.name: Mediterranean Salmon with Lemon-Herb Emulsion
recipes.description: Crisp-skinned salmon over herbed orzo, chickpeas, tomatoes and feta, with a shaken lemon, olive oil and oregano dressing.
recipeIngredient: 4 skin-on salmon fillets, 6–8 oz each, of similar thickness
2 tbsp olive oil, for searing salmon
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the dressing
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the orzo
1 tsp smoked paprika, divided equally between salmon and chickpeas
1 cup canned chickpeas, measured after draining and rinsing, then thoroughly dried
Fresh parsley and mint, chopped, to taste
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Drain, rinse and thoroughly dry the chickpeas. Zest the lemon, then juice it. Halve tomatoes, chop herbs and measure the separate oil amounts. Pat salmon skin dry, remove pin bones and refrigerate while starting the sides.

Roast chickpeas: Toss chickpeas with their allotted oil, half the smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Spread in one layer on a rimmed tray. Roast about 25–35 minutes, shaking at about 15 minutes, until lightly crisp and beginning to brown. Begin checking at 20 minutes; do not insist that the centers turn hard.

Mix dressing and cook orzo: Shake the dressing oil, garlic, honey, oregano and half the lemon juice in a closed jar. Taste, then add more of the remaining lemon juice, salt and pepper as needed. Meanwhile cook orzo in boiling salted water according to its package until tender with a little bite. Drain, then toss with the orzo oil, tomatoes, feta, parsley and mint. Cover briefly to keep warm while the fish cooks.

Heat the skillet: When chickpeas are about 10 minutes from ready, season salmon with lemon zest, the remaining smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Heat the salmon oil in a broad skillet over medium-high until shimmering, not smoking heavily. If portions cannot fit with space between them, use two skillets with the oil divided between them, or cook in batches, reserving a proportional share of the searing oil for each batch.

Sear and finish: Lay salmon skin-side down, away from you. Press gently with a spatula for the first few seconds to keep skin in contact. Cook about 4–6 minutes until the skin browns and releases; reduce heat if spices darken rapidly. Turn carefully and cook about 2–6 minutes more, depending on thickness. Check the thickest center from the side for 145°F / 63°C. If the outside is done before the center, lower the heat and continue gently. Remove each portion when ready.

Assemble: Divide the herbed orzo among plates, scatter over roasted chickpeas and add salmon with its skin facing up. Shake the dressing again and spoon around the fish and over the orzo, keeping the skin exposed. Serve immediately. The pasta, legumes and tomatoes are already part of this dish; a separate grain is unnecessary.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, sweet, acidic, herbaceous, smoky, weeknight, light-and-fresh, sear, roast, boil, no-cook

recipes.name: Melon Daiquiri
recipes.description: The daiquiri is a Cuban drink named after a beach near Santiago - born from American occupation and the sugar trade. A good daiquiri is balanced: rum, lime juice, and sugar in equal parts, with the lime juice providing the backbone.
recipeIngredient: 6 cups Honeydew Melon, peeled, deseeded and cubed
1/2 cup Fresh Lime Juice (The Acid Balance)

recipeInstructions.text: Thermal Prep: Freeze your melon cubes for 30 minutes prior to starting for the best texture.
Blend: Combine the honeydew, light rum, lime juice, and melon liqueur in a high-powered blender.
Process: Pulse on low, then increase to high until perfectly smooth. Add a handful of ice only if needed to reach a "thick-shake" consistency.
Skew: Thread 3 cantaloupe cubes onto each sugar cane skewer.
Serve: Pour into chilled coupes or martini glasses. Garnish with the skewers and serve immediately for the maximum "Bounce."

recipes.keywords: Caribbean, sweet, acidic, entertaining, blend

recipes.name: Arroz Rojo
recipes.description: Long-grain rice toasted in oil, then simmered with tomato, onion, garlic and broth. A covered rest helps the grains settle before fluffing.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup plain tomato puree, or 1 cup freshly blended Roma tomatoes
1 cup chicken broth, plus hot water as needed if the rice remains firm

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and drain: Rinse the dry rice in several changes of cool water until less cloudy. Drain thoroughly in a fine-mesh strainer, shaking out excess water while you dice the onion and mince the garlic.

Toast: Warm the oil in a heavy saucepan over medium heat. Carefully add the drained rice; residual water can spatter. Stir constantly for about 3–5 minutes, until the grains look opaque and lightly golden and smell nutty. Lower the heat if individual grains darken quickly.
Add aromatics: Stir in the onion and garlic. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant without browning the garlic.
Add liquid: Carefully stir in the measured tomato puree, broth and salt. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring once to distribute the rice and release any grains stuck to the base.

Simmer and check: Place the cilantro sprig on top. Cover tightly and reduce to a low simmer. Cook about 15–18 minutes without repeatedly opening the lid. Taste a grain: it should have no hard center, and free liquid should be absorbed. If firm and dry, add a little hot water and continue covered; if firm with liquid remaining, continue gently without adding more.
Rest: Remove from heat once tender and leave covered for 10 minutes.
Finish: Remove the cilantro sprig. Fluff gently with a fork and divide into four side portions.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, weeknight, meal-prep, fry, simmer, boil, blend

recipes.name: Skillet Esquites (Mexican Corn Salad)
recipes.description: Sweet corn with browned edges, lime, chile, and cotija in a light creamy dressing. Learn to manage pan moisture before adding the delicate finishing ingredients.
recipeIngredient: 4 cups (600 g) fresh sweet-corn kernels or thawed frozen corn, thoroughly drained
2 tbsp Mexican crema or sour cream
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, divided, plus more to taste
1/2 tsp pure ground ancho chile (not a salted seasoning blend)
Fine salt, to taste after adding the cotija

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and mix the dressing: Drain corn thoroughly and blot away surface water. Whisk mayonnaise, crema, 1 tbsp lime juice, ground ancho chile, and garlic in a large bowl. Set aside the remaining lime, cheese, scallions, cilantro, and optional jalapeño.

Brown the first batch: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add half the corn and spread it out. Leave for about 2 minutes, then stir and continue cooking for 3–5 minutes, until tender with golden-brown patches. Reduce heat if it spits violently or scorches. Transfer to a wide plate.
Repeat: Add the remaining oil and corn. Cook the second batch in the same way, adjusting the heat as needed. If dark residue is burning, remove it carefully before adding the second batch.
Dress while warm: Let the corn stop steaming vigorously for 2–3 minutes. Add both batches to the dressing and toss. Fold in cotija, scallions, cilantro, and optional jalapeño.

Balance and serve: Taste, add the remaining lime by the teaspoon as needed, and add salt only if the cheese has not supplied enough. Divide into six side portions and serve warm or cool. Chill promptly if making ahead.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, spicy, sweet, acidic, rich, weeknight, entertaining, light-and-fresh, saute, toss

recipes.name: Yogurt-Marinated Chicken and Onion Kabobs
recipes.description: Skinless chicken and thin onion layers in a garlic, lemon and yogurt marinade, grilled with warm spices and a measured center-temperature check. Plan the overnight soak and grill capacity.
recipeIngredient: 2 1/2 lbs (1130 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed and cut into about thirty-six 1 1/2-inch pieces
250 g peeled red onion, cut into 1-inch squares and separated into single or thin paired layers
1 cup (240 g) plain whole-milk Greek yogurt
1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, plus up to 1/2 tsp more for extra heat
1 tsp neutral oil, for grill grates (or 1 tbsp for the three-batch skillet option)

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and coat: Cut the peeled onion into one-inch squares and separate into single or thin paired layers. Cut chicken into about thirty-six pieces roughly 1 1/2 inches across, keeping thickness similar. In a bowl large enough to hold everything, whisk yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice and zest, garlic, paprika, cumin, cinnamon, the desired red pepper flakes, salt and black pepper. Add chicken and onion and turn to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for eight to twenty-four hours.

Prepare the grill: Near the end of marinating, heat a gas grill with the lid closed, then keep a medium-high cooking zone and a low or unlit zone. For charcoal, allow coals to establish and arrange them on one side, leaving the other side cooler. Follow the grill's lighting instructions. Set out a clean serving platter and utensils; the raw-marinated tray is not the serving platter.

Thread and drain: Divide chicken among twelve 10–12-inch skewers, about three pieces each. Distribute onion in thin layers between the chicken and at both ends, keeping the whole food-bearing length over the cooking zone. Do not thicken the onion stacks to use it up; use an additional onion-only skewer if needed and count it in the grill capacity. All this onion has contacted raw chicken and must be cooked; it cannot become a raw garnish. Thread without tightly compressing or wrapping pieces into thick bundles. Let excess marinade drain back into its bowl so a thin film remains, then discard the residue. Keep six skewers refrigerated while the first six cook, unless the grill is large enough for the whole batch with a clear cooler zone. Lightly oil clean grates with the measured teaspoon neutral oil using a folded paper towel held in long tongs.

Grill the first round: Lay six skewers over the cooking zone without touching. Close the lid between turns and turn about every three minutes once the first surface releases, using a broad spatula to help if needed. Cook for about twelve to fifteen minutes, moving skewers to the cooler zone if the coating browns too quickly. Cook any extra onion skewer alongside until the layers soften and reach 165°F / 74°C because of their raw-chicken contact. Onion edges should soften with some browned spots; the chicken coating need not become uniformly crisp.

Check and repeat: Begin checking around twelve minutes. Probe the largest pieces on each skewer from the side, avoiding the hot metal, and continue until each reaches at least 165°F / 74°C. Check any unusually thick pieces separately. Transfer fully cooked skewers to the clean platter and cover loosely during the short second round. Cook the remaining six the same way, keeping the same thermometer endpoint. A tight cover softens the coating, and the first round will not retain the same surface texture as chicken served straight from the grill.

Rest and finish: Rest the final round for five minutes, then serve two skewers per person with the chopped parsley and lemon wedges. For six plates, add one-and-a-half four-side batches of Lemon and Herb Instant Couscous, starting with 375 g dry couscous, plus vegetables or salad. Alternatively, warm six pita breads and add a vegetable side. These are extra components and preparation time. The onion in each portion is a seasoning vegetable, about 40 g raw weight, not a full vegetable side.

recipes.keywords: Middle Eastern-inspired, tangy, savory, aromatic, entertaining, family-meal, meal-prep, marinate, grill

citation.name: Adapted from Jennifer Segal's Middle Eastern-Style Grilled Chicken Kabobs, Once Upon a Chef

recipes.name: Mini-Shell Pasta with Bacon and Peas
recipes.description: Small pasta shells with smoked bacon, sweet peas, mint and a rich Parmesan finish, loosened with pasta water.
recipeIngredient: 10 slices smoked bacon, cut crosswise into thin slivers
2 tbsp crème fraîche or heavy cream
1 lemon, juiced, added gradually to taste
2 tbsp fresh mint, finely chopped, divided between sauce and garnish
1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from The New York Times’ Mini-Shell Pasta with Creamy Smoked Bacon and Peas.

itemListElement.text: Start water and prepare: Bring pasta water to a boil. Cut bacon into thin slivers, finely grate Parmesan, chop mint and juice the lemon. Season the water moderately; bacon and cheese bring much of the salt.

Cook bacon: Melt butter in a large deep skillet over medium-low to medium. Add bacon and cook, stirring, about 10–15 minutes or as its package directs, until cooked through and golden with crisp edges. Lower heat if butter darkens quickly. Keep the rendered fat for the sauce; do not add more oil.

Cook pasta and peas: Meanwhile cook pasta according to package directions until tender with a little bite. Cook peas fully according to their package in a separate saucepan or microwave-safe bowl and drain. Reserve the listed pasta water before draining pasta without rinsing.

Combine: Stir cooked peas, crème fraîche or cream and half the mint into the bacon pan over low heat. Add hot pasta and about one-quarter of the reserved water. Toss gently until hot and coated, using the pasta pot instead if the skillet is too full.

Add cheese off heat: Remove from the burner and wait until bubbling subsides. Fold in Parmesan a handful at a time, adding warm water in small amounts as needed for a creamy coating. Add half the lemon juice, taste, then add more of the remaining juice only as needed. The sauce should remain slightly loose for plating.
Serve: Add black pepper and taste before salt. Divide into the intended portions and scatter the remaining measured mint over the top. Serve promptly.

recipes.name: Mint Tzatziki with Honey
recipes.description: Thick Greek yogurt with crisp diced cucumber, fresh mint, olive oil, garlic and a little honey. Spoon it into lamb pitas or serve alongside grilled meat and vegetables.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup (240 g) plain full-fat Greek yogurt
100 g English cucumber, ends trimmed, finely diced

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the cucumber and herbs: Wash and dry the cucumber and mint. Cut the cucumber into fine dice, about 3 mm across, then pat with a clean kitchen towel. Finely chop the mint and mince the small garlic clove.
Mix: Stir the yogurt, olive oil and honey together until evenly blended. Fold in the cucumber, mint, garlic and half the measured salt.

Taste and serve: Taste, then add the reserved salt only if needed. Serve now, or cover and refrigerate while preparing the meal; stir and taste again before serving. For four lamb pitas, start with 2–3 tablespoons in each and offer the rest alongside. The full batch makes approximately 1 1/2 cups, depending on the yogurt and cucumber.

recipes.keywords: Greek-inspired, herbaceous, rich, acidic, weeknight, meal-prep, entertaining, no-cook

recipes.name: Miriam’s Melt-In-Your-Mouth Rosh Hashanah Brisket
recipes.description: Rosh Hashanah brisket is a Jewish holiday tradition that carries prayer and memory into the kitchen - the dish is as much about the ritual as the flavor. A long, low braise at 300°F for hours breaks down the connective tissue into gelatin, which is why it's so tender.
recipeIngredient: 2 large Spanish Onions, sliced into thick rounds

recipeInstructions.text: Foundation: Preheat oven to 400°F. Lay the onion rounds in a single layer at the bottom of a heavy baking dish or Dutch oven.
Rub: In a small bowl, mix the paprika, garlic powder, salt, and chives. Rub the mixture aggressively into every surface of the brisket.
The High Sear: Place the brisket on top of the onions. Roast uncovered for 1 hour. This builds the "bark" and browns the onions.
The Braise: Remove from oven. Pour the balsamic vinegar and honey over the meat. Cover the dish extremely tightly with a heavy lid or double layer of foil.
Low & Slow: Lower the oven temperature to 250°F. Return the brisket to the oven and cook for 4 more hours until fork-tender.
The Chill (Optional but Recommended): Let the meat cool in its juices, then refrigerate overnight. This allows the fat to be easily removed and the meat to be sliced perfectly thin.
Serve: Slice against the grain. Return to the sauce and reheat gently before serving.

recipes.keywords: Jewish, sweet, acidic, holiday, bake, roast, braise

recipes.name: Misir Wot (Ethiopian Red Lentil Stew)
recipes.description: Misir wot gets its soul from two things: deeply caramelized onions and berbere spice. The onions must be cooked low and slow without any oil for the first 10 minutes -- this dry-sauteing technique is traditional and concentrates their sweetness before the niter kibbeh is added.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 cups Red Lentils, rinsed until water runs clear
3 tbsp Niter Kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced butter) or Extra-Virgin Olive Oil for vegan
2 large Red Onions, finely diced (about 3 cups total)
1 tsp Kosher Salt, plus more to taste
1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice, for finishing

recipeInstructions.text: Dry-Saute the Onions: Place the diced red onions in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat with no oil. Cook, stirring frequently, for 8-10 minutes. The onions will release their moisture and begin to dry out, soften, and concentrate in flavor. This traditional step is essential.

Add the Fat and Spices: Add the niter kibbeh (or olive oil) to the softened onions. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the onions begin to turn golden. Add the garlic and ginger, stirring for 30-45 seconds. Stir in the berbere spice blend, tomato paste, cardamom, and fenugreek. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly to prevent burning. The pot should be deeply red and intensely fragrant.

Cook the Lentils: Add the rinsed red lentils, 3 cups water, and salt. Stir well to combine. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 25-30 minutes, stirring every 5-7 minutes to prevent sticking, until the lentils have completely broken down into a thick, porridge-like stew.
Adjust the Consistency: The wot should be thick and scoopable, not soupy. If it thickens too much, add water a few tablespoons at a time. If it is too thin, simmer uncovered for a few more minutes.
Finish: Stir in the lemon juice. Taste and adjust salt and berbere to your heat preference.
Serve: Traditionally served on injera (Ethiopian sourdough flatbread) for scooping. Alternatively, serve over steamed basmati rice. The wot should be vibrant red, thick, and deeply spiced.

recipes.keywords: Ethiopian, spicy, savory, rich, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Miso-Glazed Roasted Cauliflower
recipes.description: Miso is umami condensed - it transforms mild cauliflower into something deeply savory and addictive. The glaze contains the holy trifecta: miso (salt and depth), mirin (sweetness and shine), and sesame oil (richness).
recipeIngredient: Sesame Seeds and Scallions for garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Make Glaze: In a small bowl, whisk together miso, mirin, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and fresh ginger. Taste - it should taste aggressively salty and umami-rich (the cauliflower will mellow it).
Prep Oven: Preheat to 425°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss: Pat cauliflower florets dry (moisture prevents caramelization). Place in a large bowl. Pour the miso glaze over and toss with your hands until every floret is coated.
Spread: Arrange florets in a single layer on the baking sheet, cut-side down. Do not crowd.
Roast: Bake for 25-30 minutes until the cauliflower is tender inside and the glaze is caramelized and slightly charred on the edges. Shake the pan halfway through.
Finish: Remove from oven. Garnish generously with sesame seeds and thinly sliced scallions. Serve hot.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, umami, savory, caramelized, salty, weeknight, entertaining, comfort-food, roast

recipes.name: Miso-Mashed Potatoes
recipes.description: Yukon Gold potatoes gently mashed with white miso, butter, warm milk and a little garlic, finished with optional scallions.
recipeIngredient: 900 g peeled and trimmed Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into even 1-inch pieces
2 L cold water, or enough to cover the potatoes by about 1 inch
8 g salt, for the cooking water
4 tbsp (57 g) unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
2 tbsp (36 g) plain white rice miso, without added dashi; choose certified gluten-free miso if needed
1/2 cup (120 ml) whole milk, plus up to 1/4 cup (60 ml) more if needed
1/8 tsp fine salt, optional after tasting
2 tbsp thinly sliced washed scallion greens, optional garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Cut and cover: Peel and trim the potatoes to the listed net weight, then cut into even one-inch pieces. Rinse briefly, put in a 5-quart pot and cover with about two liters cold water, adding enough to sit an inch above the potatoes. Add the eight grams of cooking-water salt.

Simmer to tenderness: Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook about 18–22 minutes after the water begins simmering, until several tested pieces yield easily to a knife and a cooled bite is completely soft in the center. Keep cooking if needed; larger pieces take longer.

Warm the miso dairy during cooking: In a small saucepan over low heat, whisk the initial half-cup milk with the miso and garlic powder until the miso has no large clumps. Add the butter and warm gently until melted. Do not boil or reduce the mixture. Wash and slice the optional scallions while the potatoes finish.

Drain and briefly dry: Drain well in a colander. Return potatoes to the pot over low heat for one to two minutes, shaking gently, until surface water evaporates and the pieces look matte. Remove from heat before they stick or brown.

Mash and fold: Pass the hot potatoes through a ricer or mash gently by hand. Fold in the warm miso dairy in two additions with a spatula, stopping as soon as it is incorporated. If stiff, warm and add the reserved milk one tablespoon at a time until the mash forms a soft mound. Do not beat it smooth in a blender.

Taste and serve: Taste before adding the optional one-eighth teaspoon of salt; the miso may supply all the finishing seasoning needed. Scatter with the optional scallions and divide into four generous side portions, or six smaller portions on a plate with another starch. Pair with a simply seasoned roast and a crisp or lemony vegetable.

recipes.keywords: American, Japanese, savory, umami, rich, comfort-food, weeknight, entertaining, boil, simmer

recipes.name: Miso Salmon with Bok Choy
recipes.description: Citrus-miso salmon with garlic, scallions and oyster-seasoned bok choy over jasmine rice.
recipeIngredient: 540 ml water, for rice, plus water for rinsing
900 g skinless, boneless salmon, divided into four similar fillets
1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
1 tsp neutral oil, for the foil
600 g trimmed baby bok choy, washed and dried
4 tsp neutral oil, for the skillet, divided
2 tbsp water, for the bok choy, divided

recipeInstructions.text: Start rice and heat the oven: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C with a rack in the middle and another positioned for the later broil. Rinse the jasmine rice and drain well. Put it in a heavy 2-quart saucepan with 540 ml water, bring to a boil, cover and reduce to low. Simmer about 15 minutes until water is absorbed, then move off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff before serving. This is a starting method for regular jasmine white rice; follow the package if its ratio differs.

Mix and divide the marinade: While the rice cooks, whisk miso, honey, soy sauce, mirin, lemon juice, rice vinegar, half the minced garlic, half the scallions and half the pepper. Reserve 2 tbsp in a clean bowl for finishing. Check fish for pin bones and pat dry; place it in a shallow dish with the remaining marinade, turn to coat, cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Do not leave this acidic marinade on overnight.

Prepare the vegetables and pans: During the marinade, split small bok choy heads lengthwise; quarter larger heads so thick stem sections are about 1 inch across. Wash between the stalks, drain and dry thoroughly, then divide into two equal batches. Divide the remaining garlic, scallions and pepper between those batches. Line a metal half-sheet pan with foil and spread its teaspoon of oil where the fish will sit.

Roast the salmon: Lift fish from the marinade, letting excess drip off. Gently scrape off thick clumps, leaving a thin coating. Arrange on the prepared pan with space between portions and discard the raw-contact marinade. Roast about 12–16 minutes, until the fish is nearly cooked; check its center toward the end. If it reaches 145°F / 63°C before the final broil, it is already cooked and needs at most a very brief coloring step.

Cook bok choy in two batches: While fish roasts, heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat with 2 tsp neutral oil. Add half the bok choy cut-side down and cook 2–3 minutes until lightly browned. Turn, add half the reserved vegetable garlic and scallions, and stir 30 seconds until fragrant. Add 1 tbsp water, cover and steam 1–2 minutes until stems are crisp-tender. Uncover, evaporate any pooled water, then toss with 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1/2 tsp sesame oil and half the remaining pepper. Transfer to a serving dish and loosely cover. Repeat with the second batch and the remaining vegetable ingredients. Turn off the skillet before broiling; if the fish is waiting for its finish, set its pan briefly on a heatproof surface.

Glaze and briefly broil: Spread the clean reserved 2 tbsp marinade over the four fillets, using a clean utensil. Switch to high broil and place the fish surface 7–9 inches below the element. Watch continuously for 1–3 minutes, until the coating bubbles and browns. Check each fillet sideways in its thickest center and cook to 145°F / 63°C. If color arrives first, finish gently in the oven as described above. Let the fish stand briefly while fluffing and serving the rice.

Serve the complete dinner: Divide all the rice and bok choy among four bowls or plates and add one fillet to each. The original batch supplies about 225 g raw salmon and 150 g trimmed bok choy per diner, with roughly a cup of cooked rice. A small cucumber salad is an optional cool contrast, rather than a second required vegetable batch.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, Chinese, American, sweet, savory, umami, acidic, weeknight, family-meal, boil, simmer, roast, broil, saute, steam

citation.name: Jordan Silton

recipes.name: Miso Soup
recipes.description: Miso soup is a miracle of Emulsion and Timing. The most common mistake is boiling the miso - high heat kills the delicate probiotics and ruins the aroma.
recipeIngredient: 4 cups prepared dashi, homemade or made with instant dashi granules according to package instructions
4 oz Silken Tofu, cut into small cubes

recipeInstructions.text: Dashi: Bring the four cups of prepared dashi to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce heat to low.
Seaweed & Tofu: Add the wakame and tofu cubes. Simmer gently for 2 minutes until the seaweed is rehydrated.
The Miso: Place the miso paste in a small bowl. Ladle in about 1/2 cup of the hot broth. Whisk until the miso is completely smooth and liquid.
Finish: Turn off the heat. Stir the miso liquid back into the pot.
Serve: Add the green onions and serve immediately in small bowls.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, sweet, savory, umami, weeknight, quick-lunch, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Candy-Coated Chocolate Cookies
recipes.description: Folding only 3/4 of the candies into the dough, then pressing the remaining candies into the tops of the dough balls after scooping ensures vibrant colors stay visible on the finished cookies instead of bleeding into the batter during baking. Using a high ratio of brown sugar to white sugar creates chewy cookies that contrast the crisp candy shell.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp Baking Soda + 1 tsp Sea Salt

recipeInstructions.text: Cream: In a large bowl, beat the shortening (or butter) with both sugars until light and fluffy (2 mins). Add eggs and vanilla; beat until emulsified.
Dry Mix: Whisk together flour, baking soda, and salt. Gradually add to the wet mix until just combined.
Inclusions: Fold in 1 cup of the candies.
Shape: Preheat oven to 350°F. Drop teaspoon-sized balls of dough onto ungreased sheets.
Press: Press 3-4 of the remaining candies into the top of each ball.
Bake: Bake for 9-11 minutes until the edges are just golden. Do not over-bake; they will set on the pan.
Cool: Let rest on the pan for 5 minutes to ensure proper texture.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, kid-friendly, bake

recipes.name: Momma’s Turkey and Vegetable Meatloaf
recipes.description: A family-style turkey loaf with softened vegetables, a measured breadcrumb panade and a thin ketchup finish.
recipeIngredient: 40 g fine dry unseasoned whole-wheat breadcrumbs
100 g green bell pepper, cut into small dice
150 g zucchini, coarsely grated, then gently squeezed to about two thirds of its starting weight

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Mix breadcrumbs and milk and let hydrate at least 5 minutes. Grate and gently squeeze the zucchini to about two-thirds of its starting weight; prepare the other small-cut vegetables.

Soften and cool vegetables: Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook onion and pepper about 5 minutes, stirring. Add carrot and zucchini and cook another 4–5 minutes until softened and no liquid pools in the pan. Spread on a plate to cool about 5–10 minutes while preparing the remaining ingredients; they should no longer feel hot.
Mix: Beat egg into the hydrated crumbs with garlic powder, salt and pepper. Stir in cooled vegetables. Add cold turkey and fold gently until evenly combined, without prolonged kneading.
Shape and begin baking: Shape a free-form loaf roughly 9 by 4 inches and 2–2 1/2 inches high on the prepared tray, smoothing large cracks without packing hard. Bake about 35 minutes.

Glaze and check: Spread all the ketchup over the top in a thin layer. Continue baking about 15–25 minutes, checking until the center reaches 165°F / 74°C in several positions. Extend as needed. If the top darkens early, tent loosely with foil; a browned glaze is not the doneness test.

Rest and portion: Let rest for 10 minutes before cutting six portions. Each can be one thick slice or two thinner slices. Serve with separately prepared sides; the base recipe includes the loaf and its ketchup finish only.

recipes.keywords: American, comfort-food, saute, bake

recipes.name: Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: This family chocolate cake uses butter and boiling water to bring the cocoa into a smooth batter. The entire batter mixes in the saucepan used to melt the butter, minimizing cleanup.

recipeInstructions.text: Melt & Bloom: In a large saucepan over medium heat, bring the butter, cocoa powder, and water to a gentle boil. Remove from heat immediately.
The Batter: Into the hot saucepan, whisk in the sugar, buttermilk, baking soda, salt, and eggs until smooth. Gradually fold in the flour and vanilla.
Bake: Pour the batter into a greased 9x13 rectangular pan (or two 8-inch squares). Bake at 350°F for 25-30 minutes until a tester comes out clean.
The Frosting: While the cake bakes, melt the 1 stick of butter in a clean saucepan. Whisk in the cocoa and milk. Remove from heat and stir in the powdered sugar until silky.
Seal: Pour the warm frosting over the hot cake immediately after removing it from the oven. Let cool completely (if you can wait!) before slicing.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, holiday, entertaining, kid-friendly, comfort-food, bake, boil

recipes.name: Mongolian Beef with Ginger and Scallions
recipes.description: Thinly sliced beef browned in batches and briefly coated in a ginger-scallion soy glaze.
recipeIngredient: 680 g flank steak, sliced across the grain into 1/4-inch-thick strips about 2 inches long
3 tbsp (24 g) cornstarch, for the beef coating
3 tbsp neutral oil, for three beef batches
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, plus 1 tbsp for the slurry
3 tbsp (40 g) packed light brown sugar
80 g scallions, cut into 2-inch lengths, white and green parts separated
2 small dried red chilies, optional, left whole for mild heat or broken for more

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the beef: Pat the steak dry and slice across the grain into 1/4-inch-thick, roughly 2-inch-long strips. Toss with the 3 tbsp coating cornstarch, separating slices and shaking off loose excess. Divide into three roughly equal batches.

Mix the sauce and slurry: Stir soy sauce, 120 ml water and brown sugar together until the sugar mostly dissolves. In a separate cup, mix the 1 tsp slurry cornstarch with 1 tbsp cold water. Keep ginger, garlic, chilies and the two scallion portions beside the stove.

Sear three batches: Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high. Add 1 tbsp frying oil; it should shimmer without smoking heavily. Add one batch in a single layer and sear about 1–2 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through. Probe thicker strips from the edge to check at least 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat twice with 1 tbsp oil for each batch, letting the pan regain heat. Reduce heat if the coating burns before the meat cooks.

Cook aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Carefully discard excess oil and any blackened starch, leaving browned but unburned bits. Add the separate teaspoon oil, ginger and optional chilies; stir about 20 seconds. Add garlic and scallion whites and stir another 20–30 seconds without browning the garlic deeply.

Thicken gently: Pour in the mixed sauce and simmer about 1 minute. Stir the slurry again, add half, and simmer 20–30 seconds. Add the rest only if needed for a light spoon-coating consistency; discard unused slurry. Loosen with a tablespoon of water if it becomes sticky or pasty.

Coat and check: Return beef and its juices with the scallion greens. Toss over medium heat about 30–60 seconds, just until evenly coated and greens wilt. Verify sliced beef reaches at least 145°F / 63°C; give it at least 3 minutes before serving. Transfer off the hot pan for this wait. For the chicken variation, verify 165°F / 74°C in several thick strips instead.

Serve: Remove whole chilies or tell diners they are present. Divide among four portions with plain rice and vegetables prepared separately. Serve promptly; the coating will continue softening in the glaze.

recipes.keywords: Chinese-American, sweet, savory, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, fry, simmer

recipes.name: Moroccan-Inspired Carrot Salad with Orange and Mint
recipes.description: Coarsely grated carrots with a light citrus dressing, mint and a restrained optional orange-blossom aroma.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp sugar, optional and only if needed
1/4 tsp orange blossom water, optional, plus up to 1/4 tsp more to taste
1/2 tsp fine salt, divided and partly added to taste
1/4 cup fresh mint, thinly sliced just before serving

recipeInstructions.text: Grate carrots: Use the coarse holes of a box grater or a food-processor shredding disc. Transfer to a bowl. If loose liquid has already collected, pour it away without squeezing the shreds dry.

Mix and taste the dressing: Whisk orange juice, lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, optional cayenne and half the salt. Add the optional quarter-teaspoon orange-blossom water and taste a small amount with a carrot shred. Add sugar or more blossom water only if the balance needs it.

Dress and chill: Toss dressing through carrots, adding the optional raisins if chosen. Cover and refrigerate for about 20 minutes to let the shreds soften lightly. There is no need for a long warm countertop rest.

Finish freshly: Slice mint and chop parsley just before serving, fold them through and taste. Add remaining salt only if needed. Toss up any dressing from the bottom and divide into six side portions. If excess water has accumulated, drain a little before the final seasoning check.

recipes.keywords: Moroccan-inspired, North African, bright, sweet, tangy, warm, fresh, weeknight, family-meal, picnic, make-ahead, no-cook, toss

recipes.name: Moroccan-Inspired Chicken with Apricots, Chickpeas and Almonds
recipes.description: Bone-in chicken gently braised with onion, apricots and chickpeas, balanced with a measured preserved-lemon finish and toasted almonds.
recipeIngredient: 6 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, about 1.5 kg total, fully thawed
1 tsp fine salt, divided and partly added to taste
1 small pinch saffron threads, about 0.05 g, optional, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
1 1/2 cups (360 ml) low-sodium chicken stock, plus up to 1/2 cup (120 ml) only if needed
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) chickpeas, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
20 g preserved-lemon rind, pulp removed, rinsed if very salty and finely chopped
1 tsp honey, optional and only if needed after tasting
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and season: Pat thighs dry. Season with half the salt and all the pepper. Measure ground spices together, slice onions, chop garlic and preserved rind, and halve apricots. If using saffron, steep it in the listed warm water while preparing the pan.

Sear in two batches: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide Dutch oven over medium-high. Sear three thighs skin-side down about 6–8 minutes until golden, then turn for 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate. Add the second tablespoon oil if the pan needs it and repeat with the remaining thighs, lowering heat if drippings scorch. If enough chicken fat rendered, reserve unused oil rather than forcing it into the pan.

Build the onion base: Pour off excess fat, leaving about 1 tbsp. Cook onions over medium 10–12 minutes until soft and lightly golden, stirring. Add garlic for 30 seconds, ground spices for another 20–30 seconds and tomato paste for 1 minute. Add stock and scrape up the browned residue.

Begin the covered braise: Add apricots, cinnamon stick and optional saffron water. Return chicken skin-side up with any collected juices. The liquid should reach partway up the meat; add a little of the extra stock only if the base is too dry. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and reduce heat to maintain quiet bubbling.

Finish meat and beans: After about 30 minutes, add chickpeas and preserved-lemon rind around the chicken. Cover and continue another 10–25 minutes, checking the thickest thighs clear of bone reach 165°F / 74°C and the meat yields readily to a fork. Add a little stock if the pan is drying. Remove the cinnamon stick.

Toast almonds: During the braise, toast almonds in a dry skillet over medium-low about 3–5 minutes, stirring, until golden and fragrant. Transfer promptly to a cool plate rather than leaving them in the hot pan.

Set sauce and seasoning: If sauce is thin, lift chicken to a clean plate and simmer the sauce uncovered briefly until spoonable. Taste before adding the remaining salt, optional honey and fresh lemon juice in small amounts. Return chicken, fold half the herbs into the sauce and let stand off heat about 5 minutes.

Serve: Give each diner one thigh with sauce, chickpeas and apricots. Scatter almonds and remaining herbs at the table. A small portion of Garlic Butter Pearl Couscous is one possible accompaniment; it has its own cooking method and portion size.

recipes.name: Challah
recipes.description: Challah is traditional Jewish bread for Shabbat and holidays. Using five eggs creates rich, brioche-like crumb.

recipeInstructions.text: Activate: In a massive bowl, whisk yeast and 1 tbsp sugar into 1 3/4 cups lukewarm water. Let stand for 10 minutes until foamy.
The Emulsion: Whisk in the oil, 4 eggs, and the remaining sugar and salt.
Incorporate: Gradually add the flour, 1 cup at a time, until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Transfer to a floured surface. Knead by hand for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic (or use a stand mixer with a dough hook).
First Rise: Place in a greased bowl, cover with plastic, and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
Shape: Punch down the dough. Divide into two halves. Divide each half into 6 balls. Roll each ball into a 12-inch strand.
The Braid: Braid into two 6-strand loaves (see notes for braiding pattern). Place on a greased sheet.
Second Rise: Brush with beaten egg. Let rise for another 45-60 minutes.
Bake: Preheat oven to 375°F. Brush once more with egg and sprinkle with seeds. Bake for 35-40 minutes until deep mahogany brown.
Cool: Let cool completely on a rack before slicing.

recipes.keywords: Israeli, sweet, rich, weekend-project, entertaining, bake

recipes.name: Meera Sodha's Naan
recipes.description: Soft skillet naan with a little yogurt tang, browned bubbles and a tender center. Serve plain or brush the warm breads with garlic butter.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, reserved for kneading and rolling; use only as needed
2 tbsp neutral oil, for the dough
1 tsp neutral oil, for coating the dough
1 cup (240 ml) whole milk, warmed to 110–115°F / 43–46°C
2 tbsp (30 ml) whole milk, reserved only if the dough feels dry

recipeInstructions.text: Hydrate the yeast: Warm the measured cup of milk to 110–115°F / 43–46°C. Stir in the sugar and active dry yeast and leave for 5–10 minutes, until the granules have hydrated and activity appears at the surface. Do not use hot milk. Meanwhile, whisk the 500 g flour, fine salt and baking powder together in a large bowl.

Mix and knead: Add the yogurt, 2 tbsp oil and all the yeast-milk mixture to the flour. Mix until no loose pockets of flour remain, then knead on the work surface for about 5–8 minutes until smoother and elastic. Use the dusting flour sparingly. If the dough is stiff or cracks, knead in the correction milk a teaspoon at a time, only as needed for a soft, slightly tacky dough.

Let rise: Coat the dough with the separate teaspoon of oil and put it in a bowl with room to double. Cover and leave in a comfortably warm place for 60–90 minutes, until roughly doubled. Allow longer in a cool room; do not speed it up in a hot oven.

Divide and relax: Gently deflate and divide into 12 equal pieces, about 70 g each before any correction milk or dusting flour. Round into balls, cover and rest for 10 minutes. During this rest, melt the optional butter with the minced garlic in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir for about 1 minute after melting, until fragrant but not browned, then take off heat. Set out the towel-lined platter. During the final 5 minutes of the dough rest, begin heating the dry skillet over medium-high.

Heat the pan and roll: After the dry 12-inch cast-iron skillet has heated for about 5 minutes, roll two balls on a lightly dusted surface into ovals about 5 by 8 inches and roughly 1/8 inch / 3 mm thick. Keep the remaining balls covered. If a piece springs back, cover it for another 5–10 minutes and work on another. Do not stack uncooked ovals directly together.

Cook one bread: Brush loose flour off the oval and lay it flat in the hot pan. Cook about 30–45 seconds, until bubbles form and the underside has brown patches. Flip and cook about 30–45 seconds more. Flip again for about 10–20 seconds, pressing an undercooked edge lightly against the pan if needed. Check the first bread by tearing through a thick section near its center: there should be no sticky, raw dough inside. Adjust heat and time for the next round; a few dark freckles are enough, and blackening the whole surface is not the aim. Do not taste raw dough.

Wrap and repeat: Brush the hot bread with a little of the optional garlic butter, sharing the full amount across twelve, then enclose in the towel. Cook the second rolled bread. Between rounds, take the pan briefly off the burner while rolling the next pair; return it to the heat and let it recover before cooking. Wipe away scorched flour with a dry folded paper towel held in tongs. Allow about 30–40 minutes for rolling, pan adjustments and all twelve cooking rounds.

Serve: Bring the wrapped stack to the table promptly. Twelve breads make six portions of two, or twelve smaller one-bread accompaniments. If serving rice as well, start with one naan per person and offer the rest as wanted.

recipes.name: Nana Ruth’s Applesauce
recipes.description: This traditional applesauce appears on Jewish holiday tables for Rosh Hashanah, Thanksgiving, and Hanukkah. McIntosh apples have thin skin and high water content, allowing them to break down into naturally velvety texture without needing a blender.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Core and peel the apples. Cut into large chunks.
The Rinse: Place apple chunks in a heavy nonstick pot. Fill with water, rinse, and repeat, leaving about 1/4 inch of water at the bottom of the pot.
Season: Squeeze the lemon over the apples. Add the honey, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Boil: Bring to a boil over high heat. Immediately cover and reduce heat to very low.
Simmer: Cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. The apples should be very soft and falling apart.
The Crush: Use a potato masher or the side of a heavy spoon to crush the apples against the side of the pot into a chunky, uniform sauce.
Serve: Best served warm with a dusting of extra cinnamon.

recipes.name: Nana’s Biscuits
recipes.description: Biscuits are Southern breakfast staple, but the technique is universal - cold butter cut into flour creates pockets of steam that make them rise and flake. Buttermilk adds tang and helps with rise.
recipeIngredient: 1/4 cup Unsalted Butter, cold and cubed

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 425°F. Lightly grease a baking sheet with a little butter.

Cut the Fat: Place the sifted flour in a large bowl. Add the cold, cubed butter. Use your fingertips to rub the butter into the flour until it looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-sized bits remaining. (Speed is key to keep the butter cold).

Hydrate: Add the buttermilk and the pinch of baking soda. Mix gently with your hand just until the dough comes together. If it's too dry, add a tablespoon more buttermilk; if too sticky, a dusting of flour.
Shape: Roll the dough into 12 small balls. Place on the greased cookie sheet and flatten slightly with the palm of your hand. This flat shape ensures a crispy exterior and a tender middle.
Bake: Bake for 10-12 minutes. If the tops are not golden brown, switch to Broil for 1 minute, watching intensely to prevent burning.

recipes.name: New York Crunch Roll
recipes.description: Tuna, avocado and cucumber rolled with a small layer of crisp tempura flakes. Add the crunch just before rolling and eat promptly while it still has texture.
recipeIngredient: 230 g trimmed boneless, skinless yellowfin tuna, weighed after removing tough connective tissue; see raw-service sourcing note
150 g ripe avocado flesh, from about 1 medium avocado
100 g English cucumber, weighed after removing the watery seed core
1/3 cup ready-to-eat tempura flakes (tenkasu or agedama), not uncooked batter mix
4 full sheets unseasoned roasted nori, about 19 x 20 cm each; trim as directed
120 ml water, for dampening hands and the knife
1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, for the hand-dipping water

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare rice and equipment: Make Sushi Rice (Shari), weigh out 320 g and refrigerate surplus rice promptly. Let the rolling portion become barely warm during final preparation. Wrap a clean mat in food-safe film. Mix water and vinegar for lightly dampening fingers and the knife; it is not a sanitizer. Do not dip a raw-filling-coated hand or blade into this clean water. Wash hands and clean the blade before returning to it, use a separate damp cloth for wiping the cutting blade, and replace the water if contaminated.

Prepare vegetables: Wash the cucumber, remove the watery core and weigh 100 g; cut into slender matchsticks and pat dry. Near rolling time, halve the avocado, lift its pit out with a spoon, scoop out the flesh and weigh 150 g. Slice about 5–6 mm thick. Divide cucumber into four 25 g portions and avocado into four equal portions, about 38 g each. Refrigerate briefly until needed. Keep tempura flakes sealed and dry.

Cut tuna and portion rice: With separate clean equipment, remove tough visible connective tissue, weigh the listed usable amount of cold tuna and cut across its muscle grain where visible into strips about 6–10 mm thick. Short strips can be laid end to end. Divide into four equal portions of about 58 g and refrigerate. Clean the work area and hands. Divide rice into four 80 g portions using a clean utensil.

Lay out the first roll: Trim the first full nori sheet to about 19 x 15 cm and save its dry offcut airtight for another use. Leave the other sheets untrimmed until the first closure check. Place one rectangle shiny side down with its 19 cm edge nearest you. Lightly dampen fingers and shake off extra water, then spread one rice portion evenly, leaving a 1 cm bare strip along the far edge. Take out one portion each of tuna, avocado and cucumber and arrange in a compact horizontal line about 4 cm from the near edge.

Add crunch and roll: Sprinkle one quarter of the tempura flakes, about 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp, along the filling immediately before rolling. Lift the mat's near edge and tuck nori and rice over the filling. Lift the mat clear as you continue forward so it stays outside the roll. Seal on the bare nori edge, barely moistening it if necessary, then press gently through the mat without crushing the avocado. Check the first roll's closure, then cut and serve it following the next step. Trim the remaining sheets to match and continue one roll at a time, cutting and serving each as it is completed for the clearest crunch. Do not build a rice ridge.

Cut and serve: Set seam-side down briefly while preparing a sharp knife. Wipe and lightly dampen the blade, cut each roll in half, then halve each section twice for eight pieces per roll. Wipe and dampen between cuts as needed. Serve promptly as 32 pieces, about two main portions or four appetizer portions. Keep unused fish portions cold while working.

recipes.name: No-Cook Playdough
recipes.description: While not edible, this no-cook playdough stays soft and pliable for months. Cream of tartar acts as preservative and stiffener, preventing stickiness.
recipeIngredient: Liquid Watercolors or Wilton Icing Colors

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and cream of tartar until perfectly combined.
The Emulsion: In a separate heatproof jug, mix the boiling water and vegetable oil. If using one color for the whole batch, add the coloring to the liquid now.
Combine: Slowly pour the liquid into the dry ingredients. Stir with a large spoon until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Once cool enough to handle, dump the dough onto a clean surface. Knead vigorously for 2-3 minutes until it becomes completely smooth, elastic, and non-sticky.
Finish: If you want multiple colors, divide the white dough and knead the colors into each portion separately.
Store: Keep in an airtight container or a zip-top bag to maintain the "Bounce."

recipes.name: Noodle Pudding
recipes.description: Adapted from Mary Later's recipe. Cinnamon warms the rich custard beneath a crisp corn-flake and brown-sugar topping.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Unsalted Butter, melted and divided (divided: 6 oz for custard; 2 oz for topping), plus a little for greasing
2 cups coarsely crushed Corn Flakes (measure after crushing; for topping)
1/2 cup packed Light Brown Sugar (for topping)
1/4 cup Golden Raisins (optional; for half the pudding)

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the dish: Preheat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the center. Grease a room-temperature 9×13-inch glass baking dish, preferably a deep 4-quart model. This is a generous batch; if using a shallower 3-quart dish, have a small greased oven-safe dish ready for any excess.

Cook the noodles: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the egg noodles just until al dente, using the package timing as a guide. Drain well and let cool briefly until warm, not steaming hot.

Mix the custard: In a very large bowl, beat the softened cream cheese with a little of the sour cream until smooth. Stir in the remaining sour cream and cottage cheese; the cottage cheese curds can remain. Whisk in the beaten eggs, granulated sugar, 1½ teaspoons cinnamon, and 6 oz (12 tablespoons) melted butter, cooled until lukewarm.

Assemble: Fold the warm noodles into the custard. For a half-raisin, half-plain pudding, transfer half the mixture to a second bowl and fold ¼ cup golden raisins into that half only. Spoon the two mixtures into opposite halves of the prepared glass dish, keeping them side by side, and gently level the top. For an entirely plain pudding, omit the raisins. Leave at least ½ inch of space below the rim for the topping and slight puffing. Bake any excess separately in the smaller dish, checking it earlier.

Add the topping: Mix 2 cups coarsely crushed corn flakes with ½ cup packed light brown sugar. Drizzle in the remaining 2 oz (4 tablespoons) melted butter and toss until evenly coated. Scatter evenly over the noodles without pressing down. If using an overflow dish, divide the topping between the dishes in proportion to their surface area.

Bake: Bake at 325°F for approximately 65–80 minutes, checking at 60 minutes. The edges should be set, the center should have only a slight wobble without liquid custard, and the topping should be golden and crisp. Loosely tent with foil if the topping browns before the center sets. Use the doneness cues rather than the clock; dish depth affects timing.
Rest and serve: Set the hot glass dish on a dry trivet and let rest for 15 minutes before slicing into 12 portions. The total time includes this rest and an estimated 75-minute bake.

recipes.name: Oatmeal Risotto
recipes.description: Oatmeal risotto treats steel-cut oats with the same respect Italians give Arborio rice - an overnight soak followed by a slow simmer until each grain is creamy outside and slightly chewy at the center. The mashed banana folded in at the end acts like the butter-and-cheese mantecatura in real risotto, creating body without dairy.
recipeIngredient: 3 cups Chicken Broth or Filtered Water

recipeInstructions.text: The Hydration: In a medium bowl, combine the oats and water/broth. Cover and refrigerate overnight at 40°F or below. Keep the oats and all soaking liquid cold until ready to cook.
The Acid Balance: In a small bowl, pour the sherry vinegar over the golden raisins. Let soak while the oats cook.
Simmer: Pour the oats and their soaking liquid into a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Add brown sugar and salt.
Cook: Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the oats are "squeaky" to the bite (al dente).
The Emulsion: Fold in the mashed banana. Cook for 2 more minutes until the banana has melted into the oats, creating a creamy "Bounce."
Serve: Divide into bowls. Top with the vinegar-soaked raisins and a few generous shavings of Parmesan cheese for the final savory High Note.

recipes.name: Soft Pumpkin Cookies
recipes.description: These autumn cookies achieve incredible softness by whisking pumpkin puree directly into creamed butter and sugar, ensuring moisture is fully emulsified before flour is added. The butter-sugar glaze adds sweetness that balances earthy spices.

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: Whisk together flour, baking soda, baking powder, and spices.
Cream: In a large bowl, beat softened butter and sugar until fluffy. Add the pumpkin, egg, and vanilla; beat until smooth.
Combine: Gradually add the dry mix until just combined. The batter will be very soft and scoopable.
Shape: Drop by rounded tablespoons onto greased sheets.
Bake: Bake at 350°F for 15-18 minutes until the edges are firm and the tops are slightly golden.
Glaze: Whisk glaze ingredients until smooth. Drizzle over warm cookies.
Serve: Let cool for 10 minutes to allow the glaze to set into a "Snap."

recipes.name: Old-Fashioned Strawberry Ice Cream
recipes.description: Sliced strawberries macerated in lemon juice and sugar for several hours draw out natural syrup and soften the fruit, preventing them from freezing into icy chunks. Tempering yolks with hot milk and vanilla bean ensures dense, custardy texture that showcases bright strawberries perfectly.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)

recipeInstructions.text: Macerate: Toss strawberries with lemon juice and 1/4 cup sugar. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours until syrupy.
Custard Base: In a saucepan, heat milk, cream, and vanilla bean seeds until simmering.
Emulsify: In a large bowl, whisk yolks, salt, and remaining sugars until pale. Slowly whisk in the hot cream to temper.
Thicken: Return mixture to the pan. Cook over medium-low, stirring constantly, until the custard coats a spoon. Do not boil.
Chill: Remove vanilla pod. Let cool for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours until ice-cold.
Churn: Stir the macerated strawberries (including all juice) into the custard. Pour into ice cream maker and process for 25-35 minutes.
Set: Freeze for 2 hours to harden into the Kitchen Standard texture.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, acidic, rich, herbaceous, entertaining, comfort-food, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Old-Fashioned Vanilla Ice Cream
recipes.description: This classic custard-based vanilla ice cream forms the foundation for countless desserts. Slowly whisking hot milk into egg yolks prevents scrambling while creating stable emulsion.

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: In a small saucepan, heat milk over medium-low until just simmering.
Emulsify: In a medium bowl, whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale yellow. Slowly stream in the hot milk while whisking constantly.
Thicken: Return the mixture to the pan. Heat until it reaches 165°F and coats the back of a spoon. Do not boil.
The Chill: Transfer to a container and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (overnight is best) until cold.
Churn: Stir in the heavy cream and vanilla bean paste. Pour into your ice cream maker.
Set: Churn according to instructions (usually 20 mins). Transfer to a freezer-safe container and freeze for 2 hours before serving.
