recipes.name: Old Fashioned
recipes.description: The Old Fashioned dates to the 1880s, when bartenders started getting fancy with cocktails, adding fruit and elaborate garnishes. Patrons who wanted their drinks made the 'old fashioned way' - just whiskey, sugar, water, and bitters - gave the drink its name.

recipeInstructions.text: Place the sugar cube: in an Old Fashioned glass and saturate with bitters. Add a splash of water.
Muddle the sugar until: dissolved (or simply add simple syrup instead).
Add the whiskey and: fill the glass with one large ice cube.
Stir gently for 10-15: seconds.
Express an orange peel: over the drink by holding it over the glass and giving it a good twist to release the oils. Rub the peel around the rim of the glass and drop it in.
Optionally add a maraschino: cherry. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Orange-Rosemary Chicken with Beets and Fennel
recipes.description: Skin-on chicken thighs with roasted beets, carrots and fennel, finished with orange, garlic and a little butter.
recipeIngredient: 4 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, about 1 kg total, fully thawed
600 g peeled beets, cut into 1/4-inch-thick half-moons
300 g peeled carrots, cut into pieces no thicker than 1/2 inch
300 g trimmed fennel bulb, cut into 1/2-inch wedges with a little core holding each together
2 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary leaves

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and prepare: Heat oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Cut vegetables evenly and pat chicken skin dry. Mix orange juice, zest, melted butter, rosemary and all the garlic in a small bowl; keep aside for the final stage.

Start roots first: Toss beets and carrots with 2 tbsp oil, half the salt and half the pepper on one rimmed sheet. Spread into one layer and roast for 15 minutes. If your sheet cannot hold that layer, use a larger pan or accept an additional cooking batch rather than piling the roots.

Add the chicken tray: On the second sheet, toss fennel with the remaining tablespoon oil and arrange it around the thighs, keeping the skin exposed. Divide remaining salt and pepper over chicken and fennel; sprinkle chili powder over the chicken. Put this tray in the oven, leaving the root tray cooking too.

Roast to separate endpoints: Roast another 40–50 minutes, swapping the trays' rack positions halfway through and turning vegetables. Begin checking thighs around 35 minutes after they enter: the thickest meat, clear of bone, must reach 165°F / 74°C, and the joint should move easily. Check roots with a fork. Remove any component that finishes early instead of letting it overcook.

Finish the vegetables: During the final 8–10 minutes of vegetable cooking, spoon the orange-garlic mixture over the roots and fennel, keeping it off chicken skin. Stir the vegetables and return them to the oven so the garlic cooks and the juice reduces a little. If chicken finishes first, transfer it to a clean plate and continue finishing vegetables separately.

Rest briefly and serve: Let cooked thighs rest about 5 minutes. Divide vegetables among four plates and serve one thigh with each. Spoon a little vegetable-pan liquid around the meat rather than over the skin. Add no extra orange until you taste the finish.

recipes.keywords: American, spicy, sweet, acidic, rich, weekend-dinner, date-night, entertaining, bake, roast

recipes.name: One-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken Thighs
recipes.description: Lemon and herb chicken is the Mediterranean weeknight answer: bone-in, skin-on thighs are forgiving, hard to overcook, and get crispy skin when seared first. The acid from lemon cuts the richness of the thighs, and the herbs - oregano especially - are what makes you taste the Mediterranean.
recipeIngredient: 8 Chicken Thighs, bone-in and skin-on (about 2.5-3 lbs total)
1 lb Potatoes or Root Vegetables (optional, cut into 1-inch pieces)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description:
One-Pan Magic: Everything cooks in the same skillet - proteins, sauce, and vegetables if you add them. The cleanup is minimal.

Let the cooked chicken thighs rest for 5 minutes before serving.

itemListElement.text: The Prep: Pat chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.

Sear the Chicken: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Once shimmering, add chicken skin-side down. Do not move them for 5-6 minutes until the skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear the other side for 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 1 tbsp oil and sliced garlic. Sauté for 30-45 seconds until fragrant. Add fresh oregano and thyme, stirring for 15 seconds.
Deglaze: Pour in lemon juice and chicken stock. Scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon to release any browned bits. Stir in lemon zest.
Return and Roast: Return chicken to the pan, skin-side up. Nestle into the sauce. If using potatoes, add them now around the chicken. Transfer the skillet to a 425°F oven.

Roast: Bake for 12-15 minutes (without vegetables: 12 min; with vegetables: 15-18 min) until the thighs reach an internal temperature of 165°F at the thickest part of the thigh. The skin should be crispy and golden.
Finish: Remove from oven. Taste the sauce and adjust lemon juice, salt, or herbs. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.name: One-Pot Chicken Meatballs with Greens
recipes.description: Chicken meatballs can dry out easily since ground chicken is so lean, but adding Greek yogurt and panko keeps them moist and tender. This one-pot method borrows from Italian-American home cooking: brown the meatballs first for flavor, then pile greens and lemon slices on top to steam together.
recipeIngredient: 1/3 cup Plain Greek Yogurt for richness
1 lb Swiss Chard, sliced into ribbons
1 Lemon, halved (one half sliced, one half juiced)

recipeInstructions.text: The Mix: In a large bowl, combine chicken, yogurt, panko, garlic, scallions, and herbs. Mix gently until just combined.
Shape: Coat your palms in oil. Form the mixture into 14 uniform balls (about 2 inches each).
The Sear: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium. Sauté meatballs for 7 minutes until golden on all sides.
The Layer: In a separate bowl, toss the chard with cumin, salt, and 2 tbsp oil.
The Braise: Pile the chard and lemon slices directly on top of the meatballs. Cover tightly.
Cook: Simmer for 12-15 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through (165°F) and the chard is tender.
Serve: Use a ladle to scoop meatballs and greens together. Squeeze the remaining lemon half over the top for the mandatory High Note.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, rich, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, bake, saute, simmer, steam, braise

recipes.name: One-Pot Chicken, Quinoa & Mushrooms
recipes.description: Chicken thighs and quinoa finish together after mushrooms are browned, with spinach and lemon added at the end.
recipeIngredient: 6 boneless skinless chicken thighs, about 150 g each
255 g dry white quinoa, rinsed and well drained
2 1/2 cups (600 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, plus a little hot water if needed
150 g fresh spinach, washed and roughly chopped
2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Sear in batches: Pat chicken dry and season with half the salt, pepper, rosemary, and paprika. Heat two teaspoons oil in a wide deep sauté pan over medium-high heat. Sear three thighs at a time for about 2–3 minutes per side, lowering heat if spices darken too quickly. Transfer to a plate; the centers are not yet cooked.

Brown mushrooms: Add remaining oil, mushrooms, onion, and remaining salt. Cook about 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until mushroom liquid has mostly evaporated and golden patches appear. Scrape up browned material without burning it.
Add grains and broth: Stir in drained quinoa and broth. Bring to a gentle simmer, then nestle chicken and its juices into the quinoa in one layer. Cover tightly and reduce to a gentle simmer.

Check both components: Cook about 18–22 minutes. Probe each thigh for 165°F / 74°C and check quinoa in several places for the same temperature before tasting it. The seeds should be tender with a little bite and most free liquid absorbed. Extend gently if needed, using the component-specific fixes in troubleshooting rather than overcooking everything together.
Wilt and rest: When chicken and quinoa meet their checks, scatter spinach over the pan. Cover and heat gently for about 2 minutes until wilted. Remove from heat and rest covered for 5 minutes.

Finish with lemon: Lift chicken briefly to a clean plate, fold spinach through quinoa, and stir in half the lemon juice. Taste and add the remainder as needed. Divide quinoa and vegetables into six portions and add one thigh to each.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, smoky, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, sear, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Spicy Thai Noodles
recipes.description: This Thai-inspired one-pot noodle dish builds the sauce directly in the pasta pot, using residual heat to emulsify the sriracha-ginger glaze without extra fat. Scrambling eggs separately first keeps them distinct with bright yellow texture rather than forming a coating.

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: Cook pasta in a large pot of salted water according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
The Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, Sriracha, and grated ginger until smooth.
The Eggs: In the same large pot, heat 1 tbsp oil. Scramble the eggs with a pinch of red pepper flakes until just set. Remove and set aside with the pasta.
The Veg: Add remaining oil to the pot. Sauté zucchini, mushrooms, and carrots for 5 minutes over high heat until tender-crisp.
Bind: Turn heat to low. Return the pasta and eggs to the pot. Pour the sauce over everything.
Toss: Toss vigorously for 1 minute until the noodles are glossy and the sauce has thickened.
Serve: Remove from heat. Stir in the green onions, cilantro, and crushed peanuts. Serve hot or cold for the Kitchen Standard experience.

recipes.name: Onigiri (Japanese Rice Balls)
recipes.description: Onigiri are Japanese rice balls - simple, transportable, and a staple of bentos and home cooking for centuries. What makes them special is the ritual: the rice is still warm when shaped, and the small amount of salt on your hands seasons the outside just enough.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups Cooked Japanese Short-Grain Rice (warm or room temperature)
Filling A: 4 oz Canned Tuna, drained and mixed with 1 tbsp Mayo + 1 tsp Soy Sauce
Filling C: 1/4 cup Salmon Flakes (fresh cooked or canned) mixed with 1/2 tsp Soy Sauce
Filling D: 2 tbsp Sesame Seeds mixed with 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
Water in a small bowl (for wet hands)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description:
Filling Ideas: Keep fillings minimal - a single flavor is more traditional. Tuna mayo, umeboshi (pickled plum), grilled salmon, kombu (kelp), or just sesame salt all work beautifully.

Hand Temperature: Warm hands make shaping easier and prevent the rice from cooling too much. If your hands get cold, re-wet with warm water and re-salt.

Nori Texture: For maximum crispness, wrap nori just before serving. For softer nori, wrap 30 minutes ahead and let the moisture from the rice soften it slightly.

itemListElement.text: Cook the Rice: If starting from scratch, prepare 1 cup Japanese short-grain rice according to package directions (usually 1:1 ratio with water). Let rest for 10 minutes after cooking. Use warm rice for the best texture when shaping.

Prepare the Work Surface: Have a small bowl of water nearby. Wet your hands slightly and sprinkle a pinch of salt into your palm. This is crucial - it prevents sticking and adds a subtle salty flavor to the outer rice.

Form the Triangle (Basic Shape): Take about 1/2 cup cooked rice in your palm. Make a small indent in the center with your thumb, creating a pocket about the size of a marble. Place 1 tbsp of your chosen filling into the pocket.

Encase the Filling: Cup your hand to gently bring rice up and around the filling, enclosing it completely. You should have a ball of rice with filling inside. Squeeze gently but firmly - you want it compact enough to hold together but not so tight that it becomes dense.

Shape into Triangle: Place the rice ball on your work surface. Using both hands (re-wet and re-salt if needed), gently shape it into a triangle by applying even pressure on three sides. The shape comes from your hands, not from pressing into a mold. A triangular onigiri is iconic and practical - it sits flat and is easy to wrap.

Wrap with Nori: Cut nori into strips about 1 inch wide and 3-4 inches long. Wrap one strip around the middle of the onigiri, like a belt. The nori will stick to the rice from its slight moisture. If wrapping right before serving, the nori stays crispy; if you wrap earlier, it softens slightly from the rice moisture.

Garnish and Store: Sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature. For make-ahead service, refrigerate promptly at 40°F or below and transport with an ice pack. Count preparation and service together: discard perishable onigiri left out over 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. If frozen, thaw in the refrigerator rather than on the counter. Keep nori separate until serving for crispness.

recipes.name: Chocolate Sandwich Cookie Cheesecake
recipes.description: A dense chocolate cheesecake with a thin chocolate-cookie base, chocolate-creme cookie pieces through the filling and more cookies baked on top.
recipeIngredient: 32 regular-size chocolate sandwich cookies with chocolate-flavored creme, about 14–15 g each, divided; keep the creme filling
32 oz (907 g) full-fat block cream cheese, softened as directed
8 oz (227 g) semisweet baking chocolate, chopped
1 tsp neutral oil, for greasing the pan

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the pan and cookies: Once the cheese is softened as described above, heat the oven to 325°F / 163°C with a rack in the middle. Grease the bottom and sides of the springform pan with the measured oil. Finely crush twelve whole cookies, creme included. Quarter the other twenty cookies and keep all their crumbs. Measure a level 1 1/2 cups of these pieces and crumbs without packing for the filling; set all the remaining pieces aside for the top.

Bake the crust and melt the chocolate: Press the fine crumbs evenly and firmly across the bottom of the pan, with no bare patches. Set the pan on a rimmed baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes. Cool on a rack while mixing the filling. Put the chopped chocolate in a dry microwave-safe bowl and heat at half power in 20–30-second bursts, stirring between each, until just melted. Let it become lukewarm but still fluid; avoid getting water in it.

Smooth the cheese: Beat the softened cream cheese, sugar and vanilla at low to medium-low speed until smooth, about 2–3 minutes, stopping to scrape the bottom and sides of the bowl. Mix in the lukewarm chocolate until the color is even. Scrape again; avoid whipping the mixture fluffy.

Add eggs and cookies: Add the eggs one at a time on low speed, mixing only until each disappears. Scrape the bowl and fold in the measured 1 1/2 cups of cookie pieces with a spatula. Do not taste the raw batter. Spread gently over the cooled crust and scatter all the remaining quartered cookies and crumbs over the top.

Bake to a set center: Bake on the rimmed sheet for about 50–70 minutes, checking at 50 minutes. The edges should be set and the central few inches should tremble together when the pan is nudged, without a liquid wave. Check the filling in the center with an instant-read thermometer, avoiding cookie pieces and the pan base; it must reach at least 160°F / 71°C. Continue in 5-minute intervals if needed, then remove to a rack.

Cool and chill: After about 10 minutes, carefully run a thin knife between the cake and the pan wall without opening the clasp. Cool on the rack for about 1 hour total, then refrigerate in the pan, loosely covered and with space around it. Refrigerate within 2 hours of leaving the oven, or within 1 hour if the kitchen is above 90°F / 32°C. Once cold, cover well. Chill for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until cold and firm through the center.

Unmold and slice: Release the clasp and lift off the ring; leave the cake on its base for support. Cut into sixteen slices with a sharp knife, wiping it clean between cuts. Serve chilled, with coffee or unsweetened tea if desired.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats
recipes.description: Overnight oats are essentially Bircher muesli, invented by Swiss physician Maximilian Bircher-Benner around 1900. The principle is simple: oats hydrate overnight in liquid, softening into a creamy, pudding-like texture without any heat.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Old-Fashioned Rolled Oats (not instant, not steel-cut)
Toppings: fresh fruit, nut butter, granola, toasted coconut, or nuts

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: In a jar or airtight container, stir together oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, maple syrup, vanilla, and salt. Make sure the chia seeds are distributed throughout -- they clump if left on the surface.
Refrigerate: Seal the container and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight (up to 5 days).
Adjust: In the morning, stir the oats. If they are too thick, add a splash of milk and stir to loosen. If too thin, add a spoonful of oats and let sit for 10 minutes.
Top and Serve: Add your toppings of choice. Serve cold straight from the jar, or microwave for 1-2 minutes if you prefer warm oats.

recipes.name: Pad See Ew
recipes.description: Soy-seasoned wide rice noodles with chicken, Chinese broccoli, and egg, finished in five small batches for a home stove.
recipeIngredient: 750 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced about 1/4 inch thick
1 tbsp regular soy sauce, for the chicken
1 tsp neutral oil, for the chicken
1000 g fresh wide rice noodles (sen yai); see dried-noodle substitution
500 g Chinese broccoli (gai lan), trimmed; thick stems sliced 1/4 inch thick and leaves cut into 2-inch pieces
4 tbsp neutral oil, for cooking, divided
2 tbsp water, for steaming the broccoli, plus small splashes if needed
2 tbsp Thai sweet dark soy sauce
1 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar, optional, divided among plates to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare chicken and noodles: Toss chicken with marinade soy, cornstarch, and its teaspoon of oil; refrigerate during preparation. Gently separate flexible fresh noodles and divide into five 200 g portions. If cold and stiff, warm briefly according to their package before separating. Use the substitution instructions for dried noodles.

Organize sauce and vegetables: Mix oyster sauce, sauce soy, Thai sweet dark soy, sugar, sauce water, and white pepper until uniform. Cut broccoli, keeping stems and leaves separate. Chop garlic and beat the eggs.

Cook chicken in two batches: Heat 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Spread half the chicken in one layer. Leave 1–2 minutes, then turn and stir-fry until several thick slices reach 165°F / 74°C, about 4–6 minutes total. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat with another 1 1/2 tsp oil and the rest of the chicken.

Cook vegetables and eggs: Reduce heat to medium. Add 2 tsp oil and stir garlic for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Add broccoli stems and the steaming water; cover for about 2–3 minutes, until stems are almost tender. Uncover, add leaves and stir-fry 1–2 minutes until wilted and water has evaporated. Transfer to a bowl. Add 1 tsp oil, then beaten eggs; stir gently until fully set with no wet streaks, about 1–2 minutes. Transfer out. Divide chicken, broccoli, egg, and well-stirred sauce into five portions.

Finish one serving: Heat about one-fifth of the remaining 2 tbsp oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Add one noodle portion and one sauce portion. Lift and fold gently to coat, then spread and leave about 15–20 seconds. Turn and repeat once or twice for a few toasted patches, reducing heat if sauce starts to burn. Add one portion each of chicken, broccoli and egg with their share of any cooking juices. Fold until hot throughout, about 3–4 minutes total for this final batch. Add a small splash of water only if the noodles need loosening.

Taste, plate, and repeat: Taste the first portion and adjust the remaining sauce if necessary. Plate promptly and repeat step 5 four more times. Offer the measured vinegar at the table in small amounts. Serve plates as they finish, with an optional cool cucumber side; the main already contains its noodles, protein and vegetables.

recipes.name: Pad Thai
recipes.description: In the 1930s, Thai Prime Minister Plaek Phibunsongkhram launched a cultural campaign to create a unified national identity, which included promoting a 'national dish. ' Pad Thai was born from this movement - a street food that used local ingredients and represented Thai cuisine to the world.

recipeInstructions.text: The Soak: Place dry noodles in a large bowl of cool water. Soak for 40 minutes until flexible but still firm. Drain.
The Crunch: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok. Fry peanuts until golden; remove. Fry tofu matchsticks until golden and firm; remove.
Aromatics: Heat 1 tbsp oil. Sauté garlic, shallots, and dried chili for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the drained noodles and the tamarind mixture (sugar, fish sauce).
Toss: Stir-fry over high heat. If the noodles feel too firm, add 1 tbsp of water at a time until they are chewy and translucent.
The Egg: Push noodles to the side. Scramble the egg until set, then fold into the noodles.
Combine: Add the shrimp and cooked tofu. Toss for 2 minutes until shrimp are pink and just opaque.
Finish: Fold in the bean sprouts and chives. Toss for 15 seconds.
Serve: Mound on a plate. Top with crushed peanuts, extra sprouts, and a lime wedge.

recipes.keywords: Thai, spicy, sweet, acidic, comfort-food, fry, saute, boil

recipes.name: Pad Woon Sen
recipes.description: Pad woon sen is a Thai glass noodle stir-fry that's lighter than pad thai. Mung bean glass noodles should be soaked in hot (not boiling) water for exactly 10 minutes to reach their optimal translucent texture.
recipeIngredient: 6.3 oz Dried Mung Bean Glass Noodles

recipeInstructions.text: Noodles: Soak mung bean noodles in hot water for 10 minutes. Drain and rinse in cold water.
The Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together oyster sauce, fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar.
The Egg: In a wok, heat a splash of oil. Scramble the eggs with a pinch of salt until just set. Remove and roughly chop.
The Crunch: Heat oil until smoking. Sauté cabbage and peppers for 3-4 minutes until charred at the edges but still firm. Transfer to the egg plate.
Aromatics: Add fresh oil. Sauté onions and carrots for 2 minutes until soft. Add garlic and sauté for 45 seconds.
Bind: Add the drained noodles and the sauce. Toss vigorously over medium-high for 3 minutes until the noodles are glossy and have absorbed the liquid.
Finish: Return the eggs and charred veg to the wok. Stir in the Thai chile and scallions for the mandatory High Note.
Serve: Serve hot or at room temperature for the Kitchen Standard fuel profile.

recipes.name: Pan Fried Noodles with Shrimp
recipes.description: Pan-fried noodles (gon chow min) are a Cantonese restaurant specialty. The technique: boil noodles briefly, then pan-fry them into a crispy "bird's nest" cake - crunchy on the outside, soft inside.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Large Shrimp, peeled and deveined
8 oz Fresh Hong Kong-style Egg Noodles
4 oz Yu Choy or Bok Choy

recipeInstructions.text: The Crunch: Toss shrimp with baking soda. Let sit for 5 minutes, then rinse thoroughly and pat dry.
The Noodles: Boil noodles for 1 minute (al dente). Drain and rinse with cold water. Shake dry.

The Cake: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pan. Spread noodles in an even layer. Fry undisturbed for 5 minutes until the bottom is a golden-brown disc. Flip (in sections if needed) and crisp the other side. Transfer to a platter.
The Veg: Blanch the greens in boiling water for 30 seconds. Arrange around the noodles.
The Sear: In a hot wok or skillet, sear the shrimp for 1 minute per side. Add ginger and garlic for 30 seconds. Splash in the Shaoxing wine.
The Gravy: Pour in the sauce mixture (stock, oyster sauce, soy, pepper). Bring to a boil. Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until thickened and clear.
Serve: Pour the hot shrimp gravy directly over the center of the crispy noodle cake. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Panang Curry with Chicken
recipes.description: Thin chicken slices and red pepper in a small amount of rich coconut curry sauce, thickened with ground peanuts and scented with makrut lime leaves.
recipeIngredient: 450 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced about 1/2 inch thick
300 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, divided
3 tbsp panang curry paste, or less for a particularly strong paste
1 tbsp neutral oil, only if needed when frying the paste
2 tbsp unsalted roasted peanuts, finely ground
150 g red bell pepper, thinly sliced
4 makrut lime leaves, central ribs removed and leaves sliced into very fine threads
2 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar, added gradually to taste
1 tbsp fish sauce, added gradually only as needed
2 tbsp water, used only if needed to loosen the sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Grind roasted peanuts to a fine meal. Remove the stiff central ribs from lime leaves, stack the leaves and slice into very fine threads. Slice pepper before handling chicken, then slice chicken and clean the work area. Measure the coconut milk and reserve 180 ml, leaving 120 ml for the paste.

Cook the paste: Simmer the 120 ml coconut milk in a wide skillet over medium heat about 3–5 minutes until thickened, stirring. Add panang paste and stir for about 2 minutes until fragrant. If no oil releases and paste is sticking, add the measured neutral oil. Do not continue cooking a dry paste simply to force visible splitting.

Thicken the sauce: Add the reserved coconut milk, finely ground peanuts, half the lime-leaf threads and half the sugar. Simmer gently about 3–5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens enough to leave a brief spatula trail across the pan.

Cook chicken and pepper: Add chicken and pepper, separating the slices in the sauce. Simmer gently about 6–10 minutes, stirring, until several thick chicken slices reach 165°F / 74°C and the pepper is tender with a little bite. Use the measured water in small splashes only if the sauce becomes too dry before chicken cooks.

Balance and finish: Taste the fully cooked curry. Start with about 1 tsp fish sauce and add more only if needed; add remaining sugar only if wanted. Fold in the remaining fine lime-leaf threads and warm for about 30 seconds. Serve four modest main portions with separately prepared plain rice.

recipes.keywords: Thai, sweet, rich, weeknight, comfort-food, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Parish’s Blueberry Crisp
recipes.description: A crisp lives or dies by its topping - here, the secret is cooking the butter to brown butter stage (dark milk solids, nutty aroma) before mixing with the dry ingredients, so every crumb tastes like toasted nuts. The blueberry filling is tightened with cornstarch and lemon juice, preventing a soupy cobbler while keeping the fruit's bright acidity front and center.

recipeInstructions.text: The Fruit: In a saucepan, combine blueberries, 1/4 cup water, and lemon juice. Whisk sugar and cornstarch together and stir into the fruit. Cook over medium for 4 minutes until the juices thicken. Pour into a greased 9-inch square dish.

The Crumble: In a small pan, melt butter over medium-high. Continue heating for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the milk solids turn dark brown and smell like toasted nuts. Remove from heat immediately.
The Mix: In a large bowl, whisk flour, brown sugar, and salt. Drizzle the brown butter over the mix. Stir with a fork until large, crispy clumps form.
Bake: Sprinkle the crumble generously over the fruit. Bake at 350°F for 30 minutes until the fruit is bubbling and the topping is a deep mahogany.
Serve: Let cool for 10 minutes to allow the syrup to set. Serve warm with a scoop of Vanilla Ice Cream.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, comfort-food, bake, simmer

recipes.name: Parmigiano Reggiano Cheesecake
recipes.description: Savory cheesecake with Parmigiano-Reggiano is a Northern Italian tradition that blurs the line between cheese course and dessert - the aged cheese brings nutty, crystalline depth against the graham cracker crust. The water bath is non-negotiable: it creates gentle, even heat that prevents the edges from overcooking while the center sets.
recipeIngredient: 40 oz (5 packs) Cream Cheese, room temperature

recipeInstructions.text: The Crust: Pulse the cheese, crackers, and seeds in a food processor. Mix with butter and press into a 10-inch springform pan. Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes. Cool.
The Filling: Cream the cream cheese and sugar until silky. Add the sour cream, vanilla, and grated Parmigiano.
Eggs: Add eggs one at a time, mixing on low speed to avoid aerating the batter (bubbles cause cracks!).
The Seal: Wrap the bottom of the pan in heavy-duty foil. Place in a large roasting pan.
The Bath: Pour the batter into the crust. Pour hot water into the roasting pan until it reaches halfway up the side of the springform pan.
Bake: Bake at 325°F for 85-90 minutes until the edges are set but the center still has a slight jiggle.
The Chill: Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let it sit for 1 hour. Then refrigerate for at least 6 hours.

recipes.name: Pasta with Abruzzi-Style Lamb Sauce
recipes.description: This ragù comes from Abruzzo, the mountainous region in central Italy where sheep farming has been a way of life for centuries. Abruzzese cuisine is rustic and hearty, designed to sustain shepherds in the mountains.
recipeIngredient: 3/4 lb Boneless Lamb (Leg or Shoulder), finely diced or ground
1 (28 oz) can Whole Peeled Tomatoes, crushed by hand

recipeInstructions.text: Render: Heat olive oil in a large skillet. Add the onion and pancetta. Cook until the pancetta fat has melted and the onions are gold (8 mins).
Sear: Add the diced lamb and rosemary. Season with salt and pepper. Brown the meat aggressively until it develops a crust.
Deglaze: Pour in the white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release the fond. Simmer until the wine has evaporated by 75%.
Simmer: Add the crushed tomatoes and their juices. Reduce heat to low and simmer gently for 30-40 minutes until the sauce is thick and the fat starts to separate.
Boil: Cook pasta in salted water until al dente.
Combine: Toss the hot pasta directly into the lamb sauce. Add the Pecorino and toss to coat.
Serve: Serve with extra cheese and a crack of black pepper.

recipes.keywords: Italian, rich, comfort-food, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Pasta with Sausage, Basil & Mustard
recipes.description: Hot Italian sausage in a creamy whole-grain mustard sauce with a generous handful of fresh basil.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb raw hot Italian pork sausage, casings removed
Red pepper flakes, a pinch or to taste
Parmesan, for grating at the table
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from Nigel Slater’s recipe at Food & Wine.

itemListElement.text: Start water and prepare: Bring pasta water to a boil. Remove sausage casings, measure sauce ingredients and slice basil. Season water moderately, then time pasta by its package so it finishes near the sauce.

Brown and cook sausage: Heat olive oil in a broad deep skillet over medium-high. Add sausage and break into small crumbles. Cook about 8–12 minutes, stirring, until browned in places and representative thicker pieces reach 160°F / 71°C. Brown in rounds if necessary, sharing the oil between them, then return all cooked meat to the pan.
Reduce wine: Add wine and scrape up browned bits. Simmer about 5 minutes, or until the liquid is reduced roughly by half; pan width changes the time.

Make the sauce: Lower heat, stir in cream, about two-thirds of the mustard and the pepper flakes. Simmer gently about 2–3 minutes, until lightly thickened. Taste and add the remaining mustard if wanted. Meanwhile cook pasta until tender with a little bite and reserve the listed water amount before draining.

Toss and serve: Add pasta to the sauce and fold over low heat just until coated, adding warm pasta water in small amounts if too thick. Remove from heat and fold in basil. Taste before adding salt or pepper. Divide into the intended portions and offer Parmesan for grating at the table.

recipes.keywords: Italian, savory, acidic, umami, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, comfort-food, date-night, saute, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Patatas Bravas
recipes.description: The double-cook method is what separates bar-standard patatas bravas from unforgettable ones. Parboiling the potatoes first roughens the edges and gelatinizes the starch, creating a shatteringly crisp exterior when they hit the hot oil.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs Yukon Gold Potatoes, peeled and cut into 1.5-inch irregular chunks
2 tsp Smoked Paprika (pimenton de la Vera, hot or sweet)
1/2 tsp Cayenne Pepper, or to taste
1/3 cup Mayonnaise (use vegan mayonnaise for the vegan option; for alioli)

recipeInstructions.text: Make the Bravas Sauce: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 5-6 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds. Stir in the smoked paprika, sweet paprika, and cayenne. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the crushed tomatoes, sugar, and salt. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until thickened. Stir in the sherry vinegar. For a smooth sauce, blend with an immersion blender or pass through a sieve. Set aside.
Make the Alioli: Whisk together the mayonnaise, grated garlic, and lemon juice. Season with a pinch of salt. Refrigerate until serving.

Parboil the Potatoes: Place the potato chunks in a large pot of generously salted cold water. Bring to a boil and cook for 8-10 minutes until the edges are tender but the centers still have some resistance. Drain well and spread on a sheet pan to steam dry for 10 minutes. This step is crucial for crispiness.

Fry the Potatoes: Heat 4 cups of oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven to 375F. Working in batches to avoid crowding, fry the potatoes for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until deeply golden and crispy. Transfer to a wire rack set over a sheet pan. Season immediately with flaky sea salt.
Serve: Pile the hot potatoes on a warm serving platter. Drizzle generously with the bravas sauce and dot with the alioli. Serve immediately with toothpicks or small forks -- this is tapas, after all.

recipes.keywords: Spanish, spicy, savory, smoky, acidic, entertaining, game-day, date-night, fry, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Patate al Forno
recipes.description: Patate al forno are classic Italian oven-roasted potatoes - a Sunday staple in Roman homes. The secret to crispy edges is drying the potatoes thoroughly after cutting; any moisture will cause them to steam instead of crisp.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs Yukon Gold Potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 450°F (mandatory for snap). Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Dry: Cube the potatoes. Place them in a bowl and pat bone-dry with multiple paper towels.
Toss: Add the olive oil, salt, garlic powder, and rosemary. Toss vigorously until every chunk is heavily coated.
Spread: Spread the potatoes in a single layer on the pan. If they are crowded, they will steam instead of crisp.
Roast: Bake for 35-40 minutes. Flip with a metal spatula halfway through. They are done when they are deep mahogany gold and "pop" when bitten.
Serve: Sprinkle with a final pinch of sea salt and serve immediately.

recipes.keywords: Italian, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, entertaining, holiday, potluck, bake, roast, steam

recipes.name: Peach Pie Biscuit Bombs
recipes.description: These are a shortcut's triumph - using refrigerated biscuits legitimately, not apologetically. The filling is a lesson in flavor layering: warm peaches, creamy melted brie (unexpected richness), brown butter (nutty depth), and brown sugar with cinnamon (familiar sweetness).
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Fresh Peaches, sliced into 1-inch pieces

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 375°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Split: Pull each raw biscuit in half horizontally.
Layer: Place 3 peach slices and 1 tsp of Brie in the center of the bottom half. Sprinkle with brown sugar and cinnamon. Drizzle with a drop of honey.
Seal: Place the top half back on. Pinch the edges firmly and roll gently in your palms to form a uniform "ball." Arrange 2 inches apart on the pan.
The Sizzle: In a small pan, melt 3 tbsp butter until it crackles and turns nutty brown. Brush each "bomb" generously with the brown butter.
Bake: Bake for 12-15 minutes until the tops are deep golden brown and the biscuit has a flaky "Bounce."
Serve: Brush once more with the remaining brown butter. Serve warm while the Brie is molten.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, rich, entertaining, kid-friendly, bake

recipes.name: Peach Pie Pancakes
recipes.description: The secret to peach pie pancakes that aren't heavy is using Greek yogurt as the primary binder, creating a dense, custardy texture that mimics pie filling without excessive oil. Making small, 2-tablespoon "silver dollar" pancakes ensures the diced peaches are distributed evenly and the pancake cooks through before the fruit releases too much moisture.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Plain Greek Yogurt for richness

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt.
The Emulsion: In a separate bowl, whisk yogurt, milk, vanilla, and melted butter until perfectly smooth.
Combine: Gradually add the dry mix to the wet in 4 parts. Stir with a spatula until just incorporated. Small lumps are mandatory for a light texture.
Fold: Gently fold in the diced peaches.
Prep: Heat a non-stick skillet over low-medium heat (crucial for whole wheat). Lightly grease with oil spray.
Pour: Drop 2-tbsp portions onto the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes until bubbles form and the edges look set.
Flip: Flip gently and cook for 1-2 more minutes until golden brown.
Serve: Serve with warm maple syrup and a few extra fresh peach slices.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, kid-friendly, weekend-project, no-cook

recipes.name: Peach Salad with Tomatoes & Beets
recipes.description: Tender golden beets, ripe tomatoes and peaches with a lemon-honey shallot dressing, goat cheese, mint and thyme.
recipeIngredient: 2 medium golden beets, scrubbed, tops trimmed
3 medium ripe but firm peaches, pitted and sliced
3 tbsp fresh mint leaves, torn if large
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Water, for the covered beet baking dish

recipeInstructions.text: Bake beets: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Put scrubbed beets in a small roasting dish with about 1 inch of water. Cover tightly and bake until a thin knife slides easily to the center, checking after about 50 minutes and continuing as needed, often 60–75 minutes. Keep some water in the dish; carefully add hot water if it is drying out.

Cool and slice: Remove the cover carefully, keeping away from the escaping steam, and lift beets from the water. Cool until comfortable to handle, rub off skins, trim roots and cut into 1/4-inch slices. Spread slices on a plate and let them cool fully before assembling; allow roughly 20–30 minutes total cooling, longer if needed.

Prepare dressing and fruit: While beets cool, whisk oil, half the measured lemon juice, honey and shallot together. Season to taste. Slice tomatoes into 1/4-inch rounds. Pit and slice peaches and toss gently with the remaining half of the lemon juice.

Assemble: Layer cool beet and tomato slices on a wide platter and season lightly with salt and pepper. Arrange peach slices over them and spoon over the shallot dressing without stirring the fragile layers.
Finish: Scatter with goat cheese, mint and thyme. Serve promptly so the herbs remain fresh and the fruit holds its shape.

recipes.name: Peanut Noodles
recipes.description: Peanut noodles are Chinese-American comfort food born from the post-WWII boom when peanut butter became accessible in Chinese restaurants. What started as a Chinatown fusion dish is now everywhere - and for good reason.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Noodles (spaghetti, angel hair, or wheat noodles)
1/4 tsp Red Pepper Flakes (adjust to taste)
1/4 to 1/2 cup Warm Water (to achieve sauce consistency)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description:
Warm or Cold: Eat immediately while warm, or chill and serve cold the next day. Both are completely valid.

Customization: Top with shredded carrots, cucumber, steamed edamame, or blanched broccoli. This is a base - build on it.

itemListElement.text: Make the Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, minced garlic, ginger, and red pepper flakes. The mixture will be thick. Whisk in warm water a little at a time until you reach the consistency you want - think thickened pasta sauce that clings to noodles, not a soup. Taste and adjust for salt, heat, and acid.

Cook the Noodles: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add noodles and cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well - don't rinse (the starch helps the sauce cling). If making this ahead, toss drained noodles with 1 tsp sesame oil to prevent sticking.

Combine: In a large bowl, add warm or room-temperature noodles. Pour peanut sauce over the noodles and toss until every strand is coated. If the sauce seems too thick, add a few splashes of warm water.
Finish: Sprinkle with sliced green onions, fresh cilantro, sesame seeds, and roasted peanuts if using. Serve with lime wedges on the side.
To Serve Cold: Let the dressed noodles cool to room temperature (or chill for up to 4 hours). The sauce will continue to coat as it cools. If it tightens, add a splash of warm water before serving.

recipes.name: Pear & Spinach Salad
recipes.description: Baby spinach and crisp pear with softened raw onion and a sharp honey-Dijon dressing.
recipeIngredient: 5 cups baby spinach, washed if needed and dried
1 large ripe but firm Bosc pear, cored and thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Ice water, for soaking onion, discarded afterward

recipeInstructions.text: Soak onion: Put thinly sliced onion in ice water for 10 minutes. Meanwhile wash and dry spinach if needed and prepare the dressing. Drain onion and pat thoroughly dry.
Whisk dressing: Combine Dijon, vinegar, the measured dressing water, olive oil and honey. Whisk until smooth. Add salt and pepper to taste; the mustard already contains salt.

Assemble: Core and thinly slice pear. Put spinach, pear and dry onion in a wide bowl. Start with about one-third of the mixed dressing and lift gently to coat. Taste a leaf with pear, then add more dressing only as needed; reserve any excess.
Serve: Adjust black pepper if desired and divide among side plates. Serve immediately while spinach retains its texture.

recipes.name: Peking Duck
recipes.description: Peking duck from Beijing is famous for its crackling-crisp skin. The secret: pour boiling water over the raw duck to tighten the skin, brush with maltose syrup, then air-dry uncovered in the fridge for 24-48 hours.
recipeIngredient: 3 tbsp Sweet Bean Sauce (Tian Mian Jiang)

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Pat duck bone-dry. Rub 2 tbsp salt over the skin and cavity. Let rest for 1 hour.
The Blanch: Pour 6 cups of boiling water slowly over the entire duck skin (both sides). You will see the skin tighten instantly.
The Lacquer: Whisk maltose, boiling water, and vinegar. Brush a heavy layer over the duck. Let dry for 1 hour, then brush a second layer.
The Dehydrate: Place duck on a wire rack over a tray. Refrigerate uncovered for 24-48 hours until the skin feels like parchment paper.
Thermal Prep: Bring duck to room temp. Stuff the cavity with aromatics and apples. Seal the opening with skewers.
Bake: Preheat convection oven to 390°F (or 425°F conventional). Roast for 15 minutes.
Roast: Lower heat to 350°F. Roast for another 60 minutes until the internal temp is 165°F and the skin is dark mahogany. Rest for 15 minutes.
The Sauce: Simmer sweet bean sauce, sugar, and a spoonful of rendered duck fat until bubbling.
Serve: Slice the skin and meat separately. Serve with thin pancakes, julienned scallions, and cucumber.

recipes.name: Whole-Berry Cranberry Sauce
recipes.description: A spoonable cranberry sauce with some tender berry pieces, a light orange fragrance and an optional fuller orange variation.
recipeIngredient: 340 g fresh or frozen cranberries, divided
1 strip orange peel, about 2 by 1 inches, without white pith

recipeInstructions.text: Sort and divide: Rinse and drain fresh cranberries, discarding spoiled berries. Set aside 85 g of the total for the later addition; the other 255 g go in first. Keep frozen berries frozen until each addition. Prepare a thin orange-peel strip with no thick white pith.
Dissolve the sugar: In a 2-quart saucepan, combine water, sugar, orange peel and salt. Heat over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves and the liquid begins to simmer.

Cook the first berries: Add the 255 g cranberries, return to a gentle boil and reduce heat to a steady simmer. Cook about eight to ten minutes, stirring occasionally, until most berries have split. Keep clear of hot splashes; do not crush every berry smooth.

Tenderize the remaining berries: Add the reserved 85 g and simmer another three to five minutes, or until those berries are tender when pressed with a spoon. Some may retain their shape. The hot sauce should still flow; it will thicken as it cools. Remove the orange-peel strip.

Cool and chill: Put a small spoonful on a cool plate to assess flavor and body once cool enough to taste. Transfer the main batch to a shallow heatproof container and refrigerate promptly, loosely covered while cooling and covered fully once cold. Allow about two and a half hours to chill, or refrigerate overnight. Stir gently before serving two to three tablespoons per person.

recipes.name: Cream Cheese Mashed Potatoes
recipes.description: Yukon Gold potatoes mashed gently with warm butter, half-and-half and cream cheese, with enough liquid for a soft mound rather than a sticky paste.
recipeIngredient: 1360 g peeled Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into even 1-inch pieces
3 L cold water, or enough to cover potatoes by about 1 inch
12 g salt, for the cooking water
75 g unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
115 g cream cheese, cut into small pieces
3/4 cup (180 ml) half-and-half, plus up to 1/4 cup (60 ml) more if needed
1/2 tsp fine salt, for finishing, divided

recipeInstructions.text: Cut and cover: Peel and trim enough potatoes to weigh 1360 g, then cut into even one-inch pieces. Briefly rinse, put in a large pot and add about three liters cold water to cover by an inch. Add the twelve grams of cooking-water salt.

Simmer until fully tender: Bring to a boil, reduce to a steady simmer and cook about eighteen to twenty-two minutes. Test several pieces with a knife and taste a cooled piece; the centers should be fully soft, not just puncturable. While they cook, warm butter, cream cheese and the initial 180 ml half-and-half together over low heat, stirring until the butter melts and the cream cheese softens. Do not boil the dairy.

Drain and dry briefly: Drain thoroughly. Return the potatoes to the pot over low heat for one to two minutes, shaking or turning gently until the surfaces lose their wet sheen. Remove from heat before they brown or stick.

Mash gently: Pass hot potatoes through a ricer or use a hand masher until the large pieces are gone. Fold in the warm dairy mixture in two additions with a spatula. Stop when combined. If too stiff, warm and add the optional extra half-and-half a tablespoon at a time until it holds a soft mound.

Taste and serve: Fold in pepper and half the finishing salt, then taste; add the rest only if needed. The cooking-water salt was largely drained away, while cream cheese contributes its own seasoning. Serve about three-quarters of a cup per person alongside the main.

recipes.keywords: American, rich, buttery, tangy, holiday, entertaining, comfort-food, weeknight, boil, simmer

recipes.name: Peruvian-Style Beef Empanadas
recipes.description: Mild beef-and-onion empanadas with cumin, sweet paprika and a little tomato paste, baked in store-bought discs and served with lime.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp yellow bell pepper, finely diced
additional fine salt, to taste, only if needed
12 5-inch empanada discs labeled for baking, one 12-count package at the original yield; thawed as directed on the package
1 tsp water for egg wash, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Thaw the discs according to their package before starting; keep covered and refrigerated until needed. Finely chop the vegetables so they fit comfortably inside the pastry. Set out a shallow heatproof dish for cooling the filling and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment.

Brown the beef: Set out olive oil and 85/15 ground beef. Heat the oil in a 10- to 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the beef in a thin layer and leave it undisturbed for about 2 minutes, until browned underneath. Break it into small crumbles and cook another 4–6 minutes, stirring, until cooked through to 160°F / 71°C. Spoon off pooled fat, leaving a thin film in the pan. Transfer the cooked beef to a clean bowl.

Soften the vegetables: Lower the heat to medium and add yellow onion and yellow bell pepper to the same skillet. Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until fully softened and the onion is translucent with lightly golden edges. Lower the heat if the browned bits start to blacken.

Bloom the spices: Lower the heat to medium-low. Stir in garlic clove, ground cumin, sweet paprika, dried oregano, and ground turmeric for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant; do not let the garlic or paprika scorch.
Cook the tomato paste: Stir in tomato paste for about 1 minute, until it darkens slightly and coats the vegetables.

Finish the filling: Return the beef and add unsalted beef broth, fine salt, and ground black pepper, using the lower end of the broth range first. Scrape up the browned bits and stir over medium heat for 1–2 minutes. Add the remaining broth only if the filling seems dry. Stop when moist crumbles cling together lightly and a spatula drawn across the pan leaves no puddle.

Taste and cool: Taste the fully cooked filling and add additional fine salt only if needed. Spread it in a thin layer in the shallow dish and refrigerate promptly for about 20–30 minutes, or until cool throughout; stir once to release trapped warmth. Do not wait for a deep bowl to cool on the counter. While it chills, heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C conventional, or the temperature specified by the disc package, with a rack in the middle.

Portion the filling: Work with 5-inch empanada discs labeled for baking, keeping unused discs covered and cool. Start with 1 1/2 tablespoons of cooled filling per disc, then add a little more up to about 2 tablespoons only if it closes easily. Leave a clean 1/2-inch border. Share the filling across the batch; do not stretch the pastry or force in surplus filling. Refrigerate any extra filling separately.

Seal: Lightly moisten the clean border with water for sealing. Fold each disc over the filling, gently press out trapped air, then press and crimp firmly with a fork. Set on the lined sheet with about 1 inch between empanadas. If the pastry becomes soft or sticky, refrigerate the assembled tray for 10 minutes before baking.

Glaze if desired: For the optional glaze, beat large egg (if using) and water for egg wash (if using) together and brush a thin layer over the tops. Omit both for an unglazed finish. Discard leftover wash. Cut one small slit in the top of each empanada to vent steam.

Bake: Bake for about 20–25 minutes, rotating the tray halfway through, until the pastry is golden on top and underneath and the filling reaches 165°F / 74°C. Follow the disc package if it specifies a different temperature or time; begin checking at its earliest stated time. Use a second sheet if needed rather than crowding; larger batches need additional trays and time, not a higher oven temperature.

Rest and serve: Rest on a wire rack for 10 minutes before eating; the filling can be very hot. Serve with lime and powdered sugar (if using), squeezing the lime onto each bite and adding only a light dusting of sugar if using. Allow 2–3 empanadas per person with a crisp green salad, or serve individually as a snack.

recipes.name: Philly Tuna Roll
recipes.description: Tuna, cold cream-cheese strips and crisp cucumber rolled with nori outside. Measured fillings and a larger wrapper keep the creamy center contained.
recipeIngredient: 230 g trimmed boneless, skinless yellowfin tuna, weighed after removing tough connective tissue; see raw-service sourcing note
115 g full-fat block cream cheese, cold
100 g English cucumber, weighed after removing the watery seed core
4 full sheets unseasoned roasted nori, about 19 x 20 cm each; trim as directed
120 ml water, for dampening hands and the knife
1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, for the hand-dipping water

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare rice and the station: Follow Sushi Rice (Shari), weigh 320 g for this recipe and refrigerate surplus rice promptly. Let the rolling portion become barely warm during final preparation. Wrap a clean mat in food-safe plastic film. Mix the hand-dipping water and vinegar; it reduces sticking and is not a sanitizer. Do not dip a raw-filling-coated hand or blade into this clean water. Wash hands and clean the blade before returning to it, use a separate damp cloth for wiping the cutting blade, and replace the water if contaminated.

Prepare cheese and cucumber: During the rice process, cut cold cream cheese into strips about 6 mm thick. Wash the cucumber, remove its watery core and weigh 100 g, then cut into slender matchsticks and pat dry. Divide cheese into four equal portions of about 29 g and cucumber into four 25 g portions. Refrigerate, keeping the cheese firm.

Prepare fish near rolling: With separate clean equipment, remove tough visible connective tissue, weigh the listed usable amount of tuna and cut across the muscle grain where visible into strips about 6–10 mm thick. Shorter strips can be laid end to end. Divide into four equal portions of about 58 g and refrigerate. Clean the work area and hands before handling the rolling equipment.

Portion rice and nori: Divide the rice into four 80 g portions. Trim the first nori sheet to about 19 x 15 cm, saving its dry offcut airtight for another use. Keep the other sheets untrimmed until the first closure check. Place one rectangle shiny side down with the 19 cm edge nearest you. Lightly dampen fingers, shake off excess water and spread one rice portion evenly, leaving a 1 cm bare strip at the far edge. Scatter one quarter of the sesame seeds onto the rice.

Fill and roll: Take out one portion each of tuna, cheese and cucumber. Using clean utensils, arrange them in an even horizontal line about 4 cm from the near edge; keep their ends aligned and avoid a mound in the middle. Lift the mat's near edge and tuck nori and rice over the filling. Pull the mat out of the way while rolling forward so it stays outside. Close on the bare edge, barely moistening it if needed, and press gently through the mat. Check the first roll's closure, then trim the remaining sheets to match and proceed with the other three; no rice ridge is needed.

Cut and serve: Place seam-side down briefly while preparing the knife. Wipe and lightly dampen a sharp blade. Cut each roll in half, then halve each section twice, producing eight pieces per roll; wipe and dampen the blade as needed between cuts. Serve promptly as 32 pieces, about two main portions or four appetizer portions. Keep unused raw fish and cheese portions refrigerated during the work.

recipes.name: Pho Bo (Beef Pho)
recipes.description: The soul of great pho bo lives in the charred aromatics and the long, patient simmer. Blackening the onions and ginger under the broiler builds a smoky sweetness that no shortcut can replicate.
recipeIngredient: 3 lbs Beef Marrow Bones, cut into 3-inch pieces
2 large Yellow Onions, unpeeled and halved
3 tbsp Fish Sauce, plus more to taste
1 lb Dried Rice Noodles (banh pho, medium width)
1/2 lb Eye of Round, sliced paper-thin against the grain
Hoisin Sauce and Sriracha, for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Parboil the Bones: Place the marrow bones and brisket in a large stockpot. Cover with cold water and bring to a vigorous boil for 10 minutes. Drain, rinse the bones and meat under cold water, and scrub the pot clean. This removes impurities and is essential for a clear broth.

Char the Aromatics: While the bones parboil, place the halved onions and ginger cut-side down on a sheet pan. Broil on high for 12-15 minutes until deeply blackened and softened. The char is critical for flavor.

Toast the Spices: In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the star anise, cinnamon stick, cloves, coriander seeds, and cardamom pod for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Place them in a spice sachet or cheesecloth bundle.

Build the Broth: Return the cleaned bones and brisket to the scrubbed pot. Add 6 quarts cold water, charred aromatics, and spice bundle. Bring to a boil, then immediately reduce to the gentlest possible simmer. Skim any foam that rises during the first 30 minutes.

Remove the Brisket: After 1.5-2 hours, check the brisket with a chopstick. When it slides through with little resistance, transfer the brisket to an ice bath for 10 minutes (this firms the meat for slicing), then refrigerate. Continue simmering the bones for 2 more hours.

Season the Broth: After a total of 4 hours, strain the broth through a fine-mesh strainer lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids. Stir in the fish sauce, sugar, and salt. Taste and adjust -- the broth should be deeply savory with a hint of sweetness.
Prepare the Noodles: Soak the rice noodles in warm water for 20-25 minutes until pliable. Just before serving, cook in rapidly boiling water for 30-60 seconds until tender. Drain immediately.

Prepare the Meats: Slice the chilled brisket across the grain into thin pieces and reheat it in simmering broth to 165°F / 74°C throughout. For the fully cooked eye of round, cook the slices in simmering broth before assembly, checking representative pieces with a suitable thin-tip thermometer for at least 145°F / 63°C, then allow a 3-minute rest before serving. Color change or brief contact with hot broth alone does not establish doneness; if the thin slices cannot be reliably measured, do not assume this endpoint has been verified.

Assemble: Divide noodles among deep bowls. Top with the reheated brisket and cooked, rested eye of round. Ladle hot broth over the meat and noodles. Serve immediately with a platter of bean sprouts, Thai basil, cilantro, lime wedges, jalapenos, hoisin, and sriracha.

recipes.name: Quick Refrigerator-Pickled Red Onions
recipes.description: Thin red onion in a measured vinegar brine: a refrigerated condiment with crisp texture and a mellowing raw bite.
recipeIngredient: 200 g red onion, peeled and very thinly sliced into half-moons
1/2 cup (120 ml) apple cider or distilled white vinegar, labeled 5% acidity
1 tsp (6 g) fine or pickling salt

recipeInstructions.text: Slice and pack: Peel and rinse the onion, trim its ends and slice about 1/16–1/8 inch thick. Pack into a clean heatproof pint jar, leaving roughly 1/2 inch at the top.
Heat the brine: Put the measured vinegar, water, sugar and salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until dissolved, then remove from heat.

Cover the onion: Pour hot brine over the onion and gently press it down with a clean spoon. Leave about 1/2 inch headspace. Use a narrower container or additional same-ratio brine if coverage is inadequate; do not add plain water.

Refrigerate and develop: Cover with a clean lid and refrigerate promptly on a heatproof pad, with space around the jar. After about thirty minutes, taste a drained slice once cool enough. It will still have some raw bite; longer refrigerated time, ideally until the next day, makes the flavor more even.

Use: Lift out only the needed portion with a clean fork and drain. The full batch yields approximately 1 1/2 cups drained onions; use a tablespoon or two as a condiment, leaving the rest submerged and refrigerated.

recipes.name: Pizza Beans
recipes.description: This Tex-Mex inspired skillet dish swaps pizza dough for protein-rich white beans, creating a comfort food that's lighter but equally satisfying. Cooking kale just until wilted preserves a slight bite that contrasts with the creamy beans and melted cheese.
recipeIngredient: 2 cans (15 oz each) Giant White Beans (Butter or Gigante), rinsed

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Base: Heat oil in an oven-safe heavy skillet (cast iron is best). Sauté the onion until soft (8 mins). Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Greens: Add the kale to the pan and stir until it just turns bright green and collapses.
Simmer: Stir in the tomatoes, beans, and oregano. Season with salt and pepper. Let it simmer for 5 minutes to marry the flavors.
Assemble: Top with mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake: Transfer the skillet to the oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and has golden brown spots.
Serve: Let rest for 5 minutes. Scoop into bowls and serve with crusty bread.

recipes.name: Pizza
recipes.description: Pizza as we know it originated in Naples in the late 18th century as street food for the working class, but it didn't become an American phenomenon until Italian immigrants opened pizzerias in New York and New Haven in the early 1900s. What Americans call 'pizza' would be unrecognizable to Neapolitans - we top it with everything from pineapple to BBQ chicken, making it distinctly our own.

recipeInstructions.text: Thermal Prep: Preheat oven to 500°F (or higher). Place a pizza stone or inverted baking sheet on the middle rack.
Shape: On a floured surface, stretch the dough into 12-inch circles. Transfer to a piece of parchment paper.
Layer: Spread a thin layer of sauce over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border. Top generously with mozzarella.
Top: Arrange the pepperoni and pineapple slices.
Bake: Slide the pizza (with the parchment) onto the hot stone. Bake for 8-10 minutes until the crust is charred and the cheese is bubbling.
The Wilt: During the final 2 minutes, scatter the fresh spinach over the top.
Serve: Remove from the oven. Let rest for 2 minutes (The Finish Cycle) before slicing.

recipes.name: Play-Dough
recipes.description: Homemade play-dough is a rainy-day project that's actually food science at work - a cooked dough that stays pliable for months. The cream of tartar is the key: it acts as a preservative and keeps the dough soft, so it won't crack or harden in an airtight container.

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: In a medium non-stick saucepan, whisk together the flour, salt, and cream of tartar.
Emulsify: Add the water, oil, and food coloring. Whisk until no lumps remain.
The Cook: Place over medium heat. Stir constantly with a wooden spoon for 3-5 minutes.
The Pull: The mixture will look like a liquid, then suddenly clump together. Continue stirring until the dough pulls away from the sides of the pan and forms a single, non-sticky ball.
Knead: Remove from heat and place on a clean surface. Once cool enough to touch, knead for 1 minute until perfectly smooth.
Store: Store in an airtight container for up to 6 months to maintain the "Bounce."

recipes.name: Poke Bowl Bar
recipes.description: A measured four-bowl bar with a choice of seafood, rice, fresh vegetables, cucumber salad and garnishes. Keep the seafood cold and finish each bowl as it is eaten.
recipeIngredient: 680 g total prepared raw seafood: yellowfin tuna, salmon or shucked scallop adductor muscles; choose one or split the total between two, following the sourcing note
4 cups prepared [Sushi Rice (Shari)](/mise/recipes/master-sushi-rice), or the same total of plain cooked rice and shari
1/8 tsp fine salt, for the avocado, only if needed
1/2 recipe [Oi Muchim (Korean Cucumber Salad)](/mise/recipes/korean-pickled-cucumbers), prepared and lifted from excess dressing
150 g frozen unsalted shelled edamame, cooked according to the package and chilled
1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
2 tbsp chopped cilantro or microgreens, optional
1 tsp furikake, optional; check the label
1 tbsp extra soy sauce, optional for the table
2 tbsp prepared spicy mayonnaise, optional; check the label

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the rice and cucumber salad: Make Sushi Rice (Shari) and measure four cooked cups for the bar, refrigerating any extra promptly. For two rice types, use two cups shari and two cups safely prepared Plain Short-Grain White Rice. During the rice process, make a half batch of Oi Muchim, starting with 300 g cucumber, then lift the finished half batch from excess dressing for the four bowls.

Prepare edamame and vegetables during rice soaking/cooking: Cook shelled edamame early in the rice process according to its package, drain and chill promptly in a shallow container. Wash and cut the fresh cucumber, carrot, cabbage, scallions and optional jalapeno and herbs with clean equipment. Slice avocado last and coat with 1 tsp lime juice, adding the measured optional salt only after tasting. Refrigerate vegetables until needed and keep nori dry.

Mix the dressing: Whisk soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, rice vinegar, ginger and the remaining 1 tsp lime juice. Taste before any seafood touches it. Leave out sriracha for a mild dressing or add it now; for one mild and one spicy seafood bowl, divide the clean dressing in proportion to the seafood weights and add sriracha only to the spicy portion.

Cut and dress seafood while rice cools: During the final rice cooling period, with separate clean equipment, cut cold tuna or salmon into 1/2-inch cubes, or slice scallop muscles about 1/4 inch thick. Divide the dressing among the chosen seafoods in proportion to their weights and refrigerate for about 5–10 minutes. Keep each type in its own bowl with its own spoon. This short wait seasons the seafood; it does not cook it or establish safety.

Set out and assemble: Nest small seafood bowls in ice, with meltwater unable to enter them. Check the seafood with a clean food thermometer to confirm 40°F / 4°C or below; clean the probe between seafoods and return portions to the refrigerator if the ice setup cannot keep them cold. Set out the rice barely warm and the prepared vegetables cold, with separate spoons and garnishes alongside. For four bowls, allow about one cup total rice and one quarter of the total seafood per person; a diner choosing two seafoods splits that portion. Lift seafood and cucumber salad from pooled dressing. Add avocado, edamame and fresh vegetables, then sesame, scallion and dry nori. Offer the measured optional garnishes and sauces sparingly. Assemble only when ready to eat and refrigerate unused rice promptly.
